# Reliability audit of the unchanged G17 rule

Started 2026-10-07; revised 2026-10-11. This document supersedes the proof-status claims in
[GRAY_CONSTANTS.md](GRAY_CONSTANTS.md) and REPORT §§31–33 where they conflict
with this audit. Those documents and their measurements remain useful evidence.
No active transition rule, recipe, compiler, manifest, or registered
candidate was changed. The isolated proposal sources/artifacts are
explicitly flagged in §12.

**Paused at the owner's request, 2026-10-11.** The reliability goal remains
incomplete: no positive iid noise threshold, faithful corrected-Gray
refutation or smallest globally sufficient change is proved. Accepted
records end at J309/G285. The individual new replays and audit-block
preflight passed; the pending complete J309 audit was rejected by
automatic approval review after the stop instruction. The last full
validation covers J307. See [ROBUSTNESS_HANDOFF.md](ROBUSTNESS_HANDOFF.md)
for exact validation scope and the unreviewed interrupted draft.

## 1. The precise target and the object being audited

Let F be the translation-invariant radius-5 Boolean rule of the pinned G17
netlist and instruction table, on S = {0,1}^258, using the unique output
completion for an out-of-range ROM key justified in §6. This completion is
needed to state a mathematical noisy CA; it has not been implemented in the
executables. Its candidate SHA256 (the existing netlist/ROM/layout) is
`23a14aab4d3dc4fde5562cf3e26a4536b05456f84e65850fcb3bd95a104d8ceb`.
The recipe SHA256 is
`369173f3738b180e442e669fcb0ca5fa8962b6314907c7fc70294d83338a9c74`.
See [candidates.py](../gacsca/candidates.py) and
[manifest.json](../gacsca/manifest.json). The audit loaded the candidate with
manifest checks enabled; its receipt is
[checks.json](../figs/robustness/checks.json).

Work on Z, with Q = 384 and U = 20,736. At each (x,t), t >= 1, independently
with probability ε replace the **entire output cell state** by a sample from
a distribution ν on S; otherwise use F. The samples are independent of the
error indicators and of the initial configuration. This is Gray's model
(pp. 3–4), rather than independent flips of the 258 bits. The stronger
deterministic repair obligations below allow arbitrary replacement values at
the error sites. No constant in the rule depends on simulation depth.

Here is a sufficient, concrete theorem to aim for:

> **Target, unproved.** Specify an explicit ε* > 0 and initial configurations
> ξ_0, ξ_1 with intact infinite simulation hierarchies, whose level-0 Address
> fields are (x-b) mod Q in ξ_b. For every 0 <= ε <= ε*, every ν, every x in Z,
> every t >= 0, and b in {0,1}, the noisy trajectory from ξ_b satisfies
> Pr{Address(X_t(x)) != (x-b) mod Q} <= 1/4.

Then the observable `Address's least significant bit XOR (x mod 2)` remembers
b with probability at least 3/4, uniformly in time. Q is even. This is the
phase-memory conclusion of Gray pp. 15–16, 43, and is enough to meet the
requested memory alternative. It does not claim Gács's stronger arbitrary
one-bit-per-site memory or self-organization from homogeneous states.

“For all time” here means a uniform bound for each site and time, not the event
that all sites are always correct. With positive ν, direct errors alone rule
out the latter: at a fixed site the probability of repeatedly drawing an
incorrect Address is positive, and independent such draws occur infinitely
often. Finite positive-noise rings also cannot remember forever: their finite
Markov transition matrix is strictly positive (all sites can be overwritten
in one step), hence initial-state information eventually disappears. The
repository's rings test mechanisms, not that infinite-volume conclusion.

An initial infinite hierarchy can be specified statically using the codec at
every level: Address j mod Q, Age zero, flags and work fields zero, represented
Info bits equal to the next level's state according to the pinned layout, and
all five copies consistent; unused primary Info bits are zero. Apply the same
encoding at each level, translating the bottom level by b. Such constraints
have a solution by compactness: every finite-depth set of constraints is
satisfied by repeated encoding of a top configuration on Z. This establishes
existence of initial states, not their subsequent evolution. The closure and
repair assertions needed to keep this hierarchy alive are separate obligations.

## 2. Proof-status map

The labels in this document are **proved**, **Gray's or Gács's argument applies**,
and **unproved**. “Proved” attaches only to the statement with the hypotheses
given here. Experiments supporting an unproved statement are identified
separately. A false unrestricted version is explicitly identified.

| Step | Required statement | Status for G17 |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | A single finite-state local Boolean rule; pinned ROM and netlist | **proved**, including the output completion in §6 |
| P0a | The executables evaluate F on every possible noisy cell state | **unproved; false as written** because of the ROM access in §6 |
| P1 | Initial infinite encoding constraints are satisfiable | **proved**, compactness argument in §1 |
| P2 | Cover residual errors by small candidates for c = 16; size and separation bounds | **proved**, §3 |
| P3 | Those candidates are rare under independent site/tick errors; every error has finite level a.s. | **proved**, §4; **Gray's argument applies** to the BK inequality used there |
| P4 | Five agreeing copies tolerate two faulty holders | **proved**; pristine operational correction and E0-only complete encoded simulation are also **proved** in §6; arbitrary flagged/partial regions remain **unproved**, §5 |
| P5a | The abstract pinned program is correct on every Boolean input; complete boundary encodings simulate every upper state noiselessly, and the pristine infinite hierarchy closes | **proved**, symbolic certificate, universal front-arrival lemma and copy/clock induction in §6 |
| P5b | Simulation extends through physically damaged or partial colonies and continuing work fields | **unproved**, §§6, 8–9; (5a) covers every encoded upper state, (5b) its E0-only punctures, and (5c) arbitrary rest fields once physical geometry is aligned |
| P6 | Arbitrary level-1 errors amid level-0 noise have confined, sufficiently fast structural recovery | **unproved**; Gray's size hypothesis fails, §7. Conditional field bounds and the complete noise-free coherent pair-block theorem J15/J16 are **proved** (§12). Incoherent clocks/phases, initial Flag2/Workspace damage and mixed-E0 escape remain gaps |
| P7 | All simulation fields recover, with an upper footprint small enough for the next induction | **unproved** in general; (5c) proves aligned residual-field reset, and J17 proves complete first-period reset and a two-cell upper support for the restricted coherent seed at initial good clock zero. Other stages/values and mixed noise remain unproved, §8 |
| P8 | Decoding damaged physical trajectories gives the required smaller-level error process | **unproved** in general; J17 realizes a pre-update upper pair replacement for its restricted initial seed, not a map for arbitrary islands and continuing errors, §9 |
| P9 | Higher-level islands erode, including coordinated Flag2 reversals and new colonies | **unproved**; conditional E0 pulses, intact-colony startup, a no-majority source cone and synchronized sources from protected clock strips are **proved**, §10; the unrestricted per-site source period is false |
| P10 | The deterministic envelopes hold uniformly for arbitrary depths and the infinite error set | **unproved**; part of the required repair lemma, §11 |
| P11 | Uniform memory follows from such envelopes and sparse errors | **proved conditionally**, §11; the unconditional target is **unproved** |

In particular, no entry asserts that Gray's deterministic Propositions 2–5
or Gács's amplifier theorem applies verbatim to this implementation.

## 3. Error geometry with λ = 24 and c = 16

This section checks and makes explicit the useful part of GRAY_CONSTANTS.md.
All boxes are half-open lattice boxes. “Linked at scale k” means that some
pair has |Δx| < λQ^k and |Δt| < λU^k. The complementary condition is
separation. Use Gray's four definitions (p. 17), replacing 104 in (iii) by c.
E_k includes all errors through level k. Candidate level k is a subset of
E minus E_(k-1), lies in a Q^k by U^k box, and contains two disjoint linked
candidate level-(k-1) sets. A real level k additionally satisfies (iii) and
is isolated from E minus (itself union E_(k-1)) by (λQ^k, λU^k).

Put μ = λ+2 = 26. Both Q and U exceed 6μ = 156.

**Covering lemma — proved.** For any integer c >= 1, every point of
E minus E_(n-1), n >= 1, belongs to a candidate level-n set contained in a
μQ^(n-1) by μU^(n-1) box. This holds for infinite E as well as finite E.

First note two consequences of isolation. If a point outside E_(k-1) is
linked at scale k to a real level-k set, it belongs to that set. Consequently
a subset of E minus E_(k-1) fitting inside a λ-box at scale k either lies
entirely in E_k or is disjoint from E_k. Its diameter makes all its points
linked to any one of its points.

For n = 1, a residual point p is not an isolated singleton. A different point
q is λ-linked to p. If q were in E_0, isolation of its real level-0 set would
put p in E_0 too. Thus {p,q} is the required candidate in a λ-box.

Induct on n. Fix residual p and obtain from the induction a small candidate
S1 at level n-1 containing p. It is contained in E minus E_(n-2), and its
small diameter, compared with scale n-1, implies S1 is disjoint from E_(n-1)
by the preceding observation. Let N be all residual points at coordinate
distances less than 2μQ^(n-2), 2μU^(n-2) from p. N contains S1 and fits
inside a 4μ-box at scale n-2.

If some residual q outside N is λ-linked at scale n-1 to S1, choose a small
level-(n-1) candidate Sq around q. It too is residual. S1 and Sq are
disjoint: an intersection would put q within 2μ of p at scale n-2. They
are linked through q and S1, and their union has coordinate spans at most
λQ^(n-1)+2μQ^(n-2), and the analogous time span. It is the required
level-n candidate containing p.

Otherwise N is itself a candidate level-(n-1) set: it contains S1, is residual,
and its box is smaller than Q^(n-1) by U^(n-1). It cannot be a real set at
that level, since p is residual. If N fails (iii), it contains two separated,
hence disjoint, level-(n-1) candidates. They are λ-linked at scale n-1
because N is so small. N is therefore already a level-n candidate containing p.

If N satisfies (iii), it must fail (iv). Take t in N and
q in E minus (N union E_(n-2)) linked at scale n-1. Isolation shows q is
outside E_(n-1): otherwise the real set containing q would contain t.
Choose small candidates St and Sq by induction. They are residual.
If they intersect, q is within 2μ of t, hence within 4μ of p at scale n-2.
Since q is outside N and 4μQ^(n-2) < λQ^(n-1) (also in time), q would
be linked to p in S1, the case already excluded. Thus St and Sq are
disjoint and linked through t,q. The union S1 union St union Sq is a
level-n candidate containing p; its spans are bounded by
λQ^(n-1)+5μQ^(n-2), and the time analogue.

All these bounds are less than μ at scale n-1 because Q,U >= 6μ. They
also lie inside the required Q^n by U^n box. This completes the induction.
N and all auxiliary candidates lie in bounded boxes, so the argument does
not assume E is finite. Notice that the candidate containing p need not
have exactly 2^n points; p can be outside its two dense witnesses.

**Size lemma — proved.** A real level-n set lies in a box of side at most
c+2μ = 68 at scale n-1. At level 1 its width and duration are at most
c+2λ-2 = 62 sites and ticks.

For p,p' in a real set S, take the small candidates given by the covering
lemma. They are contained in S: they lie close enough to p,p' for (iv) to
apply to all their points. By (iii) they cannot be c-separated, so some pair
of their points is c-linked. Adding the two candidate diameters bounds the
coordinate distance of p,p' by c+2μ units. At level 1 choose the pairs
from the base case: each pair has diameter at most λ-1. The distance of
the linking pair is at most c-1, giving diameter at most c+2λ-3, or width
c+2λ-2. This proves the stated bounds.

**Isolation — proved.** Distinct real level-n sets are
(λQ^n, λU^n)-separated, and a real level-n set has that separation from
every higher-level set. This follows from (iv). Overlapping real sets at
one level must coincide, since each has diameter less than the isolation
distance and each point of either is forced into the other.

The additional assertion “a level-n error becomes a box of 70 upper cells”
is **not** an error-geometry lemma. 68+2 = 70 reserves a proposed allowance
for colony overlap and damage propagation. The effects of a fault, not merely
its locations, must be bounded before that allowance is valid (§§7–10).

## 4. A complete probabilistic bound, independent of the repair rule

This proof avoids two shortcuts in the old ledger. Actual candidates use
E minus E_k, so their existence is not automatically an increasing event in
the Bernoulli errors. Also, a candidate meeting a box can have its two
subcandidates outside that box. Those issues need handling before applying
the disjoint-occurrence inequality. We do **not** claim the displayed
recurrence for the old candidate probabilities follows verbatim. We prove
the needed bound using increasing witness events instead.

Let H = QU = 7,962,624 and C = 57^2 = 3,249. Define a raw binary witness
of depth 0 to be one error point. A depth-n raw witness consists of two
depth-(n-1) raw witnesses with disjoint leaves, linked with distances
26Q^(n-1), 26U^(n-1). It has exactly 2^n distinct error leaves. These
witnesses ignore E_k and c, and their existence is an increasing event.

Every actual candidate level-n set contains such a witness. Prove this by
induction using its two linked candidate sub-sets. Trim each to a witness
inside it. A linking point of the original sub-set is less than Q^(n-1)
in space and U^(n-1) in time from any leaf in its trimmed witness. Thus
the trimmed children are linked within (24+2) units at scale n-1. At
level 0 simply choose a singleton inside the candidate. Disjointness is
preserved. The trimmed witness need not contain a prescribed point of the
original candidate; its location within that candidate is enough.

The spatial diameter of any depth-n raw witness is at most

    26 Σ_(i=0)^(n-1) 2^i Q^(n-1-i) < 27 Q^(n-1),

and its time diameter is less than 27U^(n-1). This follows by adding the
two child diameters and the linking distance; 26/(1-2/Q) < 27 and likewise
for U. For a witness with a leaf p in one child, any leaf q in the other
is within 28Q^(n-1), 28U^(n-1) of p (the bound 26+54/Q < 28 suffices;
depth 1 is immediate). There are at most C H^(n-1) possible q's.

Let r_n be the supremum over p of the probability of a depth-n witness
having p as a leaf. r_0 = ε. The two rooted child events occur with disjoint
error certificates. The van den Berg–Kesten inequality for increasing
events in a Bernoulli product measure, the same inequality Gray uses on
p. 19, and a union bound over q give

    r_n <= C H^(n-1) r_(n-1)^2
        <= C^(2^n-1) H^(2^n-n-1) ε^(2^n)
         = (C H ε)^(2^n) / (C H^(n+1)).                    (1)

The exponents follow by induction (the exponent of H is 2^n-n-1).
Each rooted event depends on finitely many sites in a bounded box, so the
finite-product BK inequality is sufficient, including on the half-plane t>0.
No independence of decoded upper-cell failures is assumed.

If an actual level-n candidate intersects a fixed Q^n by U^n box B,
some leaf of a witness in it is in the box obtained by enlarging B one
Q^n/U^n unit on each side. That box has at most 9H^n sites. Hence, writing
e_n for Gray's candidate-meets-B probability,

    e_n <= 9 H^n r_n
        <= 9 (C H ε)^(2^n) / (C H),       n >= 1.         (2)

Since H > C and 9/(C H) < 1, this also proves for G17 the useful displayed
bound from Gray's Proposition 1:

    e_n <= (H^2 ε)^(2^n).

Thus the old numerical sufficient condition H^-2 is valid **for error-set
bookkeeping**; its exact G17 value is 1.5772029579e-14, not the ledger's
rounded 1.8e-14. A less conservative sufficient condition for the same
bookkeeping follows from (1)–(2):

    ε < 1/(C H) = 1/25,870,565,376 ≈ 3.8653967761e-11.   (3)

For completeness, take a fixed residual point p outside E_(n-1). By §3
it has a candidate within 26 units at scale n-1. A witness leaf in that
candidate is within those same coordinate distances of p. There are at
most C H^(n-1) possible leaves, so (1) gives

    Pr{p in E minus E_(n-1)} <= (C H ε)^(2^n) / H^2.     (4)

When C H ε < 1 this tends to zero. E_k increases, so the probability that
p belongs to E but to no E_k is zero. There are countably many p; their
union also has probability zero. Every error has a finite level almost surely.

Equations (1)–(4) are proved statements about a Bernoulli set, valid regardless
of the replacement states. They are **not** noise thresholds of G17. An
arbitrarily sparse set can still destroy memory if its individual defects
are not controlled by the rule.

## 5. What fivefold voting proves, and the flagged-region exception

The elementary statement is exact: if a stored bit has five identical
reference copies on five distinct holders, changing any two holders leaves
its majority unchanged. Directional word votes of five equally extrapolated
correct Addresses/Ages likewise tolerate two altered holders. In a locally
flag-free, replication-consistent execution, these facts account for the
healthy-colony one-tick measurements. They do not prove that all execution
states meet that invariant, or that geometry and erasure decisions are
independent of a corrupted stored Address in flagged regions.

In fact an unrestricted one-tick statement is false for the unchanged rule.
The simulation updates in [rule_g.py](../gacsca/rule_g.py), function `build`,
contain

    wipe = computed_Flag1 AND (computed_Address != stored_Address)
    new_simulation_bit = NOT(wipe) AND ordinary_update

Take a two-colony periodic state, Address x mod Q, common valid Age 2000,
Flag1 = 1, Flag2 = Wf1 = Wf2 = 0, all five Info slots = 1, and other
simulation fields zero. Flip Address bit 0 at site 100 (100 becomes 101).
Both the unaltered and altered states have computed Address 100 and
computed Flag1 = 1 there: the directional majorities still have at least
four correct Address words, and the right-hand Flag1 neighbors keep the flag
raised. Only the altered state satisfies `wipe`. At the next tick its five
stored Info slots at site 100 are zero, while the reference slots are one.
One tick later the three or four intact copies of each relevant logical bit
restore them. The whole two rings agree after two ticks.

That calculation proves a counterexample to unrestricted one-tick recovery.
It is also reproduced with the exact netlist in both NumPy and C:
[check.py](../figs/robustness/check.py),
[checks.json](../figs/robustness/checks.json), and the saved states
[flagged_single_site.npz](../figs/robustness/flagged_single_site.npz).
The two implementations agree at both comparison ticks; five Info bits at
one site differ at tick 1, none at tick 2. Reproduce with
`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=. python3 figs/robustness/check.py`.

This initial state is a legal flagged state, **not** a pristine infinite
hierarchy. Therefore it does not disprove the target theorem, or Gray's
Proposition 4 with its hierarchy hypotheses and its union of higher damage
boxes. A proof may absorb these delayed footprints into the larger island
whose flags caused them. It must actually prove that absorption, including
the Flag2 return wave. The existing G17 upper-wipe receipt records 199/200
two-tick cases during the window, and 3/200 discrepancies still present
after three ticks in the post-window experiment. That finite observation
does not establish a bound on the latter discrepancies' lifetime.

## 6. Universal program verification and noiseless closure

### A prior implementation defect: ROM access on unused state patterns

G17 uses a 9-bit Address and a packed Age with a 9-bit position. Q is only
384 and the valid Age position is less than PL = 288. Independent whole-state
noise is permitted to write the other bit patterns. A uniform state with
Address 500, Age word 17868 = (34 << 9) OR 460, and all other bits zero
has computed arrival true, lookup Address **498**, and lookup page 0.
The instruction table has only 384 rows. `Candidate.step_numpy` raises
`IndexError: index 498 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 384`.
The C, CUDA and role-kernel generators emit `rom[a * NPT + ps]` without
a row guard, so this case attempts an out-of-bounds memory read.

This is safely reproduced without executing that invalid native read:
[check_invalid_rom.py](../figs/robustness/check_invalid_rom.py),
[invalid_rom.json](../figs/robustness/invalid_rom.json), and
[invalid_rom_state.npz](../figs/robustness/invalid_rom_state.npz).
It is not confined to an artificial global state. Eleven overwritten cells
at one tick give their central cell exactly this radius-5 neighborhood on
the next tick. For any strictly positive ν the event has probability at
least `(ε ν(s_bad))^11 (1-ε) > 0` for 0 < ε < 1. Thus a claim about the
current executables under all allowed whole-state noise is not even a
defined stochastic CA on the specified state space.

There is nevertheless a unique mathematical output completion here,
**proved by the instruction guards**, rather than a choice of new dynamics.
In G17's `_mux_front`, when any slot arrives, `key_addr` is the Address of
one arriving slot. The Address `xaddr` used in the output logic is the
bitwise OR of all arriving-slot Addresses. If `key_addr >= Q`, this OR
is also >= Q, so `inside = (lo <= xaddr < hi)` is false. All instruction
`kind_lines` are gated by `inside`, as is `matched`. Thus the registers only
carry their source values, pending writes are off, and their values are zero;
the output contains no dependence on I. With no arriving slot the same
independence holds directly. All other field updates are independent of the
current I. Therefore setting I=0 for an out-of-range key defines F on these
neighborhoods and gives the same output as **any** extension of the ROM.

A local remedy for this concrete defect is to guard every ROM
fetch by `a < Q`, using I=0 otherwise (including NumPy's unconditional
vectorized fetch). This changes executable access behavior; it preserves
the Boolean output on every formerly defined input and implements the
unique completion just proved. Alternatively explicitly pad the lookup
table to all 512 rows and audit its self-interpreter representation. Neither
remedy was implemented here. A guard is a sufficient fix for this fetch
defect, **not** for the reliability gaps below. Increasing Q to 512 would
also remove this row-range problem at k=9, but would change the rule and
would not establish a threshold.

### The universal abstract program certificate: proved

[check_g17_schedule.py](proofs/check_g17_schedule.py) supplies a finite
symbolic certificate, with receipt
[symbolic_schedule.json](../figs/robustness/symbolic_schedule.json). It
regenerates the listing, reconstructs its ROM independently from the packed
instruction fields, and checks equality with the pinned table. It then
evaluates the original netlist and that instruction table using distinct
Boolean variables for **all 2,862 inputs**. It does not trust the scheduler's
value annotations, rewritten DAG, or numerical replay to identify results.

Here is why the check proves a universal assertion. Every canonical term
denotes a Boolean function. The canonicalizer flattens equal operations and
sorts their arguments; AND and OR remove repeated arguments and apply their
neutral/absorbing constants and complement identity; XOR removes even
multiplicities and zero. ANDN(a,b) becomes AND(a,XOR(b,1)). Every rewrite is
a Boolean identity, so induction over gate/instruction execution proves that
each term denotes its actual Boolean result. Identical canonical terms
therefore denote identical functions on every assignment. No converse or
complete Boolean decision procedure is needed.

The checker reconstructs input locations from the schema, layout and signed
skews. It decodes the packed ROM instructions, tracks registers and scratch,
rejects reads before definition, and checks visit geometry and deadlines.
At the match pass it checks all 18 key bits, discards all register contents,
then supplies the 24 independent instruction bits in front 0. Discarding the
other contents certifies that subsequent outputs cannot depend on them.
The checked equalities are the 18 key bits, both early flags, and all 258
final Hold bits. There are 22,863 nonzero instructions, 2,499 scratch reads,
and 260 Hold stores. The least scratch write-to-read delay is five ticks.
Flag2 at cell 58 is stored at Age 12661; Flag1 at cell 325 at Age 12394;
both precede the required deadline 13248. Every final store is before the
evaluation end 20448, which is before commit at 20735.

**Proved statement.** Given the correct, persistent gathered inputs at these
locations, abstract execution of the pinned ROM computes the original
netlist's key, flags and outputs for every Boolean assignment, provided
front 0 receives the correct external instruction during the match pass.
This finite proof establishes the program, rather than its physical
preconditions. The following argument establishes those preconditions on
an intact noiseless hierarchy.

### Front-arrival uniqueness for all raw words: proved

The compact front's claim of at most one arriving logical slot needs to
include **all** raw Address and Age words, not just legal aligned geometry.
Let A be any 9-bit computed holder Address. The five slot Addresses are
the actual `w_add_const_mod(A,d mod Q,Q)`, for d=-2,...,2. For A<384
they are `(A+d) mod 384`. For A>=384, in slot order they are

    A−2, A−1, A−384, A−383, A−382.

All these expressions fit in nine bits. Any two distinct slot Addresses
have circular distance modulo 512 in `{1,2,3,4,127,128,129,130,131,132}`.
For a raw Age position r in 0,...,511, an active forward comb has targets
`38+r+5j mod 512`; an active backward comb has targets
`325−r+5j mod 512`, j=0,...,4. Distinct targets have circular distance
5,10,15 or 20. Consequently two different slots cannot arrive together.
This remains true for every raw Age: the high bits merely select the
window and its direction, and outside blocks 34,...,70 no slot arrives.
Register values do not enter any arrival predicate. Thus the conclusion
holds even when maintenance computes arbitrary unused words.

With one arrival, the priority-selected lookup Address and the bitwise-OR
Address used by `_mux_front` are the same slot Address. If it is outside
[58,326), `inside` is false, all instruction kind lines and matching are
off, and the output is independent of the current I. With no arrival
the same independence holds. This proves that any instruction key outside
the physical matching front's working interval can be left unfetched.
It also covers keys outside the ROM in the output-completed F from §1.

[check_front_arrivals.py](proofs/check_front_arrivals.py) evaluates the
actual addition and timing gates on all 524,288 Address/position/direction
assignments and independently checks the pair differences. Its receipt is
[front_arrival_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/front_arrival_certificate.json).
There are 25,600 assignments with one arrival, including 10,070 outside
the working interval and 2,530 outside the ROM rows. This is an exhaustive
finite local certificate supporting the elementary proof, not a noisy
simulation claim.

### A physical one-period lemma: proved on healthy structure

Call an upper configuration **structurally healthy** when its Addresses are
an aligned sequence j mod Q, all Ages are the same valid packed value, and
Flag1, Flag2 and both Workspace flags are zero. Its other fields may be
arbitrary. Translations of the aligned sequence have the same argument.
Let `Enc(z)` be the repository's canonical codec encoding of z at lower
Age zero, with all lower work fields zero. Then

    F^U(Enc(z)) = Enc(F(z))                                  (5)

for every structurally healthy z. Throughout this one lower period, lower
Addresses/Ages remain correct, all four lower flags remain zero, and logical
Info at the unused special Addresses 3 and Q−3 remains zero. This is an
equality of whole physical configurations, not only a decoder equality.

**Proof.** On legal aligned structure, every adjusted right Address equals
the holder's Address, every right Age equals its Age, and every counted
left in-colony value agrees. In `maintenance.build` the majority votes
exist, inconsistency is false, both flags remain zero and the right vote is
selected. The modular adder subtracts Q exactly when its legal sum reaches
Q; the packed increment wraps position 287 and block 71. Thus computed
geometry is exact and the wipe predicate is false. Workspace flags remain
zero as long as the two special logical Info values are zero; the flag
couriers below establish this throughout the period.

Use the copy invariant that slot s at holder y contains the value of logical
cell y+s−2, for each fivefold simulation field. All holders have the same
Age. Their computed slot Address equals that logical cell's Address even
across a colony boundary. Consequently every copy holder performs the same
update on a given logical value; majority voting returns that value exactly.
Pending writes preserve this invariant: a store at tick t puts the same
pending value in all five holders at t+1. At t+1 `lv` forwards it; the next
copy update materializes it in Hold/scratch at t+2. The checked five-tick
minimum consumer delay exceeds this latency. Pending buffers at other
logical cells are zero. There is no store at either wipe or commit.

At gather start gQ, mail loads logical Info and is present at gQ+1. Mail
then moves one site per tick. At a lane cell `layout[b]+skew_j`, the capture
Age is `gQ+|j|Q+1+skew_j` for j<0 and `gQ+jQ+1−skew_j` for j>0. Therefore
the captured source is exactly `layout[b]+jQ`. All represented Info is
unchanged until commit; all three captures agree. Each capture finishes
before the next reload, and the last finishes before evaluation. Thus the
voted histories and own Info supply exactly z's eleven-cell neighborhood,
at the locations checked by the symbolic program certificate. Hold is
cleared in the update at Age E0−1, before evaluation starts.

On page p and tick r, the comb centers are

    38+r+5j                    if p is even,
    325−r+5j                   if p is odd,   j=0,...,4.

They lie between 38 and 345. Their five-holder windows stay within one
colony, and distinct fronts' windows are disjoint. At the first tick their
register sources are zero. At a turn they retain their own sources; at
other ticks the source center is the preceding position of the same front.
Those five source holders all contain that front's preceding register word.
Every holder computes the same operands, instruction key and result for
that front. Cells outside [58,326) carry registers without executing a
store. Word zero is AND R0,R0 into R0, an identity even when R0 was never
used. These observations prove by induction over the 37 pages that physical
register execution agrees with the certified abstract machine. The receipt
also checks all 53,280 center/clock identities.

At match page 21 front 0 traverses every working Address once. Its first
nine key bits remain fixed. If the required key Address lies in [58,326),
exactly that cell replaces registers 9 through 32 with the ROM word at the
certified Address/page; hence the external instruction is correct. If the
key lies outside this interval, no matching cell writes it. By the universal
front-arrival lemma, the upper output is independent of I whenever
its key cannot be fetched, including on malformed upper geometry.
The post-match certificate holds for every I,
so it holds for the retained register bits too. Registers of other fronts
may also retain or fetch values during matching; the certificate proves
subsequent execution does not depend on those initial contents.

For a structurally healthy z its computed new Flag1/Flag2 are zero.
The two early Hold values are therefore zero, by the certificate. The
left courier loads at Age 13480 and travels 55 cells to Address 3; the
right loads at 13479 and travels 56 cells to Address 381. Loaded mail
appears one tick later, so both arrive at Age T_sig=13536. Their special
Info writes are zero. Before then those logical Info cells retain their
initial zero; afterwards they stay zero until commit. This closes the
Workspace-flag/geometry induction used above, including the trickle window.

All 258 represented Hold values equal F(z)'s bits. There are no other Hold
stores except the two zero early flags. The evaluation ends at 20448;
pending writes settle and registers become zero before commit at 20735.
Commit copies Hold to Info and clears Hold, scratch, both mail tracks and
histories. No arriving front is present, so all front buffers are zero.
The unused logical Hold cells, including the two flag cells, are zero.
Hence all unused Info is zero after commit as well. Addresses are aligned,
Age is zero and all lower flags/work fields are zero. The resulting whole
configuration is precisely `Enc(F(z))`, proving (5). ∎

Equation (5) is restricted to healthy upper structure. General upper states
require the following boundary encoding; ordinary canonical equality can
fail at unused Info cells.

### Every upper state: proved noiselessly with two auxiliary bits

Let z be **any** configuration in S^Z. Its Address, Age, flags and simulation
fields may all be arbitrary, including unused raw words and inconsistent
copies. Define Enc_a(z) by the same canonical codec,
with two additional logical Info bits per physical colony: at Address 58
store z's Flag2, and at 325 store z's Flag1, in all five holders. These
addresses are absent from the represented layout. All other unused Info
and every lower work field remain zero, with lower Age zero. This is a
proof encoding for the **unchanged** rule; `codec.py` is not modified.
Then for every z, with the mathematically completed F of §1,

    F^U(Enc_a(z)) = Enc_a(F(z)),
    F^U(Enc(z))   = Enc_a(F(z)).                              (5a)

**Proof.** The lower physical Address/Age are aligned by either encoding,
independently of z's upper geometry. Both lower Address votes and both
Age votes agree, regardless of any lower flags, so lower geometry remains
aligned and the raw-Address wipe
never fires. The two auxiliary Info cells are not original input locations.
The symbolic replay rejects every nonconstant lane read not corresponding
to an input or a previously defined scratch/register value; consequently
none of its instructions reads these auxiliary Info values. Gathered
values at actual input locations are exactly z's bits with or without
the two auxiliary cells. This includes all bits of upper Address/Age and
every upper work field; it does not treat them as physically valid lower
structure. The universal program certificate computes the netlist on these
arbitrary bits. If its instruction key is in [58,326), the physical match
front fetches the exact pinned ROM word. Otherwise the universal arrival
lemma proves the desired upper output is independent of I, and the symbolic
certificate holds for the retained instruction bits. No upper legality,
alignment or copy-consistency hypothesis is used.

Lower flags are zero through the courier and special signal procedures:
the initial special Info cells 3 and 381 are zero, and Workspace sources
are off until T_wf. Thus the gather, register, pending-write and courier
proof above still applies. The two early Hold values are now arbitrary
correct output flags B2=F(z).Flag2 and B1=F(z).Flag1. They reach special
Info on Age 13536, one tick before the Workspace window. Lower flags may
then turn on and move during that window. This clears mail in flagged
cells but never invokes the raw-Address wipe. All gathers and the flag
couriers have already finished; there are no further captures. The
certified program's remaining reads use Info at represented input
locations, histories, scratch and registers, rather than live mail.
The two special Info writes are outside the represented layout. Hence
flagging cannot change its inputs or its execution, and every final Hold
value is still correct.

After the window, the quieting lemma (18)–(20), with no noise, makes Flag1
zero within 212 updates. Workspace flags are already zero. The right
Address majority exists, so d3 is false and there is no Flag2 source.
With computed Flag1 zero, the actual Flag2 rule is (21). Its complement
has the same threshold-four/old-bit-threshold-two form, directed right,
with a virtual zero-Flag2 half-line outside the colony's left boundary.
This half-line extends two sites right per update: the first new site has
five zero left inputs and the second has four. At most 192 further updates
therefore erase every Flag2 in a 384-site colony. All four lower flags are
zero well before commit, since 212+192=404<6431 source-free updates before
the period boundary.

The only Hold stores outside the 258 represented locations are the two
certified early flags at 58 and 325. Commit clears all lower work as in
the preceding proof, writes F(z)'s represented bits, writes B2/B1 at these
two unused Info locations, and writes zero at every other unused location,
including the special cells 3 and 381. This is exactly Enc_a(F(z)). The
initial auxiliary bits never influenced the calculation, giving both
equalities in (5a). Since the claim includes every upper state, it applies
again to F(z), whatever its new geometry or flags. Induction therefore gives
`F^(nU)(Enc_a(z))=Enc_a(F^n(z))` for every n>=0, and
`F^(nU)(Enc(z))=Enc_a(F^n(z))` for every n>=1. No rule or encoding operation
depends on simulation depth. The argument is local on Z; the same proof
applies to finite periodic rings. ∎

There is finite full-rule support: starting from arbitrary upper flags and
other fields, on aligned geometry, two periods over 147,456 physical sites
equaled the entire augmented encoding. Fresh ordinary codec encodings
differed at the auxiliary Info copies, as predicted. The driver and receipt
are [check_noiseless_flags.py](../figs/robustness/check_noiseless_flags.py) and
[noiseless_flags_canonical.json](../figs/robustness/noiseless_flags_canonical.json),
with saved input [noiseless_flags_upper.npz](../figs/robustness/noiseless_flags_upper.npz).
Four additional upper contexts have arbitrary geometry: uniformly random
bits; constant unused Address 500/Age 17868 with random other fields;
random active raw clocks; and unused Addresses with staggered clocks.
Both Enc and Enc_a starts match the entire expected Enc_a boundary at each
of two periods over 147,456 physical sites, sixteen period-runs total.
The expected one-step upper outputs also agree in C and NumPy. The driver,
receipt and saved inputs are
[check_noiseless_arbitrary.py](../figs/robustness/check_noiseless_arbitrary.py),
[noiseless_arbitrary.json](../figs/robustness/noiseless_arbitrary.json), and
[noiseless_arbitrary_upper.npz](../figs/robustness/noiseless_arbitrary_upper.npz).
These runs use only the uniquely justified ROM zero-padding completion in
an experiment-memory copy; repository rule/backends are unchanged.

Both experiments are supplementary: the universal all-period claim is the
copy/program, arrival and flag-erasure proof above. It starts from a
**complete physical boundary encoding**. Noisy or partial lower colonies,
residual work states and a decoder relation through damaged trajectories
remain **unproved**. Arbitrary *represented upper geometry* is now covered;
arbitrary *physical encoding damage* is not.

### Complete encodings tolerate separated E0 errors: proved conditionally

There is also a deterministic extension of (5a) to all E0-only overwrite
patterns, including arbitrary values of every overwritten bit. Start from
Enc(z) or Enc_a(z), for any upper z. Allow only singleton/adjacent-pair
groups mutually (24,24)-separated throughout the evolution. Write X_t
for the resulting noisy lower state and N_t for the direct overwrite sites
at state time t. Then for every n>=1,

    X_(nU)(x) = Enc_a(F^n(z))(x) for every x outside N_(nU),
    decode(X_(nU)) = F^n(z).                                 (5b)

Here decode uses the five-copy Info vote, as in `codec.decode`; the first
equality concerns the entire raw cell state. The same result holds if the
initial encoding already differs only on an N_0 group pattern included
in the separation hypothesis. This is an **E0-only encoded-state theorem**,
not independent Bernoulli noise reliability. Positive iid noise also has
higher-level clusters. The statement cannot be applied to an exterior
E0 component while silently removing the physical influence of those
clusters or the partial colonies they create.

**Proof.** Computed lower geometry is exactly aligned at every tick by
§10's geometry-only vote induction; raw geometry differs only on N_t.
Thus the raw-Address wipe can fire only at a current overwritten site.
For the simulation fields used by the program, preserve the physical
copy/front invariant of (5a) except at

    Z_t = N_t union N_(t−1).

In any eleven-site input window these two rows of faults meet at most one
E0 group, containing at most two sites. Every logical five-copy vote,
pending-bit/value/kind vote and consumed compact register vote therefore
returns its reference value. This includes scratch forwarding: the
pending votes are correct before their value is selected. With corrected
geometry, every holder has the same front arrival, instruction lookup,
capture, courier, wipe-stage and commit timing as in the clean proof.
All holders not in N_t compute the correct next simulation value; a wipe
can affect only N_t, and new overwrites add N_(t+1). Hence their next raw
errors are confined to Z_(t+1), closing the copy induction.

The flag-dependent mail clearance needs separate treatment. Before the
trickle window, both computed lower flags are zero. Their right geometry
votes are correct, so inconsistency and D3 are false. At most two corrupted
Workspace bits cannot create a three-bit source; a corrupt center Flag1
has at most one other corrupt right input and cannot persist. Candidate B
likewise removes a corrupt center Flag2. Initially the special Info is
zero, so Workspace outputs are also zero until the window. Induction
therefore keeps Flag1/Flag2/Workspace clear except current N_t through all
gathers and the special signal procedure. Their mail/history/Info votes
and all captures and couriers are exactly correct by the copy induction.
Both output commands are installed on the special Info cells at Age 13536.

During the window lower flags may differ from their clean trajectories,
and lower mail can be cleared on additional sites. Drop the mail invariant
after the special signal: there are no later captures, courier loads or
special mail-to-Info writes. The certified program's remaining reads use
represented Info, histories, scratch and registers. None reads live mail.
The raw-Address wipe is still confined to N_t, independently of these
flag differences. Consequently the copy induction continues for every
program input/output field and the special Info commands. All represented
Hold outputs and both auxiliary flag Hold values are those of F(z).
This argument allows arbitrary upper work fields and flags; it only
requires their complete lower encoding.

After the window, computed Workspace outputs are zero. The source-free
Flag1 bound (18)–(20) gives computed Flag1=0 within 212 updates, despite
E0. It stays zero thereafter. Right Address majorities always exist, so
D3=0; Workspace.Flag2 has only current direct faults, insufficient for
D4. The source-free Flag2 erasure lemma (24a) below then gives computed
Flag2=0 within another 212 updates. Thus all four computed flags are
zero after at most 424 source-free updates, well inside the 6,431-update
reserve before commit.

At commit computed Flag1=0, so **no raw-Address wipe fires**, even at
N_(U−1). Correct voted Hold values write every Info copy, all work fields
are cleared, no front arrives, and all computed flags and geometry are
the canonical boundary values. Before the new overwrites, the entire
state is Enc_a(F(z)). After them it differs only on N_U. Each logical
Info vote still has at least three correct holders, proving the decoder
identity. The next period starts with exactly the allowed N_0-type
punctures. Induction over periods proves (5b). ∎

This proof does not assert one-tick full-field correction inside raised
flags: the Z_t allowance includes the wipe delay from §5. Nor does it
compare the intermediate lower flags/mail to their clean values during
the window. It proves their eventual boundary reset and that the program
does not depend on those intermediate differences.

Finite support uses two arbitrary upper states, four separated-overwrite
value modes (random, all-one, invert and next-colony copy), and two periods
on 147,456 sites per ring. The first commit coincides with 11,342 direct
overwrites; the full boundary equality holds outside exactly those sites.
The second boundary has no current errors and matches the entire encoding.
The driver, receipt and saved inputs are
[check_encoded_e0.py](../figs/robustness/check_encoded_e0.py),
[encoded_e0.json](../figs/robustness/encoded_e0.json), and
[encoded_e0_upper.npz](../figs/robustness/encoded_e0_upper.npz).
The native noise grid is 26-by-26 with pair threshold 65536; it skips
the incomplete final grid cell, preserving separation across the ring
wrap. All these are finite measurements supporting the preceding
deterministic proof, and use the same experiment-only output completion.

### Aligned physical geometry restores arbitrary other fields: proved conditionally

The two clean later gathers give a stronger restoration statement. Let
X_0 have aligned canonical **physical** Addresses and common lower Age zero.
Every other raw field can be arbitrary, including all four lower flags,
mail, histories, Hold, scratch, front/pending fields, disagreeing copies,
and unused Info. Define z=`decode(X_0)` by majority of the five Info copies
at every represented location. Permit E0-only overwrite groups with the
same global separation as (5b). Then

    X_U(x) = Enc_a(F(z))(x) for x outside N_U,
    decode(X_U) = F(z).                                      (5c)

Current N_0-type geometric punctures may also be included if those groups
are part of the separation hypothesis; z is then the decode of the actual
punctured initial state. This does not assert recovery of an intended z
whose initial copy majority was already wrong.

**Proof.** Computed geometry stays aligned. Every holder's update of one
logical Info value reads the same five raw copies, so the first update
makes them all the initial majority, except current noise and the wipe
on N_0. The static-copy induction confines further Info errors to
N_t union N_(t−1), until commit or the special signal. Thus represented
Info continues to encode z even though its initial raw copies disagreed.
Initial unused Info cannot supply Workspace sources before the trickle
window: the window factor in both Workspace outputs is false. Initial
Workspace flags reset at the first update. By the source-free bounds,
computed Flag1 is zero by update 212 and computed Flag2 by update 424.
They remain zero until the later window, apart from direct overwrites in
the stored fields.

Consequently the **second** gather, loaded at Age 3840, is correct at
every input capture, as is the third loaded at Age 7680. The first gather
may have been cleared by initial Flag1, and its h1 values may be arbitrary.
That is harmless: the second capture writes correct h2; at the third
capture the actual `maj3(h1,h2,passing)` has two correct operands. Every
history input needed by the program is therefore correct after the third
capture, whose latest Age is 9591, before evaluation at 9792. Neither
garbage at unused history locations nor initial mail can enter the
certified lane reads. The mail reload at 3840 removes all earlier mail,
and Flag1 is already quiet throughout its route and all later gathers.

No front arrives before evaluation, so arbitrary front/pending buffers
are reset at the first update. Initial Hold is erased by the stage wipe
at Age 9791. Initial scratch can remain arbitrary, but the symbolic
certificate rejects every scratch read before a certified earlier write.
No output depends on its starting contents. Initial unused Info is likewise
absent from all nonconstant certified operand reads. These observations
establish all input, register and scratch preconditions of the universal
program proof; they do not assume that lower work was initially encoded.

The remaining copy, instruction-match, courier and command proof is the
same as (5b). The couriers install both correct output commands before
the window, replacing any initial special Info. Subsequent flags can
affect only unused live mail and wipes at N_t. Every represented Hold and
both auxiliary Hold values are correct, while other Hold values were
wiped and never stored. The 424-update source-free bound quiets the flags
again before commit. Commit has no wipe, writes precisely Enc_a(F(z))
and clears every lower work field, before adding N_U. Five-copy decoding
removes those at most two local faults. This proves (5c). ∎

There is a useful conditional consequence for a recovered clock. Suppose
physical geometry is everywhere aligned with a common **legal** Age a,
apart from current direct faults, while all other fields are arbitrary.
Let s be the number of updates to the next Age-zero boundary, with s=0
if a is already zero. At s the other fields can still be arbitrary, but
the geometry satisfies (5c). For z_s=`decode(X_s)`, therefore X_(s+U)
is Enc_a(F(z_s)) outside current errors. Since 0<=s<U, a complete encoding
is obtained within **less than 2U** updates. This proves restoration to
an admissible encoding, not correctness of an earlier intended bit.
It assumes global aligned geometry or enough surrounding causal context;
it does not yield a two-colony damage envelope by itself.

Finite support starts with every raw field/copy independently random
except aligned physical Address and Age zero. No Info copies agree
globally. On 147,456 sites one full period yields exactly the predicted
Enc_a(F(decode(X_0))), with no noise and with each of four E0 overwrite
value modes. In the noisy runs the boundary differs only on its 11,342
current direct errors. The driver, receipt and saved state are
[check_aligned_restoration.py](../figs/robustness/check_aligned_restoration.py),
[aligned_restoration.json](../figs/robustness/aligned_restoration.json), and
[aligned_restoration_initial.npz](../figs/robustness/aligned_restoration_initial.npz).
This is one sampled starting state and five runs, not a universal
experimental claim; the universal result is the two-gather/reset argument.

What remains **unproved** is achieving the required geometric alignment
and clock phase after higher errors, localizing this restoration to the
claimed upper support, and supplying an admissible effective error map.
Thus (5c) narrows P7's residual-field problem but does not close P6–P10.

### The pristine infinite hierarchy remains intact without noise: proved

Let `(ξ^l)_{l>=0}` be any static infinite hierarchy from §1, so
`ξ^l=Enc(ξ^(l+1))` at every level (with the chosen bottom translation).
Every ξ^l is structurally healthy, has zero special Info, and has zero work
fields. Then at every l and integer n>=0,

    F^(nU)(ξ^l) = Enc(F^n(ξ^(l+1))).                         (6)

Moreover every local structure remains healthy at every physical tick.
Here is an induction that avoids assuming the conclusion at higher levels.
Prove these statements simultaneously for all l through n completed
periods, including all intermediate ticks. For n=0 the static constraints
give the boundary state; the one-period lemma applies to every ξ^(l+1)
and proves the first period. For n>=1 the upper input at the next boundary
is `F^n(ξ^(l+1))`, by the already proved decoder identity. Since n<=nU,
its healthy structure is part of the induction hypothesis, measured in its
own physical ticks. Apply (5) to each level for the next period. Its output
is `Enc(F^(n+1)(ξ^(l+1)))` and its intermediate structure stays healthy.
No induction on an infinite downward chain is being used: the finite
physical time n needed for the upper input has already been covered. This
proves (6) and perpetual noiseless hierarchy preservation. ∎

### Operational level-0 correction along that healthy orbit: proved

Let X be any state on the pristine noiseless orbit just proved. Overwrite
arbitrary sites by arbitrary states to obtain X', subject to the condition
that every interval of eleven sites contains at most two overwritten sites.
Then

    F(X') = F(X).                                            (7)

This includes one or two arbitrary sites, isolated adjacent pairs, and a
collection of pairs with at least nine clean sites between successive pairs
at that tick. Every radius-5 neighborhood sees at most two overwritten cells.
In maintenance, three of five adjusted right Addresses
and Ages are still correct; at most two left inconsistencies or Workspace
flags can be counted. The healthy stored Flag1 is zero unless the holder
itself was overwritten. In that case at most one other overwritten right
neighbor remains, so the persistence test cannot have two right Flag1 bits.
Thus computed Flag1 is zero. A corrupt stored Flag2 is erased because at
most one left Flag2 is set; a healthy zero Flag2 cannot turn on because its
four-left and three-Workspace tests fail and a right majority exists.
Computed geometry is therefore exact and the wipe remains off.

All simulation and pending-buffer votes see at least three correct copies.
Every consumed compact register vote is at the preceding center of its own
front, whose five holders agree, so it too is correct. The corrected
instruction lookup and operands agree with F(X). Every output field is
therefore its clean value, proving (7), including the next Workspace flags.
There is no native out-of-range fetch in this corrected geometry.

Iterating (7) proves exact correction one tick after each overwrite when
every tick's fault set satisfies that local density condition: before
each update only the preceding tick's pairs differ from the pristine orbit.
This proves the healthy level-0 base case, rather than a measured version of
it. It does **not** apply in a damage island with pre-existing flags or
incoherent copies; §5's counterexample rules out that unrestricted extension.

### The remaining simulation obligation: unproved

Equations (5a)–(5b) prove the decoder identity and its complete boundary-state
induction for **every represented upper configuration**, using Enc_a, also
with E0-only punctures. Equation (5c) proves reset from arbitrary rest fields
once lower physical geometry is aligned. The
remaining obligation is an invariant and decoder for physical trajectories
whose lower colonies are damaged, partial or misaligned and whose work
fields continue from such damage. It must show that every discrepancy in
the decoded trajectory belongs to the claimed effective upper error set,
with its size, duration, isolation and restoration bounds.

Starting such a trajectory from a fresh encode would discard the lower
damage and work fields that the proof must handle. In these cases physical
holders can disagree about clock and Address, different fronts' copy windows
can overlap, mail can be erased, and wipes can erase some copies. The
abstract certificate then lacks its input and transport preconditions.

Gray's Proposition 3 constructs simulation procedures; it does not certify
this five-front straight-line compiler and its particular schedule. Gács's
universal-machine simulation results likewise do not certify its ROM. The
existing G17 exact periods and the one full physical U^2 step are additional
measured evidence. The proof above supersedes those experiments for complete
noiseless boundary encodings; it does not supersede the noisy obligations P6–P10.

## 7. The first failed deterministic transplant: structural recovery

Gray's Proposition 2 needs the island to remain shorter than a whole apparent
colony, so its left edge cannot remain an undetectable colony boundary.
His pp. 25–26 estimates, parameterized by an error-box side B, require

    15B < Q/2,       23B < 3Q/4,

or Q > (92/3)B, in addition to the wave-speed and timing assumptions. Even
using the proved sharp first-level B = 62 requires Q > 1901.33. With the
proposed uniform footprint allowance B = 70 it requires Q > 2146.67.
G17 has Q = 384. Reducing c to zero would not fix this route: already the
λ-dependent part of the box is too large. Making ε smaller does not change
these deterministic inequalities.

### A smaller source of first-level damage: proved, but not a repair bound

The operational lemma (7) gives a new reduction that does not use the
square-block race. For a real level-1 error S define D(S) to be the error
points belonging to a triple of distinct points at one tick, whose spatial
span is at most ten. Then, if D(S) is nonempty,

    spatial span of D(S) <= 33,
    temporal span of D(S) <= 15.                            (8)

Thus the fault points capable of starting damage on the healthy orbit fit
in a **34-site by 16-tick** box, even though S's bounding box can be 62 by
62. This statement uses the actual c=16 condition (iii), rather than
treating every point of the larger box as an available adversarial error.

**Proof.** Any two distinct points in such a triple form a candidate
level-1 error: their singleton level-0 candidates are disjoint and
(24,24)-linked, and the pair fits in the required box. If two triples occur
at ticks at least sixteen apart, choose one pair from each. They are
(16,16)-separated, contradicting (iii). This proves the temporal bound.

Let a be the least spatial coordinate of D(S), and z the greatest. A triple
containing a has a as its least coordinate; its second point has coordinate
b<=a+9. A triple containing z has z as its greatest coordinate; its
second-largest point has coordinate d>=z−9. If z−a>=34, the candidate
pairs containing coordinates {a,b} and {d,z} have every cross spatial
distance at least sixteen, irrespective of their ticks. They violate
(iii). Hence z−a<=33. ∎

The spatial bound is sharp for this definition: six errors at one tick with
coordinates 0,9,10,23,24,33 form an isolated real level-1 set at c=16, and
all six belong to D. Its minimal candidate pairs cannot be separated by
sixteen: even the two outer pairs {0,9} and {24,33} are only fifteen apart.
There are no level-0 points, since each point has multiple linked neighbors.
The temporal bound is also sharp: triples at coordinates 0,1,2 at ticks
0 and 15 form an isolated real level-1 set. These two finite examples are
independently checked in
[dangerous_core.json](../figs/robustness/dangerous_core.json), with driver
[check_dangerous_core.py](../figs/robustness/check_dangerous_core.py).

For a trajectory from a pristine hierarchy with errors **only in E0 and
one such S**, a same-tick triple of span ten cannot include an E0 point:
the point's isolated singleton/pair would have a further linked point
outside that real level-0 error. Thus all triples of the full fault set are
in D(S). If D(S) is empty, (7) proves that all errors are corrected one tick
later, even though S was assigned level 1 geometrically.

More generally, all differences other than the current direct overwrites
lie in the radius-5 forward causal cone from D(S). To prove this, induct on
ticks. Outside the cone, a cell's input neighborhood contains no preceding
indirect difference. It contains at most two direct faults; otherwise its
triple belongs to D(S) and the output is in that cone. The local proof of
(7) therefore gives the pristine output there. New direct overwrites are
kept separate at the next tick. This establishes the induction for finite
or infinite E0 patterns.

In particular, at one tick after the last dangerous overwrite, indirect
damage lies in an interval of at most **194 sites**: its source span is at
most 33, and sixteen radius-5 steps enlarge that span by at most 160.
So the indirectly damaged interval is shorter than Q−10=374 throughout
the entire dangerous-forcing interval, by locality alone. The interval may
meet two adjacent actual colonies. This does not bound subsequent growth:
the remaining faults and autonomous island evolution still have to be
analyzed after that time.

This is a **source localization**, not an erosion theorem: its forward
cone keeps widening forever. Once a flagged island exists, faults outside
D can disturb it despite satisfying the healthy local density condition.
Replacing B=62 by 16 in Gray's complete recovery argument is therefore
unjustified. To finish a small-Q proof one still needs bounds on expansion,
flag return and erosion under these remaining faults. The new fact is that
the arbitrary-error forcing of a healthy trajectory is confined to (8).

### Universal growth of geometric damage under E0: proved

This statement concerns **Address/Age only**, allowing arbitrary flags,
Info and all other fields. The clean reference has aligned Address and a
common legal Age. Suppose at time t every stored geometric difference is
in an interval I_t=[a_t,b_t] or at the current direct overwrite sites N_t.
The N_t are singleton/adjacent-pair groups, mutually (24,24)-separated.
Additional arbitrary overwrites **inside** I_t are permitted. In particular
a fixed interior region may continue to be forced.

If a cell has at least three geometrically correct neighbors on each side,
both Address and both Age votes are correct. The flags can select either
vote without changing that conclusion. Therefore a computed geometric
difference needs at least three bad inputs in some one-sided five-site
window. This is a necessary condition, independent of replacement values.
Mark the whole I_t bad for an upper bound. Define

    l_t = |N_t intersect [a_t−4,a_t−1]|,
    r_t = |N_t intersect [b_t+1,b_t+4]|.                      (G1)

Both counts are at most two. Before new direct overwrites all geometric
differences are contained in

    [a_t−3−l_t, b_t+3+r_t].                                 (G2)

Indeed, without a fault in the exterior four-site window the first cell
four sites beyond the old edge has only two bad inward neighbors. With
one such fault only the fourth new site can be added; a fifth new site
would need two exterior faults. Six sites beyond the edge neither side
has an old bad neighbor, so E0's two faults cannot defeat either vote.
The left argument is identical. Arbitrary flags elsewhere cannot create
geometric differences when these votes agree. Iterating (G2), with the
new N_(t+1) kept separate, proves the interval invariant for any duration.

The following packing argument bounds the accumulated r_t more sharply
than just using radius five. For k nonzero right events at times t_i,
let p_i be the leftmost point in the counted exterior group. Its counted
part has r_i sites and span r_i−1, with
p_i=b_(t_i)+u_i, 1<=u_i<=4 and u_i+r_i−1<=4. Consecutive events d ticks
apart have frontier displacement 3d+r_i and increasing p_i. If d<24,
E0 separation implies p_(i+1)−(p_i+r_i−1)>=24. If d>=24 the frontier's
advance already implies that same inequality. Thus

    p_k−p_1 >= 23(k−1) + sum(i<k) r_i.

But the endpoint recurrence gives
p_k−p_1=3(t_k−t_1)+sum(i<k)r_i+u_k−u_1.
For T updates, t_k−t_1<=T−1 and u_k−u_1<=3, so
23(k−1)<=3T. Consequently

    sum(t<T) r_t <= 2[1+floor(3T/23)],
    b_T <= b_0 + (75/23)T + 2,
    a_T >= a_0 − (75/23)T − 2.                              (G3)

Use rightmost counted points for the reflected left argument. Empty event
lists have sum zero. This proves an arbitrary-time geometric growth bound
**strictly below four cells per tick**, with explicit startup terms, rather
than inferring it from a chosen coherent injection. The same proof with
spatial/time separation (22,23) gives rate 23/7 and allowance two. This
reduced-spacing result is also geometry-only; it does not provide the
missing effective upper error process or simulation-field correction.

A single E0 pair can nevertheless advance an edge **five sites in one
update**. For an explicit legal state take clean aligned geometry at Age
2000, change sites 70,...,95 to Address shifted by 32 and Age 2001, and
leave flags and other fields zero. Without another error the computed right
edge becomes 98. Overwriting sites 98,99 with the same wrong phase/Age
moves that edge to 100. At 100 three left adjusted words agree with the
wrong phase, three left Ages agree with 2001, inconsistency raises Flag1,
and Flag2 is zero; the left vote is therefore selected. At 101 both
geometric votes have three correct inputs. This is an exact counterexample
to a universal three-site **one-update** growth claim, not a counterexample
from a pristine hierarchy. Full C/NumPy equality and saved states are in
[geometry_jump.json](../figs/robustness/geometry_jump.json),
[check_geometry_jump.py](../figs/robustness/check_geometry_jump.py), and
[geometry_jump_state.npz](../figs/robustness/geometry_jump_state.npz).

[check_geometry_growth.py](proofs/check_geometry_growth.py) certifies the
actual whole-word majority's dominance for arbitrary faulty words by
constant Boolean expressions, checks (G2) in 182,016 local interval cases,
and verifies the event-packing arithmetic. Its receipt is
[geometry_growth_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/geometry_growth_certificate.json).
A separated-pair packing with time gaps 7,8,8 attains 75/23 in the scalar
count envelope. This does not assert that a repairing G17 island attains
that rate or survives that long. The universal claims rest on the proofs
above. **Erosion, lifetime and apparent-colony confinement remain unproved.**

### A 141-site geometric seed and subsequent lower-noise pattern: proved

There is a sharper reduction for phase memory than the 194-site all-field
cone. Still assume a pristine initial hierarchy and faults only in E0 and
one real level-1 set S. Define D_g(S) using triples at one tick of spatial
span at most **four**. A cell's Address/Age can first differ indirectly only
if some one-sided five-site vote sees such a triple. When D_g is empty,
the two-vote induction proves all computed geometry correct for all time,
irrespective of any resulting flag or simulation-field damage.

Otherwise let tau be the first tick of D_g and choose the closest pair
P={(p,tau),(q,tau)} in one of that tick's triples. Then 1<=q−p<=2.
It is a candidate level-1 pair. Put J=[p−15,q+15], of at most 33 sites.
Two distinct S points outside J on the same side cannot be (24,24)-linked:
otherwise their candidate pair would be (16,16)-separated from P in the
spatial coordinate, violating condition (iii). Points on opposite sides
are already at least 32 apart. Hence **all S points outside this fixed
spatial J are mutually (24,24)-separated**, across all their ticks. They
also have that separation from every actual E0 group, by level-0 isolation.

Before tau there is no indirect geometric damage, since every five-site
window has at most two direct faults. At tau the geometry outside J is
therefore correct except at N_tau consisting of these exterior singleton
S points and E0 groups. Treat geometry inside J as arbitrary, and include
all subsequent interior S overwrites in the permitted interior forcing.
The hypotheses of (G1)–(G3) now hold with I_0=J. At T=16 each endpoint
has advanced by at most 3*16+2[1+floor(48/23)]=54 sites. Thus at tau+16
all indirect geometric differences fit in an interval of at most

    33 + 2*54 = **141 sites**.                               (G4)

Current direct overwrites remain separate. This argument allows arbitrary
Address/Age words and every other overwritten field; no coherent shifted
block or measured return speed is assumed. It uses a fixed small forcing
interval and a separated exterior pattern, rather than treating S's entire
62-by-62 box as adversarial at every point.

Finally two S points at ticks >=tau+16 cannot be (24,24)-linked either:
their candidate pair would be temporally (16,16)-separated from P and again
violate (iii). From this cutoff onward, the **whole remaining overwrite
pattern** consists of separated singleton S points and E0 groups. The
original S points have not become real level-0 errors in the original
decomposition; only the forward restricted noise pattern has the required
spacing. The geometry at the cutoff has the 141-site seed (G4), while
flags and simulation fields are allowed to be damaged elsewhere.

[check_geometry_seed.py](proofs/check_geometry_seed.py) checks the closest
pair and seed arithmetic, and supplies literal real-level-1 examples for
both kinds of tail. In one example an original S error occurs at tick 38
despite a sixteen-tick cutoff: it is the **remaining pattern's spacing**,
not the last original error time, that changes. The certificate is
[geometry_seed_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/geometry_seed_certificate.json).
These finite examples check the interpretation of the definitions; the
universal tail conclusions are the candidate-pair contradictions above.

This reduces the structural repair problem to that smaller seed under
lower noise. It does **not** show its subsequent erosion. In particular
one still needs escape from the exceptional apparent-left-boundary case
below, delivery of Flag1 through apparent boundaries, control of Flag2
and a recovery deadline.
Nor does (G4) localize every simulation-field difference. No reliability
threshold or sufficient new Q/U pair follows from (G4) alone.

### A local left-front repair dichotomy: proved conditionally

There is a precise part of the left-edge inconsistency argument that does
not require a coherent shifted block. Consider one computed update at x.
Let A be its canonical reference Address and alpha its expected current
raw Age. Suppose at least three of its five left input cells have
canonical Addresses `(A−d) mod Q` and Age alpha, d=1,...,5. The other
inputs, flags and work fields may be arbitrary.

If the right Address vote has no majority, the update selects the left
votes regardless of computed Flag2 and returns canonical A and `h(alpha)`.
If that right majority does exist, assume **computed Flag2=0**. Then
either the computed Address has residue A modulo Q and computed Age is
`h(alpha)`, or both right whole-word majorities exist and their right
Address vote v lies in **0,...,4**. Without the two left faulty holders,
the exceptional set narrows to **0,1,2**. This is a single-update
statement before any new direct overwrite.

Proof: the two left votes equal A and alpha by whole-word dominance.
Failure of either right whole-word majority raises computed Flag1, so the
left votes are selected when the right Address majority is absent or
computed Flag2 is zero. Otherwise both right votes exist. If their
Address phase and raw Age already agree with A and alpha, either direction
gives the stated phase/Age result. If not, take v>=5. Every left input is
then in the apparent colony's `inside` mask. If `v mod Q != A`, each of
the at least three correct left Addresses mismatches the extrapolation
from v. The exact adder preserves residues on all raw words, so this also
covers invalid v. If instead the right Age differs from alpha, the at least
three correct left Ages mismatch it. Either case raises Flag1 and selects
the correct left votes. With five correct left inputs, v>=3 already gives
at least three mismatches through the mask. ∎

When this correction uses the left votes the Address is canonical, not
just phase-correct. The neutral case with an already correct right phase
can select a noncanonical alias, so the statement deliberately claims only
the Address **residue** there. The conditional 43-update normalization
theorem in §7 treats such aliases separately.

The exception cannot be removed from this snapshot lemma. Set A=100,
alpha=`age_code(2000)`, and give all five right inputs a coherent Address
vote v=2 and Age `age_code(2001)`. Leave all flags/workspace signals zero
and all five left inputs correct. Only two left mismatches are inside,
so computed Flag1=Flag2=0 and the wrong right vote is selected. With v=4,
overwriting the adjacent left inputs at distances one and two with that
same wrong pair leaves only two correct mismatches inside; it produces
the same failure despite three correct left votes. These are exact local
states, not a claim that such a state is reached from a pristine hierarchy
by one admissible burst.

[check_left_boundary.py](proofs/check_left_boundary.py) checks 1,966,080
Address/mask cases, including every raw v and canonical A, and 840
actual-gate symbolic cases whose output constants hold for **every**
assignment of their faulty words and free flags. It also verifies the
two sharp snapshot examples with the actual gates. Its receipt is
[left_boundary_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/left_boundary_certificate.json).
The general proof is the vote/mismatch argument above, not an extrapolation
from those examples. Control of computed Flag2, escape from apparent
left boundaries and a mixed-noise island lifetime remain **unproved**.

### Quiet rightward ancestry and an apparent-boundary window: proved conditionally

There is a useful constraint on Gray's p. 25 apparent-left-boundary exception
which does not assume a coherently shifted block. Call a stored cell
**quiet** when Flag1=0. The following is a local statement about the actual
G17 rule, with arbitrary Age, Flag2, Workspace and simulation fields.

Suppose (x,t), t>=1, is not a direct overwrite, is quiet, and its raw
Address is a in 0,...,Q−6. Then some j in 1,...,5 has

    Address_(t−1)(x+j)=a+j,  Flag1_(t−1)(x+j)=0.              (Q1)

This is an equality of canonical raw Address words, not just their residues.
For proof, computed Flag1=0 implies that both right whole-word majorities
exist. The selected Address is the right vote a regardless of Flag2.
Since a<Q−5, all five right neighbors are inside. The three-right-Flag1
setting test is false, so at least three of these neighbors have Flag1=0.
At least three adjusted right Address words equal a. These two sets must
intersect. For their common j, the exact adder's only preimage of a under
adjustment by −j mod Q is the canonical word a+j: a+j<Q, and an unused
raw input or a wrap from below j cannot give a<=Q−6. This proves (Q1).

Iterate (Q1) backwards until encountering a direct overwrite, the initial
time, or a quiet ancestor with Address in [Q−5,Q−1]. Each step moves right
by one to five sites and raises the raw Address by exactly that displacement.
Thus every node has the same phase `(position−Address) mod Q`. The total
displacement is at most Q−1−a, and the number of steps at most Q−5−a.
The terminal near-right-boundary alternative requires displacement at least

    D = Q−5−a, and at least ceil(D/5) backward updates.       (Q2)

This is a **proved noisy provenance alternative**, not a statement that
noise never terminates the path. If the starting Address phase is wrong,
all path nodes have that same wrong phase. In particular, with initially
correct Addresses, a quiet wrong small Address has a recent original
overwrite or a quiet wrong near-right-boundary ancestor. The near-boundary
alternative is not yet bounded probabilistically or repaired.

There is a clock version with an extra hypothesis: every non-overwritten
cell along the history has its canonical reference Address. Let alpha_t
be the common reference raw Age, advanced by the actual increment h.
A quiet, non-overwritten node with wrong raw Age and Address a<=Q−6 has
a quiet wrong-Age right ancestor at x+j, whose Address is a+j. Indeed
three right Age words equal the selected word beta; at least three right
Flag1 bits are zero. Choose their common neighbor. Its Age is wrong,
because `h(beta)!=alpha_t` implies `beta!=alpha_(t−1)`. Its Address is
a+j by the alignment hypothesis. No inverse of h, clock legality or common
wrong phase is assumed. The same terminal alternatives and distances (Q2)
hold. For initial globally aligned Address and no Address overwrites, that
Address hypothesis follows from the geometry-only vote invariant.

**Noise-free window for a short seed.** Suppose all initial Address
differences from the canonical reference lie in I_0=[a_0,b_0] of width w;
all other fields can be arbitrary everywhere. There are no subsequent
overwrites. Then at times

    w <= T <= floor((600−w)/3),  provided 1<=w<=150,          (Q3)

no site x>=a_0 can have both a wrong Address phase, Flag1=0 and raw
Address in 0,...,4. This concerns the apparent-boundary exception only;
it does not say all Address damage has disappeared. If instead Address
is initially aligned everywhere and Age differs from a common reference
only in I_0, the same window excludes a quiet wrong **raw Age** at any
x>=a_0 whose reference Address is in 0,...,4. Initial clocks can include
every unused word within I_0.

Here is the proof and the source of 600. For either field separately,
three correct inputs on each side force its next correct value, regardless
of which side the flags select. Thus the appropriate field's indirect
right endpoint is at most `b_s<=b_0+3s` without noise; arbitrary other
fields do not change this majority bound. Trace a supposed quiet bad node
back from (x,T). All its ancestors remain bad, hence lie at or left of
b_s. If the path reaches initial time, its at least T-site displacement
gives `y>=x+T>=a_0+w>b_0`, a contradiction. For a terminal Address near
the apparent right boundary, D>=Q−9=375. It needs at least 75 backward
steps. At its time s<=T−75 its displacement would satisfy

    D <= b_s−x <= (w−1)+3(T−75).

But (Q3) gives `(w−1)+3(T−75)<=374<D`. This excludes the other terminal
alternative. There is no overwrite alternative by hypothesis. The clock
proof uses its canonical-Address ancestry; the Address proof needs no
clock or workspace assumption. ∎

For the 141-site seed in (G4), the window is **updates 141 through 153**.
For width 150 it contains update 150 only. The number 150 is the largest
width admitted by this particular bound, not a maximum correctable burst.
For general Q the corresponding arithmetic is
`4w <= Q−9+3 ceil((Q−9)/5)`. This is a local sufficient condition on the
quiet-boundary witness, **not** a replacement for all of Gray's Proposition 2.
The actual (G4) tail can contain E0 and remaining S points: applying (Q3)
to it requires an error-free tail, not merely the already-proved spacing.
Mixed-E0 path interruption, lower Flag2/D4 control, motion to the left of
a_0, and a full structural recovery deadline remain **unproved**.

[check_quiet_ancestry.py](proofs/check_quiet_ancestry.py) checks all 1,895
relevant modular-inverse cases using the actual gates, 256 support
intersections, 24,256 actual Flag1 assignments and 75,000 window-arithmetic
cases. Its receipt is
[quiet_ancestry_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/quiet_ancestry_certificate.json).
The path and all-time alternatives are the elementary induction above;
the finite checker does not turn the noise-free window into a noisy bound.

### Independent votes obstruct joint quiet ancestry: proved counterexample
