The Address and clock statements above cannot be merged by supposing
every quiet rightward ancestor supports **both** votes. Address, Age and
quiet-Flag1 support each contain at least three of five neighbors, but
their triple intersection need not contain any neighbor. G17 has separate
whole-word votes, not a whole-pair vote.

An exact local example has reference Address 0 and current Age
alpha=`age_code(2000)`. The five right Addresses are 1,2,3,379,380;
the five Ages are alpha,alpha,beta,beta,beta with
beta=`age_code(2001)`; their Flag1 bits are 0,1,1,0,0. All left
geometry is correct; center Flag1/Flag2 and all Workspace flags are zero.
The adjusted right Address vote is 0, supported at distances {1,2,3}.
The right Age vote is beta, supported at {3,4,5}. Quiet right neighbors
are {1,4,5}. There is **no quiet neighbor supporting both votes**.
No left inconsistency is counted because the apparent Address is 0.
The actual output is quiet, with Address 0 and Age `age_code(2002)`.
The correct next Age would be `age_code(2001)`.

This obstruction can arise from a **single real c=16 level-1 error**:
overwrite the four adjacent sites at distances 2,3,4,5 at one tick of
an otherwise pristine Age-2000 orbit, leaving other fields unchanged.
The radius-five local formulas are exactly those just evaluated; all
pristine Workspace flags are zero there. The fault set fits a four-site
by one-tick box, has no real level-0 points, satisfies (iii) and is isolated
when there are no other errors. A finite reproduction starts from two
codec levels, runs 2000 ticks, applies these four overwrites and compares
the entire one-update C and CUDA outputs; they agree. The saved states are
[quiet_ancestry_burst.npz](../figs/robustness/quiet_ancestry_burst.npz), with
the classifier certificate and full-output hashes in the receipt above.
Reachability on a pristine infinite orbit follows from its proved local
geometry/zero-Workspace values; it does not depend on treating the finite
ring as an infinite hierarchy.

This disproves the proposed **joint ancestor inference**, not G17's
reliability or later correction of this burst. It also does not contradict
(7), which covers at most two faults per eleven sites, or the clock lemma
whose canonical-Address hypothesis fails at the two rightmost quiet
neighbors in this example. A proof must handle independent-vote mixing
or first establish Address alignment; it cannot assume a coherent pair
label merely because both individual majorities exist.

### Prefix erosion with controlled Flag1 and no Workspace.Flag2 source: proved conditionally

One part of Gray's p. 24 argument can be made quantitative at these constants:
periodic Flag2 generation can slow a correcting left front without stopping
it. This statement has explicit hypotheses stronger than those yet proved
for an actual island. It does not assume a coherent shifted block to its
right.

Let the reference Address be canonical `(x−b) mod Q` and the reference raw
Age at state time t be alpha_t=`h^t(alpha_0)`, with arbitrary initial word.
Let N_t be the current direct overwrites from E0 groups. Initially every
site x<=B_0 has the reference geometry and Flag2=0 except N_0. For the
frontier B_t defined below require, before the next direct overwrites,

* computed Flag1=1 on `[B_t−4,B_t+1]`;
* computed D4, the three-inside-Workspace.Flag2 source test, is zero at
  every x<=B_t+1.

All other fields, and everything to the right of B_0, may be arbitrary.
Distinct singleton/adjacent-pair overwrite groups are (24,24)-separated.
Then after T updates the reference-geometry/zero-Flag2 prefix extends to
a frontier satisfying

    B_T >= B_0+T−4 ceil(T/16)−2 ceil(T/17)
        >= B_0+(43/68)T−6.                                 (G5)

The only permitted exceptions in that prefix are N_T and a one-update
halo H_T: the right endpoints of adjacent pairs in N_(T−1) that lie at
or before B_T. Multiple separated groups can create multiple such halo
sites, but at most one halo site meets any eleven-site input window.
The halo is an overapproximation of possible retained Flag2 and geometry
errors; it is not a claim that each such endpoint is actually wrong.

**Invariant and one-step proof.** Initially H_0 is empty. In an input
window of eleven sites, N_t and H_t cannot coexist: a halo is caused by
the preceding tick's adjacent pair, and another group that close would
violate separation. Thus at most two inputs are exceptional in any such
window. Every x<=B_t+1 has three correct left geometry inputs. Its left
Address vote is canonical and its left Age vote is alpha_t.

For arbitrary computed Flag1 and inside masks, the actual Flag2 update
obeys the upper bound

    Flag2_new <= D3 OR D4 OR T2(s),
    T2(s) = [at least four left s bits are 1]
            OR [s(x)=1 AND at least one left s bit is 1].

This follows separately for old s(x)=0 and 1 from candidate B's setting
and erasure predicates. On the prefix D4=0 by hypothesis. D3 can only
fire when alpha_t's low four bits are 15, once per sixteen updates, since
the left Age vote is exact even for an unused raw word. A missing right
Address majority needs at least three incorrect right inputs.

Define `phase_t=1` on that clock residue. On other updates let

    B_(t+1) = B_t+1−I,
    I = 1 if (N_t union H_t) meets [B_t−4,B_t], else 0.

On a source-phase update let

    B_(t+1) = B_t−3−2J−K,
    J = 1 if N_t meets [B_t−3,B_t], else 0,
    K = 1 if H_t meets [B_t−2,B_t], else 0.

Here J and K cannot both be one. Set H_(t+1) to the right endpoints of
current adjacent pairs lying at or before B_(t+1).

To verify Flag2, first take a nonphase update. At x<=B_t, four left ones
cannot arise from the at most two exceptional sites. An old isolated
halo one has no left one and clears. Of a current adjacent pair only its
right endpoint can retain a one, giving H_(t+1). At B_t+1 all five left
bits are zero unless I=1, explaining the omitted advance in that case.
At a phase update, without a nearby exception three arbitrary right
inputs first become possible at x=B_t−2. A current pair can move this
possibility left to B_t−4, and a halo to B_t−3. The stated J/K recurrence
cuts the prefix before every such source. The same T2 argument covers
the nonsource part of the prefix.

For geometry, sufficiently far left both right and left geometry votes
are correct despite the two exceptions. In `[B_t−4,B_t+1]`, computed
Flag1=1 and the just-proved computed Flag2=0 select the correct left
votes, whether or not a right majority exists. Only the retained halo
sites are excluded. New direct overwrites add N_(t+1) and cannot be near
the old group producing H_(t+1). This closes the invariant. It covers
arbitrary right phases/Ages and flags, not just square-block patterns.

**Loss accounting.** A phase update costs four sites relative to a unit
advance. There are at most ceil(T/16) such updates. All extra losses come
from E0 groups meeting the eight-site zone `[B_t−7,B_t]`; a halo can be
charged to its causing group there at the preceding tick. One group costs
at most two sites over its current and halo updates. A nonphase adjacent
pair can freeze one advance and its right-end halo the next. If it causes
J=1 on a phase update, the two-site extra retreat already drops that
pair outside the new prefix; it cannot also leave a delaying halo. If a
nonphase pair precedes a halo-phase K=1, each update costs one. A pair
farther left can leave a halo after a phase retreat, but its next-update
delay costs only one. Singletons obey the same two-site upper bound.
Groups outside the eight-site zone contribute no loss.

Let u<v be consecutive affecting events, d=v−u. They cannot be adjacent:
the frontier's one-step change lies between −5 and 1, and the two
event points have offsets in −7,...,0, giving spatial distance at most
12<24. Thus no older halo loss is pending when event u occurs. Between
u and v there are no other affecting groups, so

    B_v−B_u = d−4P−L,  P<=ceil(d/16),  0<=L<=2.

This displacement lies between −5 and d. For d<=16 the distance between
selected event points is at most `max(d,5)+7 <= 23`, and their time gap
is below 24. Separation forbids this, so d>=17. There are at most
ceil(T/17) affecting events. Summing their charges proves (G5), using
`1−4/16−2/17=43/68`. ∎

[check_eroding_prefix.py](proofs/check_eroding_prefix.py) checks the Flag2
upper predicate on 8,192 assignments, 488 local prefix/halo cases,
1,184 two-update group charges and 768 packing cases. Its receipt is
[eroding_prefix_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/eroding_prefix_certificate.json).
The all-duration conclusion is the invariant and packing proof, not a
finite simulation extrapolation. **Unproved:** the island supplies computed
Flag1 on the moving edge, has no D4 source invading that prefix, escapes
apparent-boundary exceptions, and has a right edge/lifetime compatible
with the schedule. In particular (G5) is not Proposition 2 or a reliability
threshold, and its startup allowance is not asserted minimal.

### A true-colony right barrier: proved with explicit source hypotheses

The undamaged-right-colony assertion in Gray pp. 23–24 can be made
precise for this rule. It needs a Workspace.Flag1 hypothesis; unrestricted
other fields alone do not supply it. The following theorem allows arbitrary
damage and arbitrary forcing to its left.

Let C be a **true colony boundary**, so its canonical reference Address
is zero. At state time zero, all x>=C have canonical Address and a common
raw Age alpha_0, apart from current direct overwrite sites N_0. Let
alpha_t=h^t(alpha_0). In the first colony [C,C+Q), initial Flag1 is zero
outside N_0. Here N_t denotes current direct overwrites in the protected
suffix; left-hand forcing is unrestricted separately. For every input
time t, require Workspace.Flag1 zero in that first colony outside N_t.
At each tick the overwrite sites in x>=C have
at most two members in any eleven-site interval. Everything else can be
arbitrary: the entire state left of C, Flag1/Workspace.Flag1 beyond the
first colony, all Flag2/Workspace.Flag2 bits and all simulation fields.
No temporal spacing or adjacency assumption is needed for this theorem.

Then, at every update before the next overwrites,

    Address_new(x) = (x−b) mod Q,  Age_new(x)=alpha_(t+1)
                         for every x>=C,
    Flag1_new(x)=0       for C<=x<C+Q.                      (G6)

The stored geometry differs from reference only on N_(t+1), and stored
Flag1 in the first colony is zero outside N_(t+1).

**Proof.** Suppose the input invariant holds. Every right five-site vote
in the suffix has three correct inputs, so the right Address vote is the
canonical holder Address A and the right Age vote is alpha_t. The computed
inside mask is therefore the actual true colony. At a holder in the
first colony, all left inputs counted by that mask are at or right of C.
Only direct faults among the counted inputs can mismatch its right votes;
there are at most two such faults in the protected part of its eleven-site
neighborhood. No inconsistency is raised. Its
in-colony Workspace.Flag1 test also sees at most two ones. Right Flag1
bits counted by the mask are zero except direct faults, so the threshold
of three cannot fire. If the center Flag1 is one, it is a direct fault;
two counted right ones would require three faults in the same window.
Thus the persistence test cannot fire either, and computed Flag1 is zero
throughout the first colony. Those holders select the correct right
geometry, independently of Flag2. For x>=C+Q, all five left inputs also
lie in the healthy suffix, so both directional votes are correct and any
flag selection gives the reference geometry. New overwrites add only
N_(t+1). This proves the induction. The same proof works under the weaker
hypothesis that each computed in-colony Workspace.Flag1 source test is
zero. ∎

If geometric damage initially ends at b_0<C, (G6) prevents any indirect
rightward escape beyond C−1 for as long as its source hypothesis holds.
Choosing the next true boundary after b_0 would give an edge allowance
of at most Q−1. Establishing quiet Flag1 and source exclusion there from
an actual higher-error trajectory remains a separate obligation.

**The source hypothesis cannot simply be omitted.** At reference Address
zero and Age `age_code(2000)`, put correct geometry throughout the suffix,
but Workspace.Flag1 ones at offsets 0,1,2. Take all Flag1/Flag2 and
Workspace.Flag2 bits zero. On the left put coherent Address phase shifted
by 32 and Age `age_code(2001)`. The actual computed boundary output has
Flag1=1, Flag2=0, Address 32 and Age `age_code(2002)`. The three sources
select the incorrect left vote. This is an exact local counterexample
to removing the premise, not a pristine-hierarchy unreliability example.
These input Workspace bits are outside the range of **fresh** healthy
Workspace writes; damaged input states can nevertheless contain them.

### A finite right barrier with arbitrary command bits: proved for the full rule

One can discharge a weaker source premise for a finite interval without
proving command provenance. The actual full-rule output in `rule_g.build`
has Workspace.Flag1 gated by computed Address in [Q−5,Q). Thus, whenever
computed geometry in the suffix is correct, every non-overwritten fresh
Workspace.Flag1 bit there lies in its true colony's last five cells,
whatever values the program, Info copies or command bits contain.

Keep the preceding initial suffix-geometry hypothesis. In the first colony,
initial Flag1 may be arbitrary on its last **ten** cells, but is zero
elsewhere outside N_0; initial Workspace.Flag1 may be arbitrary on its
last **five** cells, but is zero elsewhere outside N_0. Future overwrite
groups in the protected suffix are singletons or adjacent pairs,
mutually (24,24)-separated.
No subsequent Workspace source exclusion is assumed. All other fields
and the state/forcing to the left of C are unrestricted as in (G6).

Then the full G17 rule preserves correct computed geometry on x>=C for
at least **113 updates**, with only current direct overwrite exceptions
in the stored geometry. More generally the proved sufficient duration T
for these radius-five/end-gated formulas satisfies

    3T + 2[1+floor((3T+1)/23)] <= Q−15.                    (G7)

This is a lower bound on barrier duration under the stated initial
hypotheses, not a claim of failure after it or an optimal duration.

**Proof.** Bootstrap correct suffix geometry. Only direct faults can
produce inconsistencies in the first colony's inside mask, and their
number is at most two, so its inconsistency source is zero. Any
nonfault Workspace.Flag1 input is in the last five cells. A holder with
Address <Q−10 cannot see any such input in its eleven-site neighborhood;
two direct faults alone cannot set its source. Hence computed Workspace
sources are confined to Addresses >=Q−10, even when commands are wrong.

Start an upper envelope of raised Flag1 bits at L_0=Q−10, filling its
entire suffix within the first colony, and add current direct fault sites.
Let

    r_t = |N_t intersect [C+L_t−5,C+L_t−1]|,
    L_(t+1)=L_t−3−r_t.

All computed Flag1 ones are at Address >=L_(t+1). To check this,
three right ones cannot reach more than three cells left of L_t without
noise. One fault can add at most one cell. To reach five cells left
requires two faults: either two right faults join the one old envelope
bit, or a faulty center persists using that bit and another right fault.
Six cells left has no old envelope bit among its right five inputs;
the two faults cannot set three right ones or a center with two right
ones. This proves the recurrence; the five-site noise zone, including
the center at distance five, is essential for the persistence case.
Workspace sources are already to its right since L_t<=Q−10.

Reflect the leading coordinate, B_t=−(C+L_t). It advances by 3+r_t.
For k affecting events at times t_i, their counted noise sites lie in
[B_(t_i)+1,B_(t_i)+5]. Let p_i be the leftmost counted point and r_i
its count. As in (G3), adjacent groups have counted span r_i−1.
Consecutive events satisfy

    p_(i+1)−(p_i+r_i−1) >= 24:

for a time gap below 24 this follows from the noise separation; for a
gap at least 24 it follows from the frontier's advance, even allowing
the four-site difference of offsets in this five-site zone. Telescoping
and using t_k−t_1<=T−1 gives

    23(k−1) <= 3(T−1)+4 = 3T+1,
    L_T >= Q−10−3T−2[1+floor((3T+1)/23)].

If this last bound is at least five, computed Flag1 is zero at the
first five sites of the protected suffix. Those sites select the correct
right vote. Every later site has three correct left and three correct
right inputs regardless of its flags. Thus all computed geometry is
correct, and fresh Workspace.Flag1 satisfies the end gate. This closes
the bootstrap and induction until the stated bound reaches five.
For G17, T=113 costs 369 sites, leaving 384−10−369=5;
T=114 does not satisfy this sufficient inequality. ∎

There is a longer **clock-gated corollary** to (G6). If the initial
Workspace.Flag1 is zero in the first colony outside N_0 and the common
reference clock stays outside the full rule's Workspace window, fresh
Workspace.Flag1 there is zero regardless of all other fields. The (G6)
source premise then follows inductively until the window opens. On legal
clocks that window is Ages 13,537 through 14,304 inclusive. This removes
command provenance from the right-barrier proof during source-free clock
intervals; it does not remove the initial Flag1/geometry hypotheses or
prove their restoration after an error. During the active window (G7)
gives the stated finite conservative protection under its specified
initial bounds.

The local proof and certificates are in
[check_right_barrier.py](proofs/check_right_barrier.py) and
[right_barrier_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/right_barrier_certificate.json).
The checker covers all 384 canonical Addresses and all 55 choices of two
arbitrary structural faults in eleven sites: 21,120 symbolic cases, with
all sixteen common Age bits free, arbitrary Flag2/Workspace.Flag2 and
arbitrary flags outside the first colony. It uses a **proved identical-word
majority shortcut** in a copied build function: three identical symbolic
words force the actual bitwise majority and three whole-word equality
tests. The original primitive is checked on all 160 one-bit assignments
for the ten fault-pair placements and arbitrary fallback. No active
helper or rule was changed. The recurrence additionally has 128 actual
Flag1 truth-table assignments, local front/source cases, packing checks
and duration arithmetic; the output gates are checked on all 512 Address
and 65,536 Age words. These support the algebraic induction above,
which supplies the unbounded (G6) conclusion and the finite (G7) bound.

**Still unproved:** an admissible protected boundary exists through every
higher-error episode, its source-free interval or finite protection lasts
until left erosion finishes, and recovery/restoration then gives the
required simulation and upper-error footprints. In particular, the
113-update certificate does not supply G17's 648-tick Proposition 2
envelope. Neither theorem is an all-time noise threshold.

J41 below now supplies a separate3944-tick barrier for G17 at every starting
clock when the right half-line begins as the full pristine operational
snapshot. It closes command protection under that stronger local premise;
it does not supply the missing left-erosion or higher-error projection.

### The existing replacement race remains unproved

The proposed replacement says that a held, coherently shifted block can
finish forming only after (5/6)(Q-w) ticks: expansion at speed 3, followed
by flag return at speed 2. The measured thresholds in REPORT §§32–33 are
consistent with this description **for those injections**. Missing are:

* a proof that every adversarial error pattern is dominated by that block;
* arbitrary Address/Age/flag/workspace values, including unused bit patterns;
* pre-existing partial colonies and islands, several fronts, and both flags;
* worst-case level-0 errors during erosion and flag return; (G3) now bounds
  geometric growth universally but does not prove their joint race;
* explicit bounds on both spatial escape and all repair delays, with startup
  and boundary terms, sufficient for the simulation schedule.

Acceleration of the growing edge and slowing of flag return need not have
the same effect on the race. Replacing 3 by a measured or hypothesized
upper speed 4 while leaving the rest of the pattern fixed does not settle
the mixed-noise problem. It is not a worst-case comparison lemma.

There is a separate timing obstacle to using Gray's proposition literally.
G17 has U/32 = 648. The quoted estimate 2Q+5.5B is 1109 for B=62 and
1169.5 for B=73, both greater than 648. REPORT instead compares it with
the rest between gathers. That could support a different proposition, but
not the stated U/32 envelope without a new argument. Nor is every active
operation that far from the next one: the pinned recipe's latest third
capture is Age 9591, and evaluation starts at Age 9792, just 201 ticks later.
Thus the generic “at most one active stage disturbed” inference cannot be
imported for the entire G17 schedule. These are failed proof hypotheses,
not experiments showing that G17 fails to repair a level-1 error.

Finally, the local rule is not exactly Gray's printed rule. Gray p. 21 erases
Flag2 in case (a) when computed Flag1 is zero and **no** left in-colony
site has Flag2 zero. G17's `maintenance.build` erases in this case when
at most **one** left in-colony site has Flag2 one. These predicates are
different. Gray's printed predicate also appears inconsistent with the
one-tick correction discussion; that is a reason to analyze the corrected
variant, not to silently replace a proof hypothesis. REPORT §9 already
calls this candidate-B erasure and leaves the printed persistence question
open. Its wave behavior, especially amid lower errors, needs its own proof.

### Whole-word ancestry and unused clock words: proved auxiliary bounds

`majority_word` returns a whole input word appearing at least three times,
or its supplied default. It never returns a synthesized bitwise word when
there is no whole-word majority. Thus each computed current Age is one
neighbor's stored Age or the holder's own word, followed by one application
of the packed increment h. Its ancestral path moves at most five sites per
tick. Independent Address and Age votes can have different ancestors, so
this does not identify an island with one coherently shifted block.

For any 16-bit Age word write p for its low nine bits and b for the other
seven. The **actual** increment, including unused values, is

    p' = 0 if p=287, else (p+1) mod 512;
    b' = (0 if b=71, else (b+1) mod 128) if p=287, else b.     (C1)

The legal set is p<288, b<72. It is closed under h. If p>=288, it reaches
zero in at most 224 steps without changing b, after which positions remain
legal. An invalid b>=72 reaches block zero after 128−b block increments.
If p was initially legal this takes `(128−b)288−p` steps. If p>=288 it
takes `(512−p)+(128−b)288`. Hence every word becomes legal within

    K = 224 + 56*288 = **16352** updates.                    (C2)

This is sharp at word 37152, with b=72 and p=288. The exhaustive checker
[check_g17_clock.py](proofs/check_g17_clock.py) compares the actual increment
gates with (C1) on **all 65,536 words** and computes all distances to the
legal set; its receipt is
[clock_legality_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/clock_legality_certificate.json).

The ancestry property promotes this word bound to a CA statement: after
K error-free updates, every Age in an arbitrary initial configuration is
legal. Trace one Age backward for K steps, obtaining `h^K(a)` for an initial
word a. Which ancestor is selected can depend on the other fields and the
flags; every selection still gives one word, so the argument is universal.
With noise, a nonlegal Age at (x,t), from an initially legal clock, requires
an overwrite in the last min(t,K) ticks of its radius-5 backward cone.
For independent rate-ε overwrites, therefore,

    Pr{Age at (x,t) is nonlegal} <= M ε,
    M = sum(j=0,...,K−1)(10j+1)
      = 5K²−4K = **1,336,874,112**.                         (C3)

For t>=K this bound even allows arbitrary initial Ages. This statement is
about the mathematically completed F, not the unguarded executables. It
proves legality only: a legal clock can have the wrong phase indefinitely
without external repair. K greatly exceeds both U/32 and the gather rest,
so natural expiration of invalid words cannot justify the short repair
deadline by itself. Equation (C3) is **not a memory/noise threshold**.

Unused clock words also admit an exact **phase map**. Let d(a) be the
distance of raw word a to the legal clock cycle, and let L(a) be the legal
word obtained by applying h exactly d(a) times. Define

    psi(a) = [tick(L(a)) − d(a)] mod U.
    psi(h(a)) = psi(a)+1 mod U.                              (C4)

For a nonlegal a its successor has distance d(a)−1, proving the identity;
on the legal cycle it is ordinary clock increment. Thus if an update has
no Age overwrite, `psi(Age_new(x))−(t+1)` is exactly
`psi(Age_t(y))−t` for some selected y with |y−x|<=5. Other fields and flags
can change that selection but cannot create a clock phase. An arbitrary
Age overwrite can introduce one. This is a provenance invariant for all
raw words, not an assertion that wrong phases are repaired.

Each phase has at most four raw representations. Indeed put
`r(b)=288b` for b<72 and `r(b)=288(b−128)` otherwise. Formula (C1) gives
`psi(a)=[r(b)+p−512*1_{p>=288}] mod U`. A target phase with legal position
q has possible raw positions p=q and, when q>=64, p=q+224. For each of
these there are at most two raw blocks b with the required r(b) modulo U.
The extended clock certificate checks (C4) on every one of the 65,536
actual gate outputs and counts these preimages. For example the phases
of words 37152, 17868 and 65535 are 4384, 9740 and 20447 respectively.
Equal phase does not mean equal stored word: their nonlegal aliases can
remain nonlegal for the long bound (C2). Neither (C4) nor that four-word
count supplies the missing island eroder.

There is also an Address ancestry statement, including unused words. For
a stored word A at site x put θ=(x−A) mod Q. The exact adder's output has
residue `(A+v) mod Q` for every 9-bit A and every constant 0<=v<Q, because
the sum is at most 511+383=894 and it subtracts Q once when necessary.
The result is at most 510 and fits in nine bits, so no truncation changes
its residue. Even when its output is
noncanonical, that residue is correct. Consequently each adjusted Address
has its neighbor's θ; whole-word majority/default selection and the final
mux choose one existing θ. No new Address phase is created without an
Address overwrite. Canonical Address words also form a closed domain if
all Address overwrites are canonical. None of these facts bounds the
spread or survival of an already incorrect phase.

Unlike Age legality, Address legality is not an unconditional normalizer.
If the entire Address field is any fixed word A, all five adjusted left
words are distinct, as are the five adjusted right words. Both majorities
fail, and the left fallback is the current A. The Address field stays
constant forever regardless of the other fields; this includes A=500.
This is not a counterexample from a pristine hierarchy, but it rules out
repair arguments that assume invalid Addresses disappear just by running
the local rule for a fixed time.

There is, however, a useful **conditional 43-update normalization theorem**.
Suppose all stored Address phases are correct: at every x,
`Address(x) mod Q = (x-b) mod Q`. Assume there are no further Address
overwrites for 43 updates. Every other field may be arbitrary and may even
be overwritten arbitrarily during those updates. Then every Address word
becomes exactly the canonical `(x-b) mod Q` within 43 updates.

To prove this, write A for the canonical reference at the holder. A stored
phase-correct word is either A or A+384, the latter possible only when
A<128. At a left neighbor at distance j=1,...,5, the actual modular adder
uses constant +j. Its maximum sum is 516, so one subtraction of 384 gives
the **canonical** holder reference A for either stored representation,
including wraparound. All five adjusted left words therefore agree with
A. Adjusted right words are either A or A+384; the second case requires
an aliased right input within the same true colony's first 128 sites.
Their five-word majority always exists, and is aliased only if at least
three of the five right inputs are aliased. Main Address selection can
choose this right word or the canonical left word. It never creates a
wrong phase, and cannot create an alias unless that three-bit right test
holds. This conclusion is independent of Age, all flags and program data.

Thus each colony's alias indicator is dominated by the monotone update
`e_new(x) = threshold_3(e(x+1),...,e(x+5))`, with e zero beyond Address 127.
The maximal initial strip [0,127] shrinks at its right end by three sites
per update. It is empty after ceil(128/3)=43 updates. Monotonicity gives
the same bound for every initial alias pattern. Phase preservation and
normalization hold simultaneously in every colony. ∎

The checker [check_address_aliases.py](proofs/check_address_aliases.py)
verifies all 5,120 raw Address/constant combinations of the actual adder,
all phase-correct adjustment cases, and the 43-step maximal-strip
domination. A short full C run supplies supplementary finite support;
[address_alias_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/address_alias_certificate.json)
records its scope. This theorem repairs unused **representations of an
already correct phase**. A globally constant invalid Address field does
not have correct phase and is not covered. Wrong-phase erosion, clock-phase
restoration and general damaged-colony simulation remain unproved.

## 8. Simulation recovery: Proposition 4 needs a new proof

The conditional restoration theorem (5c) removes one unrestricted-workspace
obstacle **after global physical geometry is aligned**: a complete period
recovers an admissible encoding from arbitrary other fields and copies.
This does not establish a local two-colony upper footprint, preserve the
intended pre-error upper value, or prove structural alignment after a
higher error. Those are the additional obligations in this section.

For the induction, one must track **every stored copy** of Info, Hold,
histories, mail, scratch, pending writes and front registers, plus the
Workspace flag signals. Decoded majority equality is weaker than recovery
of these fields. Correct neighbors can be affected by bad mail from a
damaged colony; three gathers protect them only if the requisite two
samples and the later computations have the required provenance.

G17 has period-boundary wipes of histories/mail/scratch, a Hold wipe before
evaluation, gather reloads, and geometric resets of the front. Gray wipes
Mailbox and unneeded Workspace at the start of each of five stages, with
rest periods and specified deadlines. The repository's schedule overlaps
other computation with the flag program. To use it, prove which values
survive each hit, which are overwritten before their next use, and why at
most two adjacent upper cells can be affected at the allowed upper times.
Include a burst straddling commit, a hit on a courier or pending write, a
missed capture after an Age corruption, and the flagged-region exception
in §5. This provenance/wipe invariant is absent.

The 128 certified G17 level-1 samples and the larger design-burst campaigns
are relevant evidence. They do not quantify over every 62-wide sparse
class member or every replacement word. The dense 72-wide campaigns
are **not** single level-1 errors for c=16. The two-upper-step cases in
those campaigns do not by themselves falsify the theorem for the certified
class, but they do falsify an unrestricted claimed footprint for arbitrary
design bursts. There must be a precise contextual footprint lemma before
these cases can be used in an all-level induction.

## 9. Renormalization is a dynamical statement

Saying that the same finite rule is evaluated at every level is not enough.
One needs a decoding of faulty trajectories, even where Address and Age
are damaged, and a proof that its deviations fit the error model needed at
the next level. [codec.py](../gacsca/codec.py) decodes a fixed aligned grid;
it does not define the changing full/partial/misaligned cells in Gray's
induction, or Gács's history-dependent robust-medium decoding.

Even if a physical level-1 footprint occupies two adjacent colonies at one
upper time, its separation from other such footprints loses spatial and
temporal units when enlarging boxes and rounding times. The old ledger's
(22,23) calculation is conditional on just such an envelope. Those
footprints do not automatically satisfy the literal (24,24) definition of
upper level-0 noise. One needs either an induction formulated with adequate
slack and a correction lemma for the reduced separation, or a different
damage map with a proved restoration property. An upper footprint lasting
two times requires additional treatment.

Likewise the original error set's 68-unit box says nothing on its own about
the time taken to repair it, or its effective upper support. Merely declaring
a persistent shifted colony to be “a level-2 error” changes the damage
description, not the level of the original Bernoulli error set. Reclassification
needs explicit witnesses and support/isolation bounds. Smaller c can promote
clusters to a higher *geometric* level; §4 pays their probability cost. It
does not prove they are corrected at that level.

Executing F directly on a ring of level-1 cells reproduces the level-0
maintenance pattern in changed units. It cannot establish that damaged
physical colonies actually realize that trajectory. The hand-off and the
decoder intertwining relation are the missing implication. Thus the race
measurements on the level-1 automaton add evidence about F, but not a
proof of the hierarchical induction.

## 10. Flag propagation and the remaining higher-level repair problem

At the left edge of an island, a proof needs a quantified delay to detect
missing communication, generate the upper Flag1, and trickle it through
arbitrarily many partial levels. At the right edge it needs a quantified
retreat from Flag2 that pays for growth due to lower errors. “24 > 16”
is not that estimate. For example, if a disturbance expands the edge by at
most a cells every 24 upper steps and a reversal moves it back at least b
cells every 16 steps, positive net retreat requires b/16 > a/24, with
additional allowance for phase, failed pulses and startup. Neither a nor b
has been proved for G17's faulty hierarchy. The lifetimes and alignment of
newly created colonies must be included too.

### Candidate-B flag pulses under level-0 noise: proved conditionally

The following bounds are for the **actual candidate-B predicates**, not the
different printed erasure predicate. They apply for any duration T during
which their explicit local hypotheses hold. They do not assume that a
damaged colony can supply those hypotheses.

Write s_t(x) for one flag field after update t, and N_t for the direct
overwrite sites at that update. Suppose the noise consists of singleton or
adjacent-pair groups at one tick, and distinct groups are (24,24)-separated.
Arbitrary values of all overwritten fields are allowed. For a lower bound
we replace overwritten flag bits by zero; any positive bits only help the
monotone rules below. In any six-site window the zeros of N_t belong to
at most one such group.

When **computed Flag1 is 1**, the Flag2 output before direct noise is

    source OR T2(s),
    T2(s)(x) = [at least four of s(x−1),...,s(x−5) are 1]
               OR [s(x)=1 AND at least one of those five is 1].       (9)

Here `source` is d3 OR d4 from `maintenance.build`. To derive (9), the
all-left four-bit test dominates the inside-only four-bit test. The erase
condition reduces to no left bit being one. Substitution into the old-bit
mux gives exactly (9). In particular it is monotone in all six flag bits,
and sources can only increase it. No Address, Age or inside hypothesis is
required once computed Flag1=1 has been established at the output cell.
With no source or noise, an interval [a,b] of at least four ones becomes
exactly [a+1,b+2]: its left end advances one, its right end advances two.

For Flag1, when all five right neighbors are **inside the computed colony**,
its output before direct noise is

    source OR T1(s),
    T1(s)(x) = [at least three of s(x+1),...,s(x+5) are 1]
               OR [s(x)=1 AND at least two of those five are 1].       (10)

The source here is inconsistency OR the Workspace.Flag1 test. This is again
monotone. With no source or noise, an interval [a,b] of at least three ones
becomes [a−3,b−2]. Thus its leading left end moves three and its trailing
right end two. At an actual colony boundary the inside hypothesis can fail;
(10) then supplies no cross-boundary claim.

**One-update lower intervals.** Suppose s_t is one on every point of an
interval [a,b], except possibly N_t, and its length is at least ten. Extra
ones outside the interval are permitted. For Flag2 put

    I_L = 1 if N_t meets [a,a+3],       I_R = 1 if N_t meets [b−4,b].

If computed Flag1 is one throughout the required output interval, then
before the next direct overwrites Flag2 is one on

    [a+1+4 I_L, b+2−2 I_R].                              (11)

For completeness, consider an old zero inside that interval. Away from its
left end it is a direct overwritten point; at most one other overwritten
point lies in its five left neighbors, because its group is a singleton or
adjacent pair and every other group is at least 24 away. Those neighbors
therefore contain four good ones, restoring the zero. An old one needs
only one good left neighbor. If I_L=0, the first four input sites have no
fault; even a zero at a+4 has four good left neighbors. If I_L=1, starting
at a+5 puts all five left inputs in the old interval. This proves the
interior assertion. If I_R=0, all inputs b−4,...,b are good, and the new
sites b+1 and b+2 have five and four good left inputs. If I_R=1 these two
sites are omitted, while b and all remaining old sites satisfy the same
interior argument. This proves (11) for any interval length, rather than
only the finite examples checked below.

For Flag1 put

    J_L = 1 if N_t meets [a,a+2],       J_R = 1 if N_t meets [b−2,b].

When the inside hypothesis of (10) holds at each required output, it is one
before direct overwrites on

    [a−3+2 J_L, b−2−2 J_R].                              (12)

Here a−1 always has at least three good right inputs among a,...,a+4,
even with two faults. With J_L=0 the three inputs a,a+1,a+2 also establish
the leading site a−3 (and a−2). An old one at x<=b−4 has at least four
right inputs in the old interval, of which at least two remain good. An
old zero there has at most one other faulty right input, so at least three
remain good. If J_R=0, the last three old sites are good, and the argument
extends to b−2. Otherwise ending at b−4 gives the bound. Thus (12) holds
even with arbitrarily many separated fault groups in the bulk.

**All-duration Flag2 bound.** Start with an interval of length w_0>=16,
one except for current direct overwrites. Define its endpoints recursively
by (11), using the actual N_t at each tick. Assume computed Flag1=1 on
the required output intervals for T updates. Let L_T and R_T count the
ticks with I_L=1 and I_R=1 among those T updates. Then

    a_T = a_0 + T + 4 L_T,
    b_T = b_0 + 2T − 2 R_T.                              (13)

Two successive left-affecting faults at times u and v=u+d have selected
points in [a_u,a_u+3] and [a_v,a_v+3]. With no intervening left event,
a_v−a_u=d+4, so their spatial distance is at most d+7. If d<=16 their
time and spatial distances are both below 24, contradicting separation.
Thus left events are at least **17 ticks apart**. For successive right
events, b_v−b_u=2d−2; their selected points lie within four of those ends,
so their distance is at most 2d+2 (including d=1). If d<=10 this is less
than 24. Thus right events are at least **11 ticks apart**. Consequently

    L_T <= ceil(T/17),       R_T <= ceil(T/11),
    a_T <= a_0 + (21/17)T + 4,
    b_T >= b_0 + (20/11)T − 2,
    b_T−a_T+1 >= w_0 − 6 + (109/187)T.                   (14)

The resulting lower interval always has length at least ten, closing the
induction used in (11). All of it is one except the **current** direct
overwrites; bulk punctures heal in the next update. There may be many
separated punctures in a long interval. Its last three sites contain at
least one guaranteed one, so a guaranteed rightmost one is at least b_T−2.
These are bounds on a surviving lower interval and its advancing edge,
not an assertion that every raw flag copy is uncorrupted at every tick.

**All-duration Flag1 bound.** Start with w_0>=14 and assume (10)'s inside
hypothesis on the required output intervals for T updates. With L_T and
R_T counting J_L and J_R events, (12) gives

    a_T = a_0 − 3T + 2 L_T,
    b_T = b_0 − 2T − 2 R_T.                              (15)

For successive leading events d ticks apart, a_v−a_u=−3d+2 and their
selected fault points are within two of a_u and a_v. Their spatial
distance is at most 3d, so d<=7 contradicts separation. The gap is at
least **8 ticks**. At the trailing end b_v−b_u=−2d−2; the distance bound
is 2d+4, which forces a gap of at least **10 ticks**. Therefore

    L_T <= ceil(T/8),        R_T <= ceil(T/10),
    a_T <= a_0 − (11/4)T + 2,
    b_T >= b_0 − (11/5)T − 2,
    b_T−a_T+1 >= w_0 − 4 + (11/20)T.                     (16)

Again the lower interval stays at least ten long and survives arbitrary
duration under its stated hypothesis, with only current noise punctures.
Its first three sites include a one, providing a leading leftward one by
a_T+2. All bounds are in the current level's space/time units and involve
no hierarchy-depth parameter.

The independent checker
[check_flag_pulses.py](proofs/check_flag_pulses.py) verifies the finite
Boolean identities, both one-update interval bounds for 857,218 local
cases, and the event-gap arithmetic. It also checks the actual generated
maintenance gates on 128 arbitrary Flag1/source assignments and 2,048
Flag2/source assignments, including colony ends, noncanonical Address
words and a nonexistent right majority. Its receipt is
[flag_pulse_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/flag_pulse_certificate.json).
The all-duration claims are the induction and separation proof above;
they do not rest on random trials or on extrapolating the checked widths.

**Still unproved:** producing pulses of the required width in faulty
colonies, maintaining their hypotheses while the two flags interact,
crossing apparent/actual boundaries, and turning these field bounds into
quantified island-edge retreat. In particular (14)'s speed is not Gray's
claimed retreat b per sixteen upper periods. That conversion also needs
the simulation, clock, pulse-delivery and newly created-colony invariants.

### Static command bits survive E0 noise on aligned geometry: proved

There is a useful extension of the healthy copy lemma that allows arbitrary
stored flags. Suppose initial Address and Age are aligned and synchronized,
and all faults are the separated singleton/adjacent-pair E0 groups just
defined. Both five-word Address votes and both Age votes then have at least
three correct inputs at every update. Whichever vote the flags select,
computed Address and Age are the clean aligned values. Inductively the
only stored geometric differences at time t are at N_t. This statement
does not require flags or other simulation fields to be healthy.

For **Address/Age alone**, even the temporal separation is unnecessary:
the same induction works for any time-dependent overwrite sets having at
most two sites in **each five-site interval at each tick**. Each of the
four whole-word votes still has three correct inputs. Before new noise,
computed Address is exactly aligned and computed Age is the common clock
advanced once, regardless of every other stored field. With such noise
forever, raw geometric deviations remain confined to the current direct
overwrite sites forever. This does not assert corresponding correction of
flags or simulation fields, nor reliability under unrestricted Bernoulli
noise. The stronger geometry-only claim is useful when reduced upper
error spacing is considered; an effective upper error map is still needed.

Fix a logical Info bit initially stored as the same bit B in its five
holders. Consider an interval during which its clean clock does not select
commit or its special signal rewrite. Under the preceding geometric
hypothesis, the raw incorrect holders of that bit at time t are a subset
of N_t union N_(t−1), with N_0=N_(−1)=empty at the initial time. In its
five-holder window, noise at those two consecutive ticks can meet at most
one E0 group: points of different groups there would have spatial distance
at most four and time distance at most one, violating (24,24) separation.
That one group changes at most two holders. The voted bit is therefore B.
The update copies B except where the raw-Address wipe fires. Since computed
Address is correct, that wipe can fire only at a site of N_t. Adding the
next direct overwrites establishes the asserted subset at t+1 and closes
the induction. Thus the voted Info bit stays B throughout the interval,
even though individual raw copies can need two ticks to heal.

In particular, correctly installed command bits at logical addresses 3 and
381 survive E0 noise throughout the 768-tick trickle window. For each output
that is not directly overwritten, the actual Workspace formulas are

    Wf1_new = right_end AND in_window AND B1,
    Wf2_new = left_end AND in_window AND B2 AND NOT(Flag1_new).   (17)

The Info vote, computed endpoints and computed clock in (17) are correct;
Flag1_new still needs its own invariant. This proof protects a command
**already installed correctly**. It does not prove that flagged mail,
the special signal procedure or damaged upper simulation installed it.

### Raised Flag1 can prevent command launch: proved counterexample

The condition NOT(Flag1_new) in (17) is Gray's condition (iv), p. 41,
and is deliberate. Gray's simultaneous-wave example on p. 42 assumes that
the lower left end is quiet when the trickle window starts, so that Flag2
launches before the incoming Flag1 wave switches off its source. The
following exact G17 example shows why that startup condition cannot be
dropped. It does **not** show that the condition fails on every trajectory
needed by the reliability induction.

Use a one-colony ring, equivalently a spatially Q-periodic configuration
on Z. Set Address(x)=x mod Q, every Age to the legal code of T_wf=13537,
every one of the five Info slots to 1, Flag1 everywhere to 1, and every
other field to zero. There is no noise. For all 2Q=768 updates of the
trickle window, both logical command bits are 1, all Workspace.Flag2 and
Flag2 bits remain zero, and no Flag2 pulse launches.

Here is the proof, independent of the experiment. Both geometric votes are
correct at every site irrespective of flags. Computed Address is unchanged,
so no simulation-field wipe fires. Neither commit nor the special signal
rewrite occurs in this window; Info remains all ones by copying. At the
first update, computed Flag1 is 1 at addresses 0,...,Q−3 and zero at the
last two addresses: these last two have fewer than two right in-colony
neighbors, and the initially zero Workspace flags supply no source.
Workspace.Flag1 becomes 1 at the last five addresses. The first five
computed Flag1 bits are all 1, so Workspace.Flag2 stays zero. At the second
update, the Workspace.Flag1 source test supplies at least three ones to
each of the last six addresses, restoring their Flag1 bits. At every other
address either at least three right Flag1 bits are still one, or at least
two are one together with the old center bit. Flag1 is therefore all ones
again. The last-five Workspace.Flag1 source then keeps it all ones for
the remainder of the window. In particular Flag1_new is never zero at
any of the first five addresses. The Workspace.Flag2 guard stays closed.
The absent-right-majority source d3 is false on aligned geometry, d4 is
zero, and initially all Flag2 bits are zero, so their update keeps zero.
This proves the claimed 768-step trajectory.

The full C and CUDA implementations agree on the final entire state.
CUDA recorded all four flags at every tick: the raised-Flag1 case has no
Flag2 or Workspace.Flag2 ones, whereas the otherwise identical quiet-Flag1
control launches Flag2 on tick two. Reproduction and receipt:
[check_flag_command.py](../figs/robustness/check_flag_command.py),
[flag_command.json](../figs/robustness/flag_command.json), and
[flag_command_state.npz](../figs/robustness/flag_command_state.npz).
This is a legal, finite exact counterexample to unconditional command
delivery, not a counterexample to memory from a pristine hierarchy.

For the repair theorem, one must prove that the left source becomes quiet
early enough in each colony whose Flag2 command is needed, or give a
different delivery argument. Increasing Q or U alone does not remove this
guard obstruction: the same construction suppresses a window of any length
while its right Flag1 source remains on. Deleting NOT(Flag1_new) would
permit Workspace.Flag2 launch in this example. That would be a **rule
change**, not implemented here; its effects on Gray's coordination and
on removal of the pulse source are unproved. It is a local remedy for this
unrestricted example, not a sufficient change for reliability.

### Intact-colony quiet startup and launch: proved conditionally

The guard obstruction does have a proved resolution in an **intact aligned
colony**. The following two lemmas assume globally aligned Address and a
common legal Age, the static-command copy hypothesis above when needed,
and only the separated E0 groups. They allow arbitrary values at the direct
overwrite sites. They are not lemmas about a partial colony or an island
with inconsistent neighboring clocks.

**Quieting lemma.** During 212 consecutive updates outside the Workspace
flag window, arbitrary initial lower Flag1 and Workspace.Flag1 values
become quiet: every computed Flag1 is zero at the last update, and every
stored Flag1 one then belongs to the current direct overwrites. The
statement holds separately in each aligned colony, regardless of the
other flags and simulation fields.

After the first update, Workspace.Flag1 is zero except at N_t. Its source
test requires three in-colony ones in an eleven-site window, so E0 supplies
no such source. Inconsistency is also false: all geometric majorities are
correct and at most two left neighbors mismatch. Treat Flag1 beyond this
colony's right boundary as zero, as the inside masks actually do. Writing
z=NOT(Flag1), the source-free update is the monotone rule

    z_new = [at least four of z(x+1),...,z(x+5) are 1]
            OR [z(x)=1 AND at least three are 1].                 (18)

The virtual half-line [Q,infinity) of zeros in Flag1 supplies ones in z.
If z is one from a to the right boundary except at current N_t, it is one
before the next overwrites from

    a_new = a−2+2 I,  I=1 if N_t meets [a,a+3].                 (19)

An old good zero of Flag1 has at least three good right zeros even if two
are overwritten. At an overwritten center there is at most one other
fault in its five right neighbors, leaving four good zeros and healing
it. If the first four zeros are good, the two preceding sites acquire
four and five right zeros. Otherwise omit those two sites. This proves
(19); the virtual boundary has no faults and is included in the argument.
Successive affecting events d ticks apart have frontier displacement
−2d+2 and selected fault points within three of those frontiers. Their
distance is at most 2d+1. Separation therefore forces d>=12. After T
erasure updates,

    a_T <= Q−2T+2 ceil(T/12).                                (20)

For Q=384, T=210 gives a_T<=0. Include the initial Workspace reset and
one next update to make the **computed** flag quiet, giving 212 updates.
Once quiet, E0 alone cannot restart Flag1: two right faults cannot satisfy
the three-bit threshold, and a faulty center has at most one other nearby
fault and cannot satisfy its two-right-bit persistence test. The intact
source-free interval is 19968 ticks, comfortably longer than 212. This
proves quiet startup in this restricted geometry, not in Gray's damaged
partial hierarchy.

**Launch lemma.** Start the trickle window at Age 13537 with aligned
Address/Age, correctly installed static B1=B2=1 command bits, and all
lower Flag1 and Workspace.Flag1 bits zero. Other flags may be arbitrary.
At update 140 every computed Flag1 in the colony is one and the stored
Flag2 field is one on [177,255], except current direct overwrites. In
particular there is a 79-site lower interval, enough to start (14) wherever
its continuing computed-Flag1 hypothesis holds. The same proof allows
current E0 punctures in the initial quiet fields and command copies.

Workspace.Flag1 is on the last five addresses after each window update,
except N_t. Thus its source forces computed Flag1 on the last six
addresses from update two onward. At an output farther left than Q−10
there is no ideal Workspace.Flag1 in its eleven-site input neighborhood;
the two direct faults alone cannot meet the three-bit source threshold.
Elsewhere an already propagating Flag1 can move at most five sites left
per tick. More formally, stored Flag1 outside
[Q−10−5(t−2),Q−1] is zero except N_t for t>=2, by induction. Outside that
cone the right and center thresholds also cannot be met solely by one E0
group. Therefore the first five computed Flag1 bits stay zero through
update 64. Formula (17) consequently supplies all five Workspace.Flag2
source bits there, except current overwrites, through update 64. Their
three-bit source test forces Flag2 on the first six addresses from updates
two through 65.

For the rest of the calculation a useful lower rule is

    T20(s)(x) = [at least four left in-colony bits are 1]
                 OR [s(x)=1 AND at least two are 1].            (21)

Candidate B dominates this rule for either computed Flag1 value: when
Flag1 is zero this is its source-free predicate, and when one it admits
more left inputs and needs only one for persistence. Values outside the
colony are treated as zero in (21). With a persistent first-six source,
an interval [0,b], b>=5, becomes [0,b+2−2 I_R] before noise, with I_R as
in (11). Right-affecting events are at least eleven ticks apart by the
same distance calculation as (14). From update two to 65 there are 63
steps, giving b>=5+126−2 ceil(63/11)=119. All of [0,119] is therefore one
except N_65.

At the other end, the persistent last-six Flag1 source supports a lower
interval ending at Q−1. Its leading endpoint obeys (12)'s left recurrence
even when its initial length is only six; the source covers the last six
sites where an unanchored interval would otherwise lose trailing bits.
Leading events are at least eight ticks apart, giving
a<=378−3T+2 ceil(T/8). At T=138 this is zero. Hence every computed Flag1
is one by update 140, and remains one throughout the remaining window.
Only current direct overwrites puncture the stored field.

Between updates 65 and 140 we can discard the Flag2 source entirely.
For (21) an interval [a,b] becomes at least

    [a+2+3 I_L, b+2−2 I_R],                                (22)

where I_L detects a fault in [a,a+3]. With no such fault the first two
good left inputs keep the leading old one; an overwritten point at a+4
has four good left inputs. If there is an edge fault, start at a+5,
where all five left inputs lie in the interval. The old-center and right
edge arguments are otherwise exactly those above. Successive left events
have displacement 2d+3 and fault-distance at most 2d+6, forcing d>=9;
right events still have gap at least eleven. Over these 75 updates,
a<=150+3 ceil(75/9)=177 and
b>=119+150−2 ceil(75/11)=255. Its nominal length stays at least
120−3 ceil(T/9)−2 ceil(T/11)>=79 for 0<=T<=75, so every step's local
interval argument has the required room. The interval stays inside the
colony. This proves the launch bound without assuming a favorable noise
pattern or extrapolating a wave measurement.

[check_flag_startup.py](proofs/check_flag_startup.py) checks the actual
Flag1 gates at all six right-boundary geometries, the Boolean dual (18),
the four interval-step predicates, event-gap arithmetic and G17 bounds.
Its receipt is
[flag_startup_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/flag_startup_certificate.json).
The universal time and width claims rest on the preceding inductions.
Correct command installation, synchronization through damaged colonies,
and propagation beyond the domain where computed Flag1 stays one are
still **unproved**. Thus this resolves the startup counterexample only
under explicit intact-colony hypotheses, not P9 or the final theorem.

### Source-free Flag2 clearing on aligned geometry: proved conditionally

Assume aligned canonical Address/common Age except current E0 overwrites,
computed Flag1=0 at every update, and computed D3=D4=0. These are explicit
hypotheses; they hold in the source-free part of (5b), not on arbitrary
damaged geometry. All initial Flag2 bits can be arbitrary. Then within
**212 updates** every computed Flag2 is zero and its stored ones belong
only to current N_t. It stays quiet as long as the hypotheses hold.

Within each colony the actual update is (21), since the right Address
vote is canonical and the inside mask omits the other colonies. Its first
two sites have at most one left in-colony input, so both computed Flag2
bits are zero on the first update. Thereafter retain a zero prefix [0,B]
except N_t. Treat negative sites as a virtual zero extension, exactly as
the mask does. Put r=|N_t intersect [B−4,B]|, so 0<=r<=2. Then

    B_new = min(Q−1,B+2−r).                                 (24a)

Every old zero in the prefix stays zero: four left ones are impossible;
an overwritten center has at most one other faulty left input and cannot
satisfy the two-left persistence test. At B+1 there are at most r left
ones; at B+2 there are at most r+1. Thus r=0 allows both advances, r=1
allows the first, and r=2 allows neither. No temporary halo is needed.
New overwrites give the same punctured-prefix invariant. This proof is
monotone in the arbitrary right Flag2 inputs, so setting them all to one
is the worst case, not an assumption about the island.

For consecutive affecting groups d ticks apart, before the frontier
reaches the last site its displacement is `2d−r_u`, with r_u=1 or 2.
Selected fault points lie within four sites to the left of their frontiers.
For d<=10 their distance is at most `2d+3 <= 23`; E0 separation forbids
this. Affecting events therefore have gap at least eleven, and after T
updates beyond the initial reset,

    B_T >= min(Q−1,1+2T−2 ceil(T/11)).

At T=211 the expression is 383. Including the initial update gives 212.
Once the prefix is the entire colony, the same center/left-input argument
prevents E0 alone from creating an indirect Flag2 one. ∎

[check_flag2_quiet.py](proofs/check_flag2_quiet.py) verifies 512 actual
maintenance-gate assignments including both colony ends, 38,657 local
prefix outputs and 500 event-packing cases. Its receipt is
[flag2_quiet_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/flag2_quiet_certificate.json).
The erasure speed 20/11 and 212-update reserve are conditional field
bounds, not an island-retreat theorem or minimum constants. Combining
them with the earlier Flag1 quieting gives the 424-update source-free
reserve used in (5b).

### A no-majority source cone: proved; a fixed-site period is false

The periodic local Flag2 source in the actual rule is

    D3 = NOT(right Address majority exists)
         AND (low four bits of selected left Age are 1111).

It forces computed Flag2 one regardless of its old value. The actual h
increments the low four Age bits modulo sixteen on **every** raw word,
including unused words: both packed position moduli 288 and 512 are
divisible by sixteen. Nevertheless a voted Age need not advance at a
fixed site, so this formula is not a sixteen-tick local timer.

Here is an exact **conditional source lemma**. For an endpoint (x,t+16),
let C contain output coordinates
`(y,t+s)`, 1<=s<=16, `x−5(16−s)<=y<=x`. Suppose there are no errors at
these coordinates, and for each of their updates the computed right
Address vote has no whole-word majority. Then at some coordinate of C,
D3 is true and stored Flag2 is one. Other initial fields may be arbitrary.

Trace the endpoint's Age backward for sixteen updates. With no right
Address majority, the selected Age is always one of the five left input
words or the holder default. Thus its producer positions stay in C,
moving left at most five sites per backward step. With no overwrites on
the path, the sixteen output low-four-bit values go successively through
all sixteen residues, so one output has residue zero. At its producer
the selected input has residue fifteen; the absent right Address
majority makes D3 true. Its Flag2 output is one and is not overwritten.
This proves the lemma. The cone has a maximum row width of 76 sites and
spatial span 75. It proves source occurrence somewhere in a cone, **not**
a four-site packet, a moving pulse, or a per-site repetition rate.

For the failed per-site version, take on Z a constant raw Address 500 and
legal Age `age_code(floor(x/3) mod U)`. The five adjusted Addresses on
either side are distinct, so both Address votes default to the holder;
Address stays 500, the right majority never exists, and computed Flag1
is always one. Every left five-site Age window has three copies of the
previous staircase word and at most two of other words. Its majority
is `age_code(floor(x/3)−1 mod U)`, so applying h leaves the Age staircase
**stationary at every site**. These conclusions ignore all other fields.

Start Flag2 at zero. D3 is true exactly on the three-site patches where
`floor(x/3)=0 mod 16`, spaced 48 sites apart. After one update these are
exactly the Flag2-one sites, forever: no five-site left window contains
four ones, the right Address vote's absent `inside` mask disables the
Workspace source, and D3 retains each patch. In particular site x=3 has
no local D3 and Flag2 zero for all time despite permanently absent right
Address majority. This is a malformed infinite configuration, **not** an
initial pristine hierarchy or a counterexample to the memory target.
It rules out using an unrestricted sixteen-tick source or pulse assertion
in place of the missing island/clock invariant. Gray's intended island
argument needs its additional hypotheses proved for G17.

[check_flag2_sources.py](proofs/check_flag2_sources.py) checks the actual
increment's four-bit identity on all 65,536 words and reproduces the
stationary staircase on its complete 62,208-site spatial period for
64 updates. Completed C and CUDA agree on the entire final state;
[flag2_source_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/flag2_source_certificate.json)
and [saved states](../figs/robustness/flag2_source_staircase.npz) record this
finite support. The unbounded statements above follow from the explicit
votes, source predicate and ancestry proof. The source-cone lemma through
mixed E0, sufficiently wide launched pulses, and island retreat are still
**unproved**. Comparing λ=24 with sixteen alone does not establish them.

### Synchronized sources from a protected clock strip: proved conditionally

Gray p. 40 assumes relatively aligned full cells with common Age near the
right end of an island. This is a substantially stronger condition than
permanently missing right Address votes. The following gives explicit
sufficient reserves for its clock part, without assuming any legality of
the other fields or of the initial Age word.

Let I=[a,b] have initially one common raw Age alpha. Its rightmost three
sites must have **no computed right Address majority at every update**
under consideration. All other fields and both exterior regions may be
arbitrary. Permit E0 overwrites of singleton/adjacent-pair groups mutually
(24,24)-separated. Then:

* with width at least **57**, within sixteen updates all three rightmost
  sites simultaneously have computed D3=1 and computed Flag2=1; at least
  one of these three stored Flag2 bits is one after the current overwrites;
* with width at least **111**, within thirty-two updates all three stored
  Flag2 bits are simultaneously one at a source update;
* without E0, width **51** already suffices for the three stored source
  bits within sixteen updates.

These are **conditional clock/source lemmas**, not conclusions that a
damaged simulated island has such a strip or that the three bits launch
a lower repair pulse. Widths count cells at the level where F is being
applied; a transfer to simulated cells requires the still-unproved
damaged-trajectory simulation lemma.

Here is the proof with E0. At time t retain a common-clock interval
`[a_t,b]`, with expected word `h^t(alpha)`, except for current overwrite
sites N_t and an optional set M_t contained in `{b−4,b−3}`. Initially M_0
is empty. A nonempty M_t can occur only from the preceding update's E0
group intersecting `[b−3,b]`. In particular no current E0 group can be
near M_t: its previous causing group lies in `[b−4,b+1]`, and groups less
than 24 ticks apart must be at least 24 sites apart.

Assume `a_t<=b−7` and put `r_t=|N_t intersect [a_t,a_t+3]|`. Before new
overwrites the next common-clock interval begins at

    a_(t+1) = a_t+3+r_t.                                    (23)

For x between this new endpoint and b−5, its right Age window lies entirely
in the old interval; its left vote obeys the same three-bad-input frontier
bound as (G2). The old M pair can affect a right vote, but at most two
inputs. A current E0 group cannot add a third near this pair because of
its causing group's isolation. The left windows of these x do not meet M.
Thus both Age votes agree with the common word.

At b−2,b−1,b the absent right Address majority forces the left Age vote.
Their five left inputs are in the old interval. They contain at most the
M pair or at most two current overwrite sites, and cannot contain both;
the whole-word majority therefore agrees with the common word. At b−4,
b−3 a right vote can fail only if the current group intersects `[b−3,b]`:
without that group it still has at least three common inputs. The left
vote there has at least three common inputs when `a_t<=b−7` and no nearby
current group. These two sites can therefore become M_(t+1), but only
from that current group. If M_t was nonempty, all votes at these two sites
are again common and M_(t+1) is empty. This proves the stated invariant.
The newly overwritten sites N_(t+1) stay separate.

Equation (23) has the same separated-group packing as (G3), with exterior
offsets 0,...,3 rather than 1,...,4. For T>0,

    a_T−a_0 <= 3T + 2[1+floor(3T/23)].                      (24)

For T=15 this is 49; width 57 leaves eight common-clock sites before the
sixteenth update, as required. For T=31 it is 103; width 111 leaves the
same eight sites. Consequently all three rightmost selected left Age
words equal `h^t(alpha)` at every update through the stated duration.
Their low four bits traverse all sixteen residues together. D3 and the
computed Flag2 bits of these three cells are therefore one simultaneously
at some update s<=16, and again at s+16 if thirty-two updates are available.
At a source update an E0 group can overwrite at most two of the three
sites, proving the first stored-one bound. It cannot hit the three-site
target at both s and s+16: those groups would be linked in both coordinates,
violating E0 separation. One of the two source updates is wholly clean,
proving the width-111 statement. Without E0 there is no M and the frontier
advances only three sites per update; width 51 leaves six common-clock
sites before update sixteen, enough for all three left majorities. ∎

[check_clock_strip.py](proofs/check_clock_strip.py) checks the local
infection cases, including the boundary pair and its isolated predecessor,
and the reserve arithmetic; its receipt is
[clock_strip_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/clock_strip_certificate.json).
Whole-word majority dominance and the actual increment are certified in
§§6–7. The universal claims above use the interval induction and packing,
not a sampled simulation. No assertion is made that 51,57,111 are minimum
reserves. In particular this does not complete Gray's three-cell reversal:
the existence of the clock strip through faulty simulations, continuing
absence of right votes, command provenance, partial-cell handoff and the
quantified island retreat remain **unproved**.

### The remaining multilevel argument

Gray pp. 38–43 explicitly omits coordination details and the control of
new colonies. He claims an envelope U^k/16 in Proposition 5. The facts
needed to establish it for this rule and these constants are not stated
as a proved lemma elsewhere in the repository. The deterministic glider
and single shifted-island measurements are much narrower than this claim.
Repeated lower errors on the right of a larger island are precisely the
case for which his Flag2 mechanism is necessary; those cases are not
covered by running one isolated block through one trickle-down.

The supplied Gács paper is the **24 January 2024 corrected and strengthened
printing of the 2001 journal article**, as stated on its first page (also
available from the [author](https://cs-web.bu.edu/faculty/gacs/papers/long-ca-ms-24.pdf)).
Its section numbers should not be identified with the original version's.
It uses a different, rigorously specified mechanism: robust media,
their computation and conditional restoration properties, a damage map,
error-correcting codes, and an amplifier. In the supplied version the
simulation damage probability bound is **Lemma 10.5**, pp. 99–100
(Gray refers to Lemma 8.4 of the version he read). It assumes simulations
with the Restoration Property, Condition 10.4, and the damage map of
Definition 10.3. It proves a probability implication under those assumptions;
it does not prove this rule has them. The amplifier Lemma 11.7, p. 112,
uses the parameter and program conditions of §11; its displayed example
has Q_k = R^(k+1), growing capacities and work periods. G17's fixed-Q
five-copy code, fixed ROM and candidate-B maintenance have no verified
identification with those media, programs, or restoration conditions.

Those proofs may guide a new construction or new verification, but citing
their conclusions cannot close P5b–P10. The additional self-organization
and arbitrary payload memory of Gács are not properties established for G17.

## 11. The final probabilistic step, if a repair lemma is supplied

The missing implication can be formulated without claiming independent
noise at upper levels. Here is one sufficient deterministic statement, **R**:

> For the specified pristine initial hierarchy and every replacement of an
> error set having the §3 decomposition, every wrong physical Address at
> (x,t) is either a direct error there or is associated with a real level-n
> set S, n >= 1, containing an original error q at coordinate distances at
> most 10Q^n and 10U^n from (x,t). The statement holds uniformly in depth
> and for the infinite error set, with all intervening flagged, partial and
> misaligned states handled by its proof.

The constant 10 is a sufficient allowance for this conditional theorem,
not a measured or proved bound on G17's damage. A complete proof of R
could use more detailed simulation and flag envelopes; it cannot be
replaced by assuming that the upper errors are independent.

**Conditional theorem — proved.** If R holds for unchanged G17, the target
of §1 holds, for example with

    ε* = 1/(2 C H) = 1/51,741,130,752 ≈ 1.9326983880e-11.

Proof: by §3, q has a depth-n witness leaf within 26 units at scale n-1.
That leaf is within 11Q^n, 11U^n of (x,t). At most C H^n possible leaves
lie there. Apply (1), union over levels, and add the direct error event:

    Pr{wrong Address at (x,t)}
       <= ε + (1/H) Σ_(n>=1) (C H ε)^(2^n)
       <= ε + (C H ε)^2 / [H (1-(C H ε)^2)].

For ε <= ε*, this is at most ε*+1/(3H) < 4.2e-8 < 1/4, independently
of x,t and the replacement distribution. This also proves the bit statement
by the observable in §1. The sum converges, and §4 guarantees finite levels
almost surely. Nothing else is required in this probabilistic step.

**R is unproved.** This conditional result supplies an explicit finishing
calculation; its number must not be advertised as a noise threshold for the
implemented rule. A proof of R for finite isolated tests alone would also
need a uniform finite-depth/infinite-volume extension. Local causality of F
allows finite-cone reasoning at fixed times, but the hierarchy and error
classification need uniform bounds before taking that limit.

### A phase-only repair envelope also suffices: proved reduction

One may weaken the missing deterministic envelope from wrong raw Address
to wrong **Address phase**. Define **R_theta** exactly as R, replacing
its wrong-Address condition by `(x−Address_t(x)) mod Q != b`, for the
initial state xi_b. Retain every other quantifier, original-error
association and distance constant in R. This is a potentially simpler
repair obligation: phase-correct unused aliases need not be assigned a
higher-error envelope. **R_theta remains unproved for G17.**

For the bit observable alone, R_theta gives the same conditional bound
as R. A correct phase implies correct Address parity, since Q is even,
including a noncanonical Address alias. There is also a reduction to the
stronger raw-Address target of §1, using the 43-update normalization proved
in §7. In particular, R_theta suffices for that target at the same
conditional epsilon*, with a slightly larger probability bound.

**Localized normalization — proved.** Fix t>=43 and put s=t−43. If every
Address at time s within distance 215 of x has correct phase, and there
are no overwrites in the subsequent radius-five backward cone of (x,t),
then Address_t(x) is canonical. To prove this, extend the entire state
on that initial interval arbitrarily to Z, choosing correct-phase
Addresses outside it too. Evolve it without overwrites for 43 updates.
The global phase-normalization theorem makes its Address at (x,t)
canonical; radius-five causality makes this value identical to the actual
one. Other initial fields are unrestricted in both arguments. For t<43,
canonical initial Addresses and absence of errors in the initial-to-t
cone already imply a canonical Address by the vote invariant.

Consequently, an incorrect raw Address at (x,t) either has an original
overwrite in the last 44 layers of its backward cone (including the
cut layer s when s>=1), or there is a wrong-phase site at time s within
215 sites of x which is not a direct overwrite. The first event has at
most

    M_44 = sum(j=0,...,43)(10j+1) = **9504**

possible error locations. Including a nonexistent time-zero overwrite
only enlarges this count. In the second event, R_theta gives an associated
real level-n error, n>=1. Its original error q is within 10Q^n+215 sites
and 10U^n+43 ticks of (x,t). The witness leaf in §3 adds at most
26Q^(n−1), 26U^(n−1). Since

    215+26Q^(n−1) <= Q^n,
     43+26U^(n−1) <= U^n,

all these leaves, across the whole cut interval, fit in the same
11Q^n by 11U^n distance allowance used above. Thus their union costs
at most C H^n possible leaves, without an additional factor of 431.
Applying (1) and the union bound proves

    Pr{wrong raw Address at (x,t)}
       <= 9504 epsilon + (1/H) sum_(n>=1)(C H epsilon)^(2^n).

At epsilon<=epsilon* this is at most

    9504 epsilon* + 1/(3H)
       = 11670/51,741,130,752 < 2.3e-7 < 1/4.

This proves the target **conditionally on R_theta**, uniformly at every
site and time. It does not prove a phase-repair lemma, an unconditional
noise threshold, or any independence of effective upper errors. The
finite cone count and fraction are checked in the validation receipt;
the reduction rests on the normalization theorem and causality, not on
an experiment.

## 12. Changes: what can and cannot presently be certified

There is no proved smallest modification making the full proof go through.
There is not even a certified sufficient modification of this implementation
in the repository. The obstacles above include missing lemmas, a changed
local predicate, and different simulation procedures, so they are not solved
by optimizing a single inequality. It is possible that G17 already satisfies
a suitable R; no change has been proved necessary for the target theorem.

The following limited conclusions about proposed changes **are** justified:

| Proposal | What it accomplishes | What remains |
|---|---|---|
| Guard out-of-range ROM reads with I=0 | Makes the executables implement the unique total Boolean output completion proved in §6 | Required for whole-state noise execution; establishes no repair or memory theorem |
| Keep G17 and extend the proved healthy invariants to P5b–P10 | Could establish R without any rule change | Damaged-trajectory simulation and recovery remain unproved; measurements cannot replace them |
| Add the range-guarded quiet-pair Flag1 diagnostic specified below | Repairs joint quiet ancestry below Address Q−5 and extends (Q3) to both geometry fields without prior Address alignment | Explicit proposed rule change; no recompiled self-interpreter or noisy island/all-level proof exists |
| Validate three joint right pairs and observe eight right Flag1 bits, as specified below | Preserves healthy structural two-fault correction and gives a conditional surviving Flag1 packet whose leading speed exceeds the quiet ancestry bound | Explicit radius-eight maintenance proposal; initialization, inside masks, noise restarts, larger-neighborhood gathers and the complete reliability proof remain unproved |
| Lower c further | Shrinks geometric boxes; §3 remains valid | Does not repair Gray's Q inequality at λ=24; does not establish any dynamical lemma |
| Increase U alone | Can add recovery intervals and fit deadlines after recompilation | Does not resolve the whole-colony island obstruction or Flag2 variant |
| Increase Q until Gray's island-size estimate holds | Removes that particular failed spatial estimate | Requires a new pinned-program certificate and still does not settle damaged copies, erasure rule, or higher-level induction |
| Restore c=104, Q>=8192, U=128Q | Restores Gray's printed size parameters | Still a different ROM/schedule/rule unless redesigned and verified; Gray's omitted details remain obligations |
| Change erasure/wipes or adopt Gács's actual medium | Changes proof hypotheses and may allow another verification | A rule change, with new constants and candidate identity; no such change was performed |

### A local joint-ancestry diagnostic: proposed rule change, with a proved local effect

**This is a proposed change to the transition rule. It is not active G17,
and no core source, stored ROM or candidate was modified.** Its purpose is
to close the specific independent-vote obstruction in §7. A complete
construction and an all-time positive-noise proof for it remain **unproved**.
