Keep the existing separately computed right Address and Age votes v and
beta. Let f1_old be the original provisional Flag1 output, before it is
used by the Flag2 and geometry-selection formulas. Define

    K = OR_(j=1,...,5) [adjusted_Address(j)=v
                       AND Age(j)=beta AND stored_Flag1(j)=0],
    f1_new = f1_old OR [(v < Q−5) AND NOT K].                (J1)

Use this strengthened f1_new in **every subsequent use** of computed
Flag1, including Flag2 erasure/setting, geometry selection, raw-Address
wipes and the Workspace.Flag2 guard. The later formulas are otherwise
the same. This needs no new state bits or wider radius. It is different
from silently changing the output Flag1 after computing the other fields.

**Joint quiet ancestry — proved for (J1), below Address Q−5.** A
non-overwritten quiet output with Address a<=Q−6 has f1_old=0, so both
right whole-word majorities exist and the Address/Age pair is selected
from the right, with v=a. The range guard is therefore on, and quietness
implies K=1. Choose the corresponding quiet right neighbor; it supports
**both** selected votes. Its raw Address is exactly a+j by the actual inverse
identity in (Q1), and its Age is beta. If the output geometry is wrong,
this ancestor geometry is wrong: Address phase is preserved along the
step, and a wrong output Age cannot be h of the reference preceding Age.
This holds for arbitrary flags, unused clock words and mixed right inputs.
Iterating therefore gives the same terminal alternatives and distance
bounds as (Q1)–(Q2), now for the **combined geometry**, without a prior
global Address-alignment assumption.

**Local minimality — proved within a specified class.** Restrict attention
to changes which keep the votes and the Flag1-controlled selector, and
only enlarge the Flag1=1 predicate. On every input with f1_old=0 and K=0,
and with v<Q−5, a quiet output would select a pair having no quiet joint
right supporter. Every such change guaranteeing joint quiet ancestry
**below Q−5** must therefore raise Flag1 on that input. On inputs with
K=1 the inference already holds; on inputs with f1_old=1 there is no
quiet output to repair; v>=Q−5 is outside the specified inference.
Equation (J1) raises Flag1 exactly on the necessary extra inputs. Thus it is the
pointwise least **strengthened Flag1 output** in this restricted class.
This is not a smallest rule change sufficient for reliability; it is a
minimal local fix for this one inference. Keeping G17 and using a different
proof is still an available possibility.

**Agreement on a joint majority — proved for (J1).** Whenever three
right neighbors agree on the selected adjusted Address and raw Age,
the original and proposed maintenance outputs are identical, with
arbitrary left data and arbitrary flags everywhere. If v>=Q−5, the
extra source is off. If v<Q−5 and f1_old=0, all five right cells are
inside; the original Flag1 test implies at least three of them have
stored Flag1 zero. This set intersects the three joint supporters,
giving K=1. If f1_old=1, strengthening does not change the bit. Hence
f1_new=f1_old in every case, and all subsequent formulas are identical.
In particular, the proved aligned-geometry E0 maintenance, source-free
flag quieting and command startup bounds survive this local change.
This does not yet certify a self-interpreting program for the changed rule.

**Why the range guard is necessary for this design.** The rejected
ungated source NOT K would keep Flag1 one forever on globally aligned
geometry with all stored Flag1 bits one, Workspace.Flag1 zero and common
Age. Then K is zero everywhere, even at the colony's last two sites
where the original rule clears Flag1 and starts its quieting front.
The ungated strengthening raises it again at those sites. Geometry
stays aligned, so this is an invariant obstruction to the quieting
argument. Equation (J1) avoids it by the agreement result above. This is
an obstruction to a rejected hypothetical variant, not a defect in G17.

**Pristine two-fault structural correction — proved for (J1).** Three of
the five right cells retain both correct words and Flag1=0 after at most
two overwritten cells in an eleven-site neighborhood. They supply the
original correct votes and K=1. Hence the extra source is off, and the
original zero-flag/correct-geometry argument in (7) applies to maintenance.
The geometry-only aligned induction likewise survives arbitrary flags:
both directional votes still agree when they have three correct inputs.

**Noise-free combined window — proved conditionally for (J1).** Start
with all Address/Age differences confined to a width-w interval, and
otherwise aligned canonical Address/common reference Age. Other fields
can be arbitrary; there are no subsequent overwrites. Outside the usual
three-site-per-edge growth envelope, both directions have three correct
whole pairs, so the new diagnostic cannot create geometric errors there.
The joint quiet ancestry above keeps a wrong geometry pair wrong along
its path. The same proof of (Q3) therefore excludes quiet wrong geometry
with output Address in 0,...,4 at x>=a_0 for times
`w,...,floor((600−w)/3)`, w<=150. In particular width 141 gives 141,...,153
at Q=384 for **both** fields together. Mixed E0 may terminate the path,
and Flag2 may select a wrong pair while Flag1 is one; neither is repaired
merely by this window.

[check_joint_diagnostic.py](proofs/check_joint_diagnostic.py) generates a
clearly labeled in-memory copy of `maintenance.build` with exactly (J1).
It evaluates all 4,096 majority/quiet-support mask triples, detecting the
270 empty-intersection cases, and proves literal constant outputs for
1,210 two-arbitrary-fault symbolic cases. Another 1,920 symbolic cases
have identical output node IDs for the original and proposed formulas
on three joint right supporters, leaving the other data and flags free;
the text above supplies the universal agreement proof. The rejected
ungated variant is checked at all 384 aligned Addresses. These are
local Boolean certificates. The modified maintenance net has 2,751 gates versus 2,479
for the original when the same maintenance outputs are retained: **272
additional maintenance gates**. This does not establish the size or
schedule of a complete self-interpreting candidate. The receipt is
[joint_diagnostic_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/joint_diagnostic_certificate.json).

To make an actual alternative CA, its netlist must be rebuilt and its
**own changed rule** compiled into a new ROM, followed by new program,
copy/transport, timing and restoration certificates. Leaving the G17 ROM
in place would simulate the old rule. No claim is made that the changed
program fits the same U or that Q=384 is sufficient for all noisy recovery.
The remaining mixed-E0 escape, Flag2/D4 provenance, local footprints,
partial-colony simulation and higher-level coordination obligations are
unchanged as proof obligations. This proposal supplies a concrete local
design option toward smaller constants, not the requested complete new
construction.

### Faster Flag1 with a validated right pair: proposed maintenance design

**This is a separate proposed rule change, not G17 and not an implemented
self-simulating candidate.** It combines a stronger right-pair check with
a faster flag signal. It has a quantitative local advantage for the
structural-repair problem, but no sufficient Q/U or positive noise rate
is proved for a complete construction using it.

Keep the independent right Address and Age votes v and beta, the five
left/right geometric voters, the eleven-site Workspace tests, and the
candidate-B Flag2 predicates. Add the source

    P = [at least three j in 1,...,5 have
         adjusted_Address(j)=v AND Age(j)=beta].

Extend the right Flag1 observation from j=1,...,5 to j=1,...,8, using
`inside(j)=exists_right_Address AND (v+j<Q)` for the three extra positive
offsets too. The strengthened provisional Flag1 is

    f1_new = inconsistency OR Workspace_Flag1_source OR NOT P
             OR threshold_3(inside(j) AND Flag1(j), j=1,...,8)
             OR [Flag1(0) AND
                 threshold_2(inside(j) AND Flag1(j), j=1,...,8)].    (J2)

Use it in all subsequent Flag2, selection, wipe and Workspace guard
formulas, as with (J1). Only the three farther Flag1 bits are additional
maintenance inputs; no Address/Age bits at those offsets are read. The
local module needs no new stored state bits, but its radius is now eight.
The state/transport resources of a complete self-interpreter are not
determined by that local observation count.

**Healthy structural correction — proved for (J2).** With aligned
canonical Address, common raw Age alpha, zero flags/Workspace bits,
and at most two arbitrary faults in the fourteen-site used neighborhood
[-5,8], three correct joint pairs remain among the five right voters.
They give both correct votes and P=1. The original inconsistency and
Workspace sources are zero, and at most two counted right Flag1 bits
are one. If the faulty center is one, two faulty right bits would require
three faults, so persistence cannot fire. Thus computed Flag1 is zero,
computed geometry is correct, and the original Flag2 correction argument
gives zero too. This covers every raw overwritten word and every common
Age word. It is maintenance correction, not a claim that an unbuilt
self-interpreting program has full-field one-tick correction.

The added pair source is also off whenever three right cells jointly
support the selected words, with arbitrary other geometry and all flags.
This is agreement between the radius-eight formula with and without
pair validation; extending the flag window does change the original
radius-five formula. On the §7 independent-vote counterexample, P is
false because only one right cell supports the voted pair. Equation (J2)
raises Flag1 and selects the correct left geometry when Flag2 is zero.
It does not use the rejected ungated quiet-neighbor source of (J1).

**Joint quiet ancestry — proved for (J2).** A non-overwritten quiet
output with raw Address a<=Q−6 selects the two right votes and has P=1.
Its first five right neighbors are inside; at most two of their Flag1
bits are one, since three would set (J2). Three joint supporters and at
least three quiet right neighbors intersect. Their common cell supplies
both voted words, has Flag1 zero, and has raw Address exactly a+j,
j=1,...,5, by (Q1)'s modular inverse identity. A wrong geometry pair
has a wrong ancestor pair, without prior global Address alignment.
All terminal alternatives in (Q2) still apply: in particular an overwrite
or an apparent-right-boundary ancestor can terminate the path.

**Fast surviving packets — proved conditionally for (J2).** Suppose a
nominal Flag1-one interval [a,b] has length at least five, except for
current E0 overwrite sites N_t; extra ones elsewhere are allowed. Require
all **eight** right samples inside at each output to be protected. There
its flag output is at least

    T8(s)(x) = threshold_3(s(x+1),...,s(x+8))
               OR [s(x) AND threshold_2(s(x+1),...,s(x+8))].

All other sources are nonnegative. Put J_L=1 when N_t meets [a,a+2],
and J_R=1 when it meets [b−2,b]. Before the next overwrites, ones cover

    [a−6+2 J_L, b−2−2 J_R].                               (J3)

For the left edge, if J_L=0 the first three good inputs establish a−6,
a−5 and a−4. If J_L=1, a−4 sees five old packet sites, of which at
least three are good. This also covers the intervening new sites. In
the old bulk through b−4, a good center has at least two good right
inputs; a faulty center has at most one other faulty right input, leaving
at least three good ones to restore it. If J_R=0 the last three good
sites establish the old trailing outputs through b−2. Otherwise cap
them at b−4. These arguments use at most two faults in any local window;
many separated groups in a long packet are allowed. The new nominal
length is at least the old length: its change is
`4−2 J_L−2 J_R>=0`. Width five therefore suffices for every iteration.

Let a_t,b_t iterate (J3). Consecutive leading events d ticks apart have
`a_v−a_u=−6d+2`; their chosen fault points lie at offsets 0,...,2 from
those ends. Their spatial distance is at most 6d. For d<4 both that
distance and the time gap are below 24, contradicting separation. Thus
leading events are at least four ticks apart. Consecutive trailing events
have `b_v−b_u=−2d−2`; offsets in −2,...,0 give distance at most 2d+4,
so their gap is at least ten. Consequently, for every duration T,

    a_T <= a_0−6T+2 ceil(T/4) <= a_0−(11/2)T+2,
    b_T >= b_0−2T−2 ceil(T/10) >= b_0−(11/5)T−2,
    b_T−a_T+1 >= w_0+(33/10)T−4.                          (J4)

The packet is one on its nominal interval except current direct
overwrites; its actual first guaranteed one can be at a_T+2. The lower
interval proof, including its nondecreasing width, gives the all-duration
conclusion. This does not assume an actual damaged colony initializes
the packet or maintains the eight-sample inside hypothesis.

**Interception of an uninterrupted quiet path — proved conditionally.**
Suppose such a packet starts at [a_0,b_0], and a quiet path starts at
x_0<a_0 and moves left by one to five sites each update. None of its
nodes is a direct overwrite, and the packet hypotheses hold throughout.
The path cannot survive to `T=2(a_0−x_0)+4`. Indeed it must stay left
of a_t: at a first crossing, its preceding position is <=a_(t−1)−1,
so its new position is <=a_(t−1)−2. Since nominal width is at least
five and b_t>=b_(t−1)−4, this is also <=b_t. It would be a non-overwritten
one in the packet, contradicting quietness. But (J4) and its at-most-five
motion give

    x_T−a_T >= −(a_0−x_0)+(1/2)T−2 >= 0,

the other contradiction. Joint quiet ancestry produces paths with those
steps until its terminal alternatives occur. Noise restarts and the
near-right-boundary alternative are not removed by this comparison.

For context, the corresponding leading-edge estimate with r right
Flag1 samples and threshold three is
`(r−2)−2/ceil(24/(r−2))`, provided the interval recurrence is valid.
It gives 2.75, 11/3, 4.6 and 5.5 for r=5,6,7,8. Eight is the smallest
of these windows whose **estimate** exceeds the ancestry bound five.
This is not a minimum radius or modification for a reliability theorem.

**Source-free quieting — proved conditionally for (J2).** On aligned
canonical geometry/common Age amid E0, suppose the computed Flag1
source is zero throughout. Arbitrary initial Flag1 clears within **216
updates**. The last two cells of each true colony have at most one
counted right neighbor and clear in the first update. A zero suffix
[L,Q−1], except N_t, stays zero before new noise: two right fault bits
cannot set three, and a faulty center cannot also have two right faults.
If no fault meets [L−1,L+7], it advances two sites to the left. Otherwise
conservatively freeze L for that update. Thus

    L_(t+1)=L_t−2+2 I_t,
    I_t=[N_t meets [L_t−1,L_t+7]].

Successive events have displacement −2d+2 and offsets in −1,...,7.
For d<=8 their chosen points are at most 2d+6<=22 apart, so the gap
is at least nine. In T more updates the zero suffix advances by at
least `2T−2 ceil(T/9)`. With Q=384, T=215 covers Q−2=382 sites;
including the initial update gives 216. The source assumption follows
when geometry is aligned and Workspace.Flag1 is zero outside current
faults: the joint source is off, and neither inconsistency nor two raw
Workspace faults can trigger a three-bit source. If Flag2's sources are
also zero, the unchanged §10 Flag2 quieting bound then gives both flags
quiet within a conservative **428 source-free updates**. This is not
a quieting bound on damaged geometry or a certificate of the new program.

[check_fast_flag_proposal.py](proofs/check_fast_flag_proposal.py) produces
an in-memory maintenance function with exactly these changes. Its receipt,
[fast_flag_proposal_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/fast_flag_proposal_certificate.json),
records 34,944 symbolic structural two-fault cases, all sixteen common
Age bits free, 60 symbolic pair-source agreement cases, 182 symbolic
end-seed cases, 1,024 actual Flag1 truth assignments, 69,800 local packet
cases, separated-group checks and event/duration arithmetic. It uses
the proved identical-word shortcut described for (G6), with the original
majority truth table checked too. The maintenance net has **2,771 gates
and 322 inputs**, versus 2,479 and 319 for the original, with the same
maintenance outputs retained: **292 additional maintenance gates**.
These are local Boolean/arithmetic certificates, not experiments implying
an unbounded reliability statement.

**Unproved construction obligations.** Sources must initialize packets
in every damaged configuration; the apparent-colony masks must let them
reach the needed quiet paths; paths ending at E0 or near the apparent
right boundary must be handled. Faster flags also reach a healthy colony's
left boundary sooner when its command is wrong, so (G7)'s 113-update
bound cannot be reused for this variant. Command provenance, Flag2
launch/reversal and partial-colony coordination need new checks.

The full self-interpreter must also gather the newly used upper Flag1
bits at offsets +6,+7,+8 and compile its **own** changed rule. G17's
`LANE_OFFSETS` and ROM omit those inputs. Merely replacing maintenance
while keeping that ROM is not self-simulation. Extending the existing
gather schedule also needs a new evaluation deadline: the third gather
starts at 20Q, while an offset-eight capture in that scheme is near 28Q,
after the current E0=9792 at Q=384. Storage, clock packing, complete
program/courier certificates, damaged simulation footprints and the
all-level proof remain to be constructed and verified. No core source
or ROM was changed, no smaller reliable Q/U is certified, and the
requested complete alternative construction is still **unproved**.

### Eight-site voted mail: proposed transport module

**This is another explicit proposed rule change, not G17.** It addresses
the gather deadline raised by (J2), without establishing a complete new
construction. The local transport and capture identities below are
**proved with their hypotheses**. A wider schema, its own interpreter and
ROM, and noisy damaged-colony simulation are **unproved**.

Retain the existing five-copy convention: copy slot e at holder y
represents the logical bit at p=y+e, e in −2,...,2. Write

    V_t(f,p) = majority(copy_t(f,p−e,e), e=−2,...,2).

During each gather, replace ordinary Mail transport by an eight-site
shift of these **voted** values. At the input tick G load both tracks
from V_t(Info,p). Subsequently use

    MR_(t+1)(p) = V_t(MR,p−8),
    ML_(t+1)(p) = V_t(ML,p+8).                              (J5)

These denote the reference logical values whose five copies are stored
by the next update. At other stages, use the original one-site voted
transport. Keep the existing courier override from voted Hold, and its
priority below load. Keep the old-Mail history capture and three-gather
majority, stage clears, computed-Flag1 Mail clearing and raw-Address wipe.
In particular, capture reads the Mail present **before** (J5)'s update.
A deterministic predicate of corrected Age selects the fast interval;
it needs no new stored speed bit. This specifies a transport module,
not a changed full `rule_g.build` or a self-interpreting candidate.

**Locality — proved.** At output holder y, slot x in −2,...,2 needs
V_t(MR,y+x−8), whose five input holders are y+x−8−e. Their union is
y+[−12,−4]. ML's corresponding union is y+[4,12]. The complete
module's radius is therefore **12**, not eight: two sites are needed
for the output copy offset and two for the input copy offset. The slower
transport and local capture/history votes fit inside that radius. In
combination with (J2)'s radius-eight maintenance and G17's remaining
radius-five modules, this proposed rule would have radius 12, unless
another new component introduced farther dependencies.

**Separated-error copy correction — proved conditionally.** Suppose
computed geometry is aligned, computed Flag1 is zero on the affected
transport holders, and load/speed/courier/capture/commit controls agree
with their reference values at all five holders of every primary they
update. Suppose initial copies agree with an arbitrary reference state
except N_0. Subsequent overwrites are singleton/adjacent-pair groups
mutually (24,24)-separated; any raw-Address wipe is confined to N_t.
Then, throughout these hypotheses, every reference mail/history bit has
correct raw copies except at

    Z_t = N_t union N_(t−1).                                (J6)

The proof is the same induction on five copies as in (5b), with the
source primary replaced by p±8. Every V_t uses five consecutive holders
at the current state time. Its faults lie in these holders at original
overwrite times t or t−1. Two such points are (24,24)-linked, so they
cannot belong to distinct E0 groups. The group has at most two holders;
the other three copies give the correct reference bit. Each next value
is therefore the reference Boolean function of its voted inputs and
correct controls. A current wipe can spoil only holder N_t, and new
overwrites add only N_(t+1), establishing (J6) at t+1. In particular
there is **no shifted copy-damage term** N_t±8: the vote corrects source
damage before the shift. This argument works for any fixed integer
transport step when the same five-copy/control hypotheses hold.

For (24,24) spacing, even the full 25-holder input interval meets at
most two distinct raw damaged holders from these two rows. If it met
three, either three distinct groups would have two points less than 24
apart, or an adjacent pair and a separate singleton would have nearest
distance at most 23. Both contradict separation. The two groups at
holders −12 and +12, possibly in successive rows, show that it can meet
two groups. The proof of (J6) only needs the smaller constituent votes.

This distinction matters at prospective reduced upper spacing (22,23).
Holders −12,−11 and +11,+12 can be two separated adjacent-pair groups,
so a global two-fault bound in the radius-12 neighborhood is then false.
Each individual five-copy voter still meets at most one group, and its
correctness proof survives. The (J2) geometry/flag control neighborhood
has diameter 13, so its stated two-fault correction likewise applies
locally. This establishes local compatibility with that spacing; it
does **not** construct the required effective upper error process (P8).

Arbitrary initial Mail is also erased by a correct gather load: its
next stored value is voted Info, apart from (J6)'s exceptions. The
reference Info must stay fixed during the gather, and the voted Info
must already satisfy the copy hypothesis. Likewise two correct history
captures suffice for the third-capture majority irrespective of the
remaining capture's value. These are consequences of the local formulas,
not correction claims for arbitrary physically damaged configurations.

**Capture coordinates and deadlines — proved conditionally.** Assume
Q and each capture skew d_j are multiples of eight. For a bit at layout
address L, capture neighbor j≠0 at primary p=mQ+L+d_j and input Age

    C_(j,g) = G_g + |j| Q/8 + 1 − sign(j) d_j/8.            (J7)

Load at input G_g creates Mail at state G_g+1. After tau=C_(j,g)−G_g−1
fast updates, its source primary is

    p + sign(j) 8 tau = (m+j)Q+L.

Thus (J7) reads precisely the neighbor's represented bit. Require
tau>=0, all intervening transport updates fast, and no intervening
Info change; the local correction hypotheses must hold on their causal
support. The eight residue classes of primary coordinates do not cause
aliasing: Q and d_j being divisible by eight makes this identity exact
in each class. A speed predicate may turn on for Ages G_g+1 through
the last capture and turn off before the next load or flag courier.
Reading old Mail makes the last capture independent of that input
tick's subsequent chosen shift.

For an **illustrative timing calculation only**, take Q=384, gathers
G_g=0,3840,7680, all offsets −12,...,−1,+1,...,+12, and skews chosen
from −8,0,8. Latest input captures are 578,4418,8258; the first two
finish before the next gather and the last is 1534 input Ages before
G17's E0=9792. Its new history is available at state Age 8259. A switch
back to unit speed before G17's courier input Ages 13479 and 13480
therefore has ample time in this arithmetic. Existing G17 skews are
not all divisible by eight and are **not reused**. This calculation
does not supply a valid layout, a full new schedule, or a sufficient
Q/U pair for reliability.

**A real storage obstruction — proved for the dense extension.** The
new rule observes farther raw Mail copies as well as farther Flag1 bits;
gathering only the new +6,+7,+8 Flag1 inputs would omit dependencies
of (J5). A direct dense extension of the old interpreter from ten
nonzero input lanes to twenty-four (radius 12) adds fourteen H1 and
fourteen H2 logical bits per cell, each with five copies: **140 raw
state bits**. Its width would already be 258+140=398 before other
packing changes. G17 has only Q−2 margin=268 working cells, so its
present one-layout-bit-per-cell scheme cannot encode that state at
Q=384. Even Q=512 with the same margin leaves only 396 working cells,
before reserved cells. Faster gathers solve this specific timing
obstacle but do not solve this storage obstacle. Sparse field-specific
gathers can use fewer bits; the following subsection gives a concrete
support/capture design that removes this static obstacle, while leaving
the complete interpreter and reliability proof unfinished. A larger Q
is another possible design choice, but no smallest sufficient Q is
established.

[check_fast_mail_proposal.py](proofs/check_fast_mail_proposal.py) builds
the clearly marked proposed module without touching the active rule.
It checks the original five-bit majority truth table and uses the
proved identical-word shortcut to certify 9,780 symbolic output
equalities in all 326 zero/one/two-arbitrary-holder cases, leaving
reference data and correctly computed controls free. It additionally
checks every compatible three/four-holder pattern in a 25-holder input
interval at reduced spacing 22. Its dependency audit records radius
12, and its arithmetic checks 7,200 capture identities. The receipt is
[fast_mail_proposal_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/fast_mail_proposal_certificate.json).
These are Boolean/arithmetic certificates, not random-noise experiments.
The full compiled candidate, its own ROM and physical simulation proof,
partial-colony transport, higher-error footprints, recovery and an
explicit positive noise threshold remain **unproved**.

### Field-specific histories without extra state bits: proposed sparse design

**This is a third proposed design component, not a modification of G17.**
The dense storage obstruction above is avoidable for the specific (J2)/(J5)
dependencies. There is now a concrete isolated Boolean circuit and capture
table in [check_fast_mail_proposal.py](proofs/check_fast_mail_proposal.py).
Its own ROM has **not** been compiled; it is not a complete candidate or
a proved reliable CA.

For each represented raw state bit b, let D_b be a fixed superset of
its used nonzero neighbor offsets. Assign those offsets injectively to
history ranks r=0,...,9. Rank r at layout primary L_b then stores the
particular neighbor offset j_(b,r), rather than one offset common to
that rank at every primary. Use zero capture skew for this concrete
design. Captures therefore occur at

    G_g + |j_(b,r)| Q/8 + 1,

and choose old MR for negative j and old ML for positive j. A fixed
lookup in corrected primary Address selects the corresponding offset,
direction and capture time. There are no new history bits or stored
lookup tags. The lookup table is a finite constant of this proposed
rule, just as its layout and eventual instruction ROM must be.

**Dependency capacity — proved for the specified circuit.** An
in-memory dependency envelope combines (J2), both transport speeds,
and arbitrary per-primary capture masks/directions, while retaining
the other G17 modules and 258-bit schema. Its raw-bit profiles are
recorded in the transport receipt. Every D_b has size at most **ten**.
The field maxima are:

| Raw field | Maximum used nonzero offsets per bit |
|---|---:|
| Address, Age, Workspace.Flag1, Workspace.Flag2 | 10 |
| Flag1 | 8 |
| Flag2 | 5 |
| Info | 5 |
| MR, ML | 10 |
| Compact registers | 10 |
| Hold, H1, H2, scratch, pending bit/kind/value | 4 |

The Mail bound is particularly relevant. For fixed raw copy slot e,
the MR fast source offsets are x−8−e, x=−2,...,2. Slow transport and
history/special reads add the local offsets, but their union still
has at most ten **nonzero** members; the own-cell input stays on Info.
The broad radius-12 neighborhood thus does not require twenty-four
history slots at every represented bit. Flag1 observes only the eight
positive offsets, not all positions in [−5,8]. The remaining field
profiles are verified from the live literal circuit nodes.

The checker assigns the 258 represented raw bits, in schema order,
to distinct work primaries 59,...,316, avoiding both command stores
58 and 325 and the margin. Sorting each D_b assigns its offsets to
the ten ranks. This provides 1,648 distinct nonzero input locations
(L_b,r), plus one own-cell Info location for each b. They cannot alias:
different b have different L_b, and different offsets of one b have
different ranks. This proves static capacity and an injective input
map, not the ability to issue the resulting program in G17's U.

**The lookup introduces no circular missing inputs — proved for this
finite circuit.** The initial envelope permits all capture directions
and masks as free controls. In the concrete circuit, those controls
are replaced by fixed predicates of corrected Address/Age; no external
capture controls remain. They therefore add only geometric input
offsets already in the envelope's Address/Age profiles. Direction
selection still reads voted local MR and ML, already both included.
The actual built circuit is checked against D_b for **every live raw
input**: all 1,906 are either own-cell inputs or covered nonzero
offsets. Thus the table derived from the envelope covers the table's
resulting circuit too. This is a finite support closure argument,
not an assertion that the eventual instruction ROM can be arbitrary.

The circuit has **22,457 gates**, 258 raw state bits and radius 12;
G17's pinned Boolean circuit has 17,013 gates. These counts include
the new maintenance, speed selection and fixed sparse capture logic,
with the old front/key interfaces. The proposed circuit still needs
its own program and instruction table, and a checked lookup/output
completion. Its digest in the receipt pins the abstract Boolean
circuit with its instruction input interface; it is **not** a
candidate digest or a stored ROM digest.

**Gathered-input identity — proved conditionally.** Let arbitrary
upper raw states z_m in {0,1}^258 be represented by five agreeing
Info copies at the stated L_b. Suppose physical geometry and controls
are aligned, Info is unchanged through the three gathers, computed
Flag1 is zero during mail transport, and (J6)'s separated-error
hypotheses hold. After the last capture, until a subsequent history
clear, the voted histories satisfy

    V(H1_r, mQ+L_b) = z_(m+j_(b,r))[b]                       (J8)

for every assigned rank. Each first/second capture obtains this bit
by (J7) with d=0; the third-capture majority obtains it too. Between
captures, history votes copy the reference value; wipes/overwrites
only contribute (J6)'s current/previous exceptions. Thus five-copy
history voting gives (J8). An independent own-cell Info vote gives
z_m[b]. This supplies **all** raw neighbor inputs of the concrete
circuit by the coverage result, even when the upper states contain
invalid Address/Age, arbitrary flags or inconsistent upper copies.
The hypotheses concern healthy physical encoding and its controls,
not upper geometry.

At Q=384, zero-skew captures end at input Ages 577,4417,8257; the
final H1 values are present at state Age 8258, before evaluation at
9792. Sparse controls agree across the five holders of a logical
primary because they use its corrected primary Address and common
Age. The lookup's Boolean truth checks cover all 512 raw Address
words, all ten ranks and all capture Ages and their immediate neighbors:
552,960 assignments. Outside the listed Age words every equality
factor is identically false. These checks and the gate/input audit
are certificates, not a finite random-noise campaign.

**Remaining construction work — unproved.** The existing compiler
and scheduler assume that a history rank has the same neighbor offset
everywhere. An isolated process now supplies the new input-location map
to the existing scheduler, without changing compiler files. Its finite
probe generated a 31,191-instruction listing requiring NPe=26, match
page MP=53 and NP=96, compared with G17's 13,21,37. Replay on 64 random
Boolean input vectors had zero mismatches. This is **measured only**
for program correctness; no universal symbolic schedule certificate was
run for this listing. The driver and receipts are
[probe_sparse_schedule.py](proofs/probe_sparse_schedule.py),
[sparse_schedule_probe.json](../figs/robustness/sparse_schedule_probe.json)
and [sparse_schedule_listing.json](../figs/robustness/sparse_schedule_listing.json).
The isolated input map is therefore concrete, but its physical execution
and the listing's universal correctness remain to be proved.

The listing does **not** fit G17's constants. Incorporating its larger
deadlines/pages into a proposed rule changes that circuit's timing
predicates, page width and possibly Age width/layout; its **own rebuilt
circuit** must then be scheduled and certified. The observed 96 pages
alone cannot be converted into a sufficient new U by leaving the old
circuit and ROM unchanged. Zero skew concentrates lane reads at a bit's
primary, and the measured schedule confirms the old 37 pages do not
suffice for this particular attempt.
At these unchanged G17 constants there is no closed own-ROM candidate.
The following SP1 subsection rebuilds the design at new constants and
proves its encoded simulation. Damaged-colony restoration, the upper error
process and an all-time positive noise rate remain unproved. The local
support and gather results remove one concrete storage obstruction;
they do not settle the full goal or establish a smallest reliable rule.

### SP1: a rebuilt sparse prototype with its own certified program

**SP1 is an explicit proposed rule and constant change. G17 is unchanged.**
It implements (J2)'s joint validation/eight-neighbor Flag1, (J5)'s voted
fast Mail and (J8)'s field-specific histories, with new clock/program
constants. It is defined in [proposed_sparse.py](proofs/proposed_sparse.py),
without recipe/manifest registration or changing `candidates.CURRENT`.

| Quantity | SP1 value |
|---|---:|
| Colony Q, radius | 384, 12 |
| Period U, raw state width | 55,296, 259 bits |
| Address/Age widths | 9, 17 bits |
| Age radix / blocks | 288 / 192 |
| Work area / comb | [58,326), five fronts, spacing five |
| Gather input Ages / fast step | 0,3840,7680 / eight |
| E0 / declared pages NP | 9792 / 128 |
| Early deadline NPe / match page MP | 40 / 67 |
| Signal / Workspace window start | 21312 / 21313 |
| Represented-bit layout | 59,...,317, in schema order |
| Circuit gates / ROM dimensions | 22,936 / 384 × 1024 |

Offsets/ranks are in [SP1_capture_table.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_capture_table.json).
The ROM/layout are in [SP1_program.npz](../figs/robustness/SP1_program.npz),
with [build](../figs/robustness/SP1_program_build.json) and
[listing](../figs/robustness/SP1_program_listing.json). The proposed
candidate SHA256 is
`8e6faba3fe2ad2c8c1dd50b97e1f3d172cd6bbf6c59ebc9162fd3d215a4147f0`;
its circuit SHA256 is
`2aef1ae53dd26bbdd45abbd6b2f8b6f66629ea0f149964d112b593d52b27d8b7`.
These identify this changed object. For keys outside the 384 ROM rows,
I=0 defines the total mathematical rule F_*; the front lemma below
justifies it. The native fetch code still needs the range remedy in §6.

This ROM is compiled from **the rebuilt 259-bit circuit**, not the previous
prototype. The fixed-MP schedule needs NPe=34 and NP=83, within the
declared 40 and 128. Its 30,366 instructions have a universal Boolean
certificate in [check_sparse_schedule.py](proofs/check_sparse_schedule.py)
and [SP1_symbolic_schedule.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_symbolic_schedule.json):
19 key equalities, two early flags, all 259 final Hold outputs, no undefined
register/scratch/lane read, and no Hold store outside the represented
bits/two command stores. Scratch consumers are at least five ticks after
their writes. This **proves the abstract own-ROM program**, under the
listed execution hypotheses; the build's 64-vector replay is finite
additional evidence.

The first proposal wrapper omitted `work_range`. Its independent physical
visit check failed on the first instruction; source/artifacts are preserved
in [SP1_work_range_failure/failure.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_work_range_failure/failure.json).
After that fix, NPe=32 needed 34;
[SP1_deadline_failure.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_deadline_failure.json)
records the second failure. The accepted object uses NPe=40 and a freshly
rebuilt circuit/ROM. Neither failed attempt supplies proof or physical
evidence for the accepted object.

**Locality and all-word totality — proved for SP1.** Every capture control
is a fixed predicate of computed primary Address/Age. The rule reads only
relative neighbors within radius 12; it has no absolute-position, level,
or external timing input. The unchanged front addition gives the slot
words of §6. Age's high bits select a window/direction; comb targets still
have bases 38+r or 325−r with spacing five, for r=0,...,511. Slot-word
pair differences cannot be 0,±5,±10,±15,±20 modulo 512. Thus at most
one slot arrives for every raw Address and 17-bit Age. A selected key
outside [58,326) has `inside` false, disabling instruction stores and
matching; outputs are independent of I. No arrival also gives that
independence. This proves the completion and the unfetched-key argument.
[check_sparse_front.py](proofs/check_sparse_front.py) evaluates the actual
new addition/timing gates in 524,288 Address/position/direction cases;
window factorization covers all 131,072 Age words. Its receipt is
[SP1_front_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_front_certificate.json).

Define E(z) as the new ordinary boundary encoding: canonical lower
Address, Age zero, all lower flags/work zero, and five agreeing Info
copies representing each arbitrary upper raw bit at the new layout.
Define E_a(z) additionally to put z.Flag2 at logical Info 58 and
z.Flag1 at 325, in all five copies. All other unused Info is zero.
These fixed maps apply on Z at every level.

**Noiseless encoded self-simulation — proved for SP1.** For every
z in ({0,1}^259)^Z, including invalid raw words and inconsistent upper
copies,

    F_*^55296(E_a(z)) = E_a(F_*(z)),
    F_*^55296(E(z))   = E_a(F_*(z)).                          (J9)

Proof. Physical geometry is canonical/common independently of z. Both
directional Address/Age votes return it at every update, whatever the
lower flags; the raw-Address wipe is off. The legal clock increments
through 55,296 Ages and wraps to zero. Before the Workspace window,
geometric inconsistency, joint validation and D3 are zero. Initial
special Info 3/381 is zero and Workspace outputs are off, so lower
flags stay zero through the gathers/couriers.

The five holders of a primary have the same corrected primary Address
and common Age, hence the same sparse controls and update. Five-copy
agreement is preserved. A gather load creates Mail one tick later;
the eight-site updates and (J7) give precisely the neighbor bit.
Three captures agree, proving (J8); own inputs remain on Info.
The rebuilt circuit's live inputs are all covered. Captures finish at
577,4417,8257 before evaluation 9792. Represented Info stays fixed until
commit. Extra Info 58/325 is absent from the input map and no certified
instruction reads it.

Hold clears at input Age 9791. A store puts the same pending bit in
all five holders at the next state; `lv` forwards it there, and the
following update materializes it in Hold/scratch. Verified consumers
are at least five ticks later. Front centers are 38+r+5j on forward
pages and 325−r+5j backward. Their five-holder windows are disjoint
and inside one colony. All 184,320 carry/center identities are checked:
at a turn each retains its word; otherwise it reads its preceding
center. Every holder therefore performs the abstract certified step
of that logical front, throughout the 128 pages.

On match page 67, front zero visits every working primary once, carrying
the correct upper lookup key in its first 19 registers. For a working
key the matching primary obtains the exact word from SP1's own ROM at
that Address/upper page. Otherwise the desired upper output is independent
of I by the all-word front lemma, and the certificate holds for the
retained instruction bits too. No upper geometric hypothesis is used.

Early flag stores occur at Ages 19002/19280, before deadline 21024.
Unit-speed couriers load at 21256/21255, traverse 55/56 sites and reach
special Info at input Age 21312. Fast transport has finished. Lower
flags can then clear Mail during the window, but the remaining program
never reads live Mail. Represented Info, histories, scratch and registers
retain their invariant, so final Hold is F_*(z). The only other Hold
stores are the correct output flags at 58/325.

The last Workspace-producing input Age is 22080. Stored Workspace
bits and their sources are zero from input Age 22082. Aligned geometry
also makes the joint source and D3 zero. Source-free Flag1 quiets in
216 updates by (J2); its proof depends on Q/the flag predicate, not
the old Age width. Unchanged Flag2 then quiets in another 212. Both
are quiet by state Age 22510, before commit 55295. Commit writes
correct represented Hold and auxiliary flags to Info, zeros all other
unused Info, resets Hold/scratch/histories/Mail/pending/front fields,
and wraps the clock. This is exactly E_a(F_*(z)), proving both
equalities. ∎

Induction gives `F_*^(nU)(E_a(z))=E_a(F_*^n(z))` for every n>=0.
Intact infinite initial hierarchy constraints have a solution by the
finite-depth encoding/compactness argument of §1. The noiseless closure
argument of §6 applies with (J9): finite-time observations need only
finitely many relevant encoded levels, with the physical clock/copy
induction between boundaries. All levels run **the same** F_*, Q and U.
This establishes noiseless hierarchy simulation, not higher-error repair.

**Complete encodings under E0-only noise — proved conditionally for
SP1.** Start from E(z) or E_a(z), permitting an initial separated N_0
puncture pattern. Allow arbitrary singleton/adjacent-pair overwrites
mutually (24,24)-separated. Let X_t be the noisy state and N_t its
current direct overwrite sites. For every n>=1,

    X_(nU)(x) = E_a(F_*^n(z))(x) outside N_(nU),
    decode(X_(nU)) = F_*^n(z).                               (J10)

Decode uses SP1's layout and the five-copy Info vote. Proof. Each
geometric voter has three correct words, so computed geometry stays
canonical/common and any raw wipe is confined to N_t. Before the signal,
two raw faults in the fourteen-site maintenance neighborhood cannot
create Flag1, its joint source, D3/D4 or Workspace. The two-fault (J2)
argument works for seventeen common Age bits too: three identical
words dominate both votes and the joint test. Computed flags are zero
through gathers/couriers.

Maintain consumed five-copy/front fields outside Z_t=N_t union N_(t−1).
Each constituent voter uses five consecutive holders, meeting at most
one overwrite group in these two rows. It corrects the source before
an eight-site shift or program read. Correct controls reproduce each
reference update; current wipes/new overwrites give Z_(t+1). Thus the
register, pending-forwarding and match argument in (J9) follows the
certified program despite E0. After the signal lower Mail can differ,
but no longer enters the program. On aligned geometry the E0 quieting
bounds 216+212 still apply, leaving 32,785 input Ages before commit.
At commit computed flags are zero, so even a current raw Address fault
cannot trigger a wipe. All copied/reset fields are correct before the
new overwrite N_(nU). Each Info vote has at most two faulty holders and
decodes the exact upper state. Reapply this argument at every boundary. ∎

Individual five-copy correction also works at (22,23) spacing, as proved
above. Its full-period quieting constants must be refitted before claiming
an analogous reduced-spacing period theorem. The effective upper process
and mixed higher-error repair are still unproved.

**Finite physical support, measured only.**
[check_sparse_physical.py](proofs/check_sparse_physical.py) compared full
SP1 boundary states on twelve rings of 147,456 sites for two periods:
four arbitrary upper contexts (all bits random, invalid fetch geometry,
active raw clocks and unused staggered words), each with ordinary and
augmented initial encoding, plus one context under four E0 overwrite
value modes (random, all-one, inversion, neighbor-colony copy). All
24 comparisons had zero unequal packed words outside current overwrites;
the one-step upper outputs also agreed between C and NumPy. The four
noisy rings each had 11,342 current overwritten sites at the first
boundary, explicitly excluded from that comparison. At the second
boundary they had none, and their entire raw states matched.

The lattice uses grid 26 and pair threshold 65536, with initial GPU
tick seven; groups are separated by at least (25,26), and an incomplete
end tile is skipped. This is E0-only sampling, not iid noise. ROM rows
384,...,511 were zero-padded only in the execution object to realize
the proved completion. The input artifact and receipt are
[SP1_physical_inputs.npz](../figs/robustness/SP1_physical_inputs.npz) and
[SP1_physical.json](../figs/robustness/SP1_physical.json). The proofs of
(J9)/(J10) are the copy/clock/program inductions above, not extrapolations
from these finite cases.

**Reliability remains unproved for SP1.** Neither (J9) nor (J10) gives
a positive iid noise rate: linked clusters above E0 are absent from those
hypotheses. Packet initialization/inside masks, quiet paths ending at an
overwrite or apparent right boundary, Flag2 reversals, partial-colony
simulation and a uniform hierarchy-wide damage envelope remain unproved.
The unchanged five geometric voters still permit the 141-site geometric
seed reduction; that does not establish erosion. No old G17 measured
burst lifetime or 113-update barrier is assigned to this changed rule.
A complete mixed-noise repair theorem and all-level finishing implication
are necessary before calling SP1 a reliable smaller construction.

### Three quiet joint supporters: a separate maintenance proposal

**This is another explicit proposed rule change, not a change to G17 or
SP1. Its built own-ROM instance is SP2 below.** Retain (J2)'s three
joint-pair validation and eight right Flag1 samples, and add the source

    K3 = at least three j in {1,...,5} satisfying
         adjusted_Address_j=v, raw_Age_j=beta, raw_Flag1_j=0;
    f1_new = f1_J2 OR ((v<Q−5) AND NOT K3).                  (J11)

Here v and beta are the existing right votes. Every subsequent use of f1
in maintenance uses f1_new. The guard permits the true right end to seed
quieting. Other geometry votes, Flag2 formulas and Workspace votes are
unchanged. The added test shares gates with pair validation: at Q384,
seventeen Age bits it adds **25 maintenance gates** above (J2), with no
new maintenance state or neighborhood inputs. This is not a gate minimum
or a sufficient construction change.

The exact in-memory source, hashes and universal local certificates are
in [check_quiet_majority_proposal.py](proofs/check_quiet_majority_proposal.py)
and [quiet_majority_proposal_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/quiet_majority_proposal_certificate.json).
The certificate uses the SP1 geometry field widths, not its unchanged
ROM. No experiment is used for the following lemmas.

**Healthy structural correction — proved for the proposed maintenance
rule.** In the fourteen-site observation interval [−5,8], permit any
two complete input states to be arbitrary, with all other geometry
canonical/common and flags/Workspace zero. At least three of the five
right inputs have the correct pair and Flag1 zero, so K3=1 whenever
the guard is on. Its source is therefore zero. The (J2) correction
argument applies unchanged. The certificate checks all 384 Addresses
and 91 two-site choices, with arbitrary symbolic seventeen-bit common
Age and arbitrary faulty words: 34,944 cases. The unchanged word-majority
shortcut is separately justified on the original primitive. This
statement covers structural outputs, not arbitrary poisoned simulation
fields.

**An ancestry with no later E0 stops — proved.** Assume only the
overwrite pattern is E0: singleton/adjacent-pair groups mutually
(24,24)-separated. Geometry, flags and work fields may otherwise be
arbitrary. A non-overwritten output with raw Flag1 zero and raw
Address a<Q−5 has computed f1_new=0. Inconsistency is zero, hence right
majorities exist and Right is selected. K3 supplies three quiet joint
supporters in the previous state's five right neighbors. At most two
of those neighbors are direct overwrites, so at least one supporter is
not overwritten. The actual raw-word adjustment has, for a<Q−5,

    adjusted_Address_j=a iff raw_Address_j=a+j, j=1,...,5.

This holds also when considering invalid raw input words; the certificate
checks all 512 words, giving 1,895 inverse identities. Consequently the
chosen child has Address a+j, raw Age beta and raw Flag1 zero, and is
not a direct error. Its incremented Age is the parent's Age.

Fix a canonical reference phase and common clock alpha_t, with
alpha_(t+1)=h(alpha_t). If the parent's Address/Age pair is wrong, this
child's pair is wrong: a correct child would give the correct Address
and clock at the parent. No inverse of h is assumed. Repeat backwards,
always choosing a non-overwritten quiet joint supporter. Every edge
moves right by 1,...,5 sites and raises raw Address by that same amount.
The path stops only at initial time or at Address in [Q−5,Q−1]. It
cannot stop at a later E0 overwrite, unlike (J1)/(J2). The mask certificate
checks all possible support/quiet/error sets with at least three joint
quiet supporters and at most two faults; its 1,696 cases also include
error subsets that need not be adjacent. Initial N_0 punctures can
likewise be avoided at the last edge. ∎

**Faster backward displacement — proved.** Choose the rightmost
non-overwritten quiet joint supporter at each step of that ancestry.
Its step j is at least three unless current errors remove higher
supporters. Charge ell=max(0,3−j), which is at most two. A unit charge
means j=2 and a quiet joint supporter at offset 3,...,5 is overwritten;
associate such a singleton. A charge two means j=1 and both other
supporters are overwritten. These are the actual adjacent E0 pair
at offsets h,h+1, with 2<=h<=4.

Let d be the gap between consecutive positive charges ell_i,ell_j,
measured along the backwards path. The parent displacement is at
most (3−ell_i)+5(d−1). Compare the rightmost point of the first
associated group and the leftmost of the second. Their signed
distance is at most

    5d+1−ell_i−ell_j,

and at least d−3. Thus d<=4 would give a point pair within 24 in
both coordinates, which E0 forbids. For d=5, the same contradiction
holds if ell_i+ell_j>=3. A six-step block therefore contains at most
one charge of size two, or two unit charges five steps apart: total
charge at most two. Partitioning a length-T ancestry into six-step
blocks gives

    displacement >= 3T−2ceil(T/6).                         (J11a)

The associated point groups are subsets of distinct actual E0
groups; using subsets is enough to contradict their isolation.
For d=1,2 the signed lower bound can be negative, but its absolute
value is still below 24. The certificate exhausts the support/error
masks, possible charged-group offsets and intervening displacements,
and all admissible six-step charge patterns. This is a deterministic
path bound, not a measured average speed. ∎

**Conditional E0 packet interception — proved.** The proposed f1
contains (J2)'s entire eight-sample threshold/persistence term, so
(J2)–(J4)'s packet lower bounds still apply when their inside-mask
hypothesis holds. Let a nominal Flag1 packet [a_t,b_t] have width at
least five, Flag1 one outside N_t, and those hypotheses for every
intervening update. Consider a forward segment of the above quiet
ancestry, starting at p_0=a_0−d with d>=1. Every node avoids N_t,
and each step moves left by 1,...,5. The segment cannot jump from
left of the packet to right of it: if p_t<a_t, then

    p_(t+1)<=a_t−2,
    b_(t+1)>=b_t−4>=a_t.

It cannot occupy the new packet either, since it is quiet and
non-overwritten. Thus it must remain strictly left of a_(t+1).
But the packet's leading bound and the path's speed bound give

    a_T<=a_0−(11/2)T+2,
    p_T>=a_0−d−5T.

For T>=2d+4, the second bound is at least the first, contradicting
that strict ordering. This intercepts a continuous quiet ancestry
even with E0 holes in the packet; the chosen ancestry cannot use
those holes. It removes (J4)'s separately assumed absence of direct
overwrites along the path **for ancestries obtained by (J11)**. The
certificate checks the no-jump inequalities and interception
arithmetic. Packet existence, its placement to the right of every
relevant ancestry start, and its inside-mask compatibility are
still unproved for arbitrary damaged trajectories. Near-end
starts on the other side of a packet are not covered. ∎

**A mixed-E0 apparent-boundary window — proved conditionally.** Take
Q384. Initially every wrong geometric pair lies in I_0=[a_0,b_0], of
width w, or in the current E0 overwrite sites N_0. Outside these sets,
Address has the reference phase and Age is the common clock. Continue
arbitrary E0 overwrites and permit arbitrary initial other fields.
There is no non-overwritten, quiet, wrong geometric pair at x>=a_0
with raw Address in {0,...,4}, for every T satisfying

    3T−2ceil(T/6)>w−1, and, for each a in {0,...,4},
    w−1+3s+2(1+floor(3s/23)) < Q−5−a,
    s=T−ceil((Q−5−a)/5) >= 0.                              (J12)

If s<0, the second test for that a is unnecessary. In particular, for
the 141-site seed supplied by (G4), **53<=T<=146** satisfies (J12).
Unlike the earlier noise-free window, this statement allows continuing
E0 during every update. It excludes only the specified quiet wrong
outputs; it does not assert that the entire seed has been repaired.

Proof. Apply the no-overwrite ancestry, choosing the rightmost clean
supporter. If it reaches time zero after T steps, (J11a) gives
displacement at least 3T−2ceil(T/6). Its non-overwritten wrong terminal
point must be in I_0. This is impossible for x>=a_0 and the first
inequality of (J12).
Otherwise it reaches a near-end Address after k steps. Its displacement
is at least D=Q−5−a and k>=ceil(D/5). Geometric growth (G1)–(G3) applies
unchanged: the new test changes only the choice between the same left
and right votes. At time u the rightmost non-overwritten damage is at
most

    b_0+3u+2(1+floor(3u/23)).

The terminal point is non-overwritten. With u=T−k<=s and x>=a_0,
its displacement is at most the left side of (J12), contradicting D.
If T<ceil(D/5), such a near-end stop is impossible in the available
steps. These are all stops, proving the statement. ∎

At w141, (J11a) first excludes initial-time stops at T53:
159−18=141>140. The worst raw Address is a=4, giving D375 and
minimum 75 steps for a near-end stop. At T146 the allowance is
140+213+20=373<375. At T147 it is
140+216+20=376: **the estimate fails there**, without implying an
actual bad output. At these constants the same sufficient window is
nonempty through seed width 277, whose sufficient window is just
T105; width 278 fails this estimate. Holding w141, the arithmetic window
would be [53,277] at Q640 and [53,471] at Q1024. These are arithmetic
illustrations, not built candidates, sufficient colony sizes or a
reliability theorem. They require the same raw-word inverse and growth
hypotheses before applying to a changed rule.

**Source-free aligned clearance — proved conditionally.** Assume
canonical/common geometry outside N_t, E0 separation, and raw
Workspace Flag1 zero outside N_t. Initial raw Flag1/Flag2 may be
arbitrary. All non-quiet-support sources are then zero: geometric
inconsistency and the pair validation vanish by three good right
words, and three Workspace ones are impossible. The true last two
Addresses have at most one inside right sample and the new guard is
off. They therefore compute Flag1 zero in one update, irrespective
of all other old flags and the two current faulty states. The
certificate checks these 182 symbolic end-seed cases.

Maintain a zero suffix [L,Q−1] outside current overwrite sites.
For any old suffix output with the guard on, three good right
neighbors are joint quiet supporters. With the guard off no new
source is possible. Inside right Flag1 ones come only from the at
most two faults. A nonfaulty old center is zero, so persistence is
off; a faulty center leaves at most one other faulty right neighbor,
so persistence is again off. This preserves the suffix through
arbitrary values of the new overwrites.

If N_t misses [L−2,L+7], both L−2 and L−1 compute zero. Their first
five right inputs are jointly correct, and at most the first input
can lie outside the old zero suffix: K3 has at least four supporters
when needed. In their eight-sample flag votes at most that one inside
input can be one. Even an old center one cannot persist. At true
colony ends outside samples are masked out and the guard is off.
The checker verifies 7,680 extension cases with arbitrary old center/
first-right flags and two arbitrary left input faults, including
arbitrary next-colony flags. When the zone is hit, simply retain L.
Thus, capping the suffix at the true left end,

    L_(t+1)=L_t−2+2 I_t,
    I_t=1 if N_t meets [L_t−2,L_t+7], else 0.

Pick an error point in the zone at each affecting event. Between
consecutive such events with gap d, the frontier moves −2d+2; their
zone offsets differ by at most nine. For d<=8 their spatial distance
is at most 2d+7<=23 and their time distance is below 24, contradicting
E0 separation. Affecting events are at least nine updates apart.
After the initial seed update, the suffix advances at least
2T−2ceil(T/9) cells in T updates. For T215 this is 382, enough to
clear Q−2 remaining cells. Thus all non-overwritten Flag1 bits clear
within **216 updates**. This proof permits continued E0 and arbitrary
Flag2. Once Flag1 is quiet, the unchanged aligned Flag2 proof clears
it in another 212 updates under its no-source hypotheses. ∎

An exact local snapshot explains the distinction from (J2). Put the
correct center Address at 100 and Age alpha=2000. Right inputs 1,2,3
instead support Address vote 2 and Age beta=2001; inputs 4,5 are
correct. Set right Flag1 at 2,3 only, all further flag samples zero,
left geometry correct, Workspace and Flag2 zero. The joint supporters
are {1,2,3}, the quiet supporters {1,4,5}, and their intersection
only {1}. (J2) outputs quiet wrong Address 2/Age 2002. (J11) raises
Flag1, leaves Flag2 zero and selects correct left Address 100/Age 2001.
The certificate verifies both exact outputs. Reachability or a
particular error level for this snapshot is not asserted.

**Remaining status — unproved.** The above removes later-overwrite
stops for this separate local proposal. It does not remove near-end
stops outside (J12), prove Flag2/Workspace control at damaged fronts,
initialize and deliver every required packet, or prove partial-colony
simulation and the higher-error process. The local certificate alone
does not establish encoded self-simulation; the own-ROM step for SP2
is given next. SP1's own-ROM receipts and physical experiments apply to
unchanged SP1 only. No positive iid-noise rate, complete repair deadline
or minimal sufficient change follows from (J11)/(J12).

### SP2: own-ROM realization of the quiet-majority proposal

**SP2 is an explicit new isolated construction, not CURRENT. G17 and
SP1 are unchanged.** [proposed_sparse_quiet.py](proofs/proposed_sparse_quiet.py)
retains SP1's field-specific captures, voted eight-site gather transport,
layout, schema and constants, and substitutes (J11) for maintenance.
In particular Q384, U55296, width259, radius12, NP128/NPe40/MP67,
work [58,326), represented bits 59,...,317 and 384×1024 ROM dimensions
are unchanged from SP1. The new circuit has **22,961 gates**.

The candidate SHA256 is
`0fc552fbe43de355bb5ae45146de04bddc1fe00e9e26c2a647193a787d100cba`;
the circuit SHA256 is
`c0b4d4879778db356f16e01516e58d8a817ff0a475351eb24c26ef68a5b2da9a`.
The ROM/layout are [SP2_program.npz](../figs/robustness/SP2_program.npz),
with [build](../figs/robustness/SP2_program_build.json),
[listing](../figs/robustness/SP2_program_listing.json) and
[capture table](../figs/robustness/SP2_capture_table.json).
The build needs NPe39/NP83, within the declared 40/128; the extra
diagnostic increases the early program dependency cost despite adding
only 25 circuit gates. There are 30,388 instructions. The build's
64-vector replay is **measured only**; correctness uses the independent
universal certificate.

**Abstract own program — proved under execution hypotheses.**
[check_sparse_quiet_schedule.py](proofs/check_sparse_quiet_schedule.py)
and [SP2_symbolic_schedule.json](../figs/robustness/SP2_symbolic_schedule.json)
prove all 259 final Hold equalities, two early flag equalities and
19 key equalities for the actual new circuit. No undefined register,
scratch or history read occurs. Scratch's minimum write/read delay
is five. Early Flag2 and Flag1 stores are at input Ages 20720 and
19856, before the 21024 deadline and the couriers. Exactly 261 Hold
stores cover the represented bits and two auxiliary commands.
The abstract physical front and gather coordinates are checked
separately; latest capture inputs remain 577,4417,8257.

**Locality and total output completion — proved.** The same sparse
protocol has no absolute position, level or external control input.
All live raw inputs are covered by its table, which still uses at
most ten neighbor offsets per represented bit. The all-word front
proof applies with the unchanged timing/addition. Its independent
SP2 receipt is [SP2_front_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/SP2_front_certificate.json),
from [check_sparse_quiet_front.py](proofs/check_sparse_quiet_front.py).
At most one slot arrives, for every raw Address/Age. Outside-work
arrivals have instruction-independent outputs, proving the I=0
completion on invalid ROM keys. Native execution still needs the
range remedy in §6. Let F_SP2 denote this completed mathematical rule.

Define E_2 and E_2a by the same ordinary/augmented boundary maps as
SP1, now representing an upper SP2 raw state. They are fixed maps
on Z; E_2a additionally stores upper Flag2/Flag1 at logical Info
58/325 in five agreeing copies.

**Noiseless encoded self-simulation — proved for SP2.** For every
z in ({0,1}^259)^Z,

    F_SP2^U(E_2(z))  = E_2a(F_SP2(z)),
    F_SP2^U(E_2a(z)) = E_2a(F_SP2(z)), U=55296.             (J13)

Proof. The physical copy/clock/front argument for (J9) applies
verbatim to the unchanged schema, timing, sparse controls and
transport. The new maintenance needs the following replacement
checks. Canonical/common geometry gives both correct votes, so
the selected geometry is correct even when flags are raised.
Until the signal all lower flags remain zero: every right pair
is correct and quiet, K3=1, and the new source vanishes. This
preserves all gather/courier assumptions. The three captures
therefore give the actual SP2 circuit inputs at their certified
locations. The new symbolic identities supply the key registers,
early commands and final Hold values; the old SP1 identities are
not used for these altered outputs. The five front positions,
five-copy forwarding and five-update scratch latency are unchanged,
so those abstract identities are realized by the physical rule.
The match pass uses the new own ROM for the new key registers.
Outside-work keys ignore I, including the I=0 invalid-row case.

Commands arrive before the Workspace window. For arbitrary upper
command bits the signal source stops by input 22082. The new
216-update aligned Flag1 clearance proved above and unchanged
212-update Flag2 clearance give quiet flags by state 22510, long
before commit. The represented Info, certified histories, scratch
and front registers follow the same invariants; Mail after the
signal never enters the program. At commit all 259 represented
bits and both auxiliary commands contain the new correct upper
output. Other unused Info is zero and all physical work/flag
fields reset. This is exactly E_2a(F_SP2(z)). Reapply at every
boundary for every n. The compactness and intact infinite-hierarchy
closure arguments use these same fixed maps at every depth. ∎

**Complete encoded simulation under E0 — proved conditionally.**
Start from E_2(z) or E_2a(z), with an optional initial N_0 puncture,
and allow arbitrary whole-state E0 overwrites at (24,24) separation.
For every n>=1, with N_t the current overwrite sites,

    X_(nU)(x)=E_2a(F_SP2^n(z))(x) outside N_(nU),
    decode_2(X_(nU))=F_SP2^n(z).                            (J14)

Proof. Geometry has three correct words in each vote. Before
the signal, the proposed structural correction certificate
gives computed flags zero even with the two arbitrary states
in the fourteen-site neighborhood: three correct quiet joint
supporters turn off the new source. The consumed five-copy
fields remain correct outside N_t union N_(t−1); each constituent
five-holder vote meets at most one two-site group in these two
rows. Thus it corrects the source before every read/shift, and
the correct computed controls realize the new certified program.
Current raw Address wipes remain confined to N_t. Post-signal
Mail differences do not enter program inputs. The new aligned
216+212 clearance bound permits continuing E0 and leaves the
same commit slack as SP1. At commit computed flags are zero,
so no current Address fault causes a wipe; stores and resets
are exact before fresh N_(nU) overwrites. Three of each five Info
copies decode the exact upper state. Induction proves all n. ∎

**Finite physical support — measured only for SP2.**
[check_sparse_quiet_physical.py](proofs/check_sparse_quiet_physical.py)
checked twelve 147,456-site rings for two periods, giving 24 whole-state
boundary comparisons. Four arbitrary upper contexts, each with ordinary
and augmented encoding, cover random raw words, invalid fetch geometry,
active raw clocks and unused staggered words. Four further rings use
random/all-one/inverted/next-colony-copy E0 overwrite values. Every
comparison was exact outside current direct errors; upper one-step
outputs independently agreed between NumPy and CUDA. No native-C
comparison was made for SP2.

Seed 1082602 and all upper inputs are saved in
[SP2_physical_inputs.npz](../figs/robustness/SP2_physical_inputs.npz), with
case hashes, kernel digest and results in
[SP2_physical.json](../figs/robustness/SP2_physical.json). The 26×26
lattice, initial GPU tick seven and pair threshold 65536 give actual
E0 spacing at least (25,26). Each noisy first boundary excludes
11,342 current overwritten sites. The second boundaries have none
and match the entire encoding. Execution-only zero padding realizes
the proved invalid-key completion; stored ROM and generators are
unchanged. These finite checks are separate from (J13)/(J14)'s
universal proofs and contain no iid-error reliability experiment.

These statements concern globally encoded physical geometry and
E0-only punctures. The no-overwrite ancestry and window (J12)
also apply to actual SP2 maintenance, even with arbitrary
simulation fields, because its raw geometry/flag outputs are
exactly the stated maintenance outputs. **Mixed higher-error
restoration, localized partial-colony simulation, an effective
upper error process and positive iid-noise reliability remain
unproved.** SP2 has no proven all-field higher-error repair time
or sufficient/minimal Q,U. Its own-ROM construction resolves
one implementation obligation; it does not resolve the goal.

### A coherent phase block: complete conditional repair proofs for G17 and SP2

**Status: proved under the following hypotheses.** This is a structural
repair theorem for the unchanged G17 rule and the separately changed SP2
rule, not a repair theorem for a general real level-1 error. In particular,
the common-clock and initial Flag2/Workspace assumptions below are essential
to this proof. No Gray/Gács large-constant repair lemma is used here.

Let F be either completed mathematical rule specified above, acting on Z.
Fix two different phases theta_0,theta_1 modulo Q=384 and a finite interval
I=[a,b], of width w. At state zero assume:

- Address(x)=(x−theta_1) mod Q on I and
  Address(x)=(x−theta_0) mod Q off I, with canonical representatives.
- Every physical Age is zero. Every Flag2, Workspace.Flag1 and
  Workspace.Flag2 is zero.
- Flag1 may be arbitrary on I and is zero off I. All other fields may be
  arbitrary everywhere. There are no subsequent overwrites.

Write h for the actual packed-clock increment and alpha_t=h^t(0).
Then, for every site x and every t at or after the geometric bound in this
table, Address(x,t)=(x−theta_0) mod Q and Age(x,t)=alpha_t:

| Rule | Allowed w | Geometric repair by | Flag1 zero at | U/32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| unchanged G17 | 1,...,62 | 588 updates | 800 updates | 648 |
| changed SP2 | 1,...,141 | 631 updates | 847 updates | 1728 |

The Flag1 assertion is at the displayed time, before the Workspace stage;
it is not an assertion that flags remain zero for all later times with
arbitrary simulation data. The geometry assertion is permanent. There is
no assertion that the intended simulation data or bit has been restored.
At every time, bad geometry is confined to [a−5,C_true−1], where C_true
is the first good colony boundary strictly after b. This interval lies
in at most two adjacent good colonies: [a−5,b] has width w+5<Q, and
rounding its right end to that colony's right boundary adds no colony.

Here is the proof, including the escape from apparent colony boundaries.
Call theta_0 good and theta_1 bad, let B_t be the set of bad-phase sites,
and let K_t be its quiet subset, where stored Flag1 is zero. Use kappa=1
for G17 and kappa=3 for SP2.

**Exact reduction — proved.** With two phases and one common clock, each
adjusted five-neighbor Address vote contains just two distinct canonical
words. One has at least three votes. Both Age votes are alpha_t, so Age
remains common and the Address output remains one of these two phases.
During the bounds used below, t<T_wf: T_wf is 13537 for G17 and 21313
for SP2. Fresh Workspace sources are therefore off, regardless of all
simulation fields; the initially zero Workspace bits remain zero. The
no-right-majority source is absent and Flag2 has no source, hence stays
zero. Computed Flag1 chooses the left Address vote when one and the
right vote when zero.

More explicitly, if v is the right-voted Address at x, an opposite-phase
left input j contributes to the inconsistency source exactly when v>=j,
for j=1,...,5. Three such inputs force computed Flag1=1. G17 samples
right Flag1 with its five-input inside mask. SP2 samples eight and adds
the J11 diagnostic. When v<Q−5, a quiet wrong output requires at least
one quiet bad input among x+1,...,x+5 for G17: the three wrong-phase
voters and the three quiet flag voters intersect. For SP2 it requires
at least three quiet bad inputs among those five, directly by J11.
Consequently, provided no bad output has v>=Q−5,

    max K_(t+1) <= max K_t − kappa.                       (J15a)

The statement includes the empty-set case: an empty K_t stays empty
under that proviso. Here there is no Age/Address support-intersection
problem, because the clock is common.

**Right confinement — proved.** Let C_true be the first good colony
boundary strictly to the right of b. Thus C_true<=b+Q. Initially its
first colony has Flag1=0 and Workspace.Flag1=0. The true-colony barrier
G6 applies, with no direct faults. Its proof transfers to SP2 because
every inside Flag1 sample of this colony is quiet, and its three joint
right supporters are quiet wherever J11 is enabled. Both circuits
therefore preserve the good suffix [C_true,infinity), with its first
colony quiet, while the Workspace stage is off. Thus B_t is bounded
above by C_true−1. Also, if B_t has right edge b_t, then

    b_(t+1) <= b_t+3:                                    (J15b)

at x>b_t+3 both left and right majorities are good. B_t need not be an
interval for either assertion.

**Ordinary prefix advance — proved.** Suppose all sites x<=p are good,
and put s=(p−theta_1) mod Q. If 5<=s<Q−1, this prefix stays good and
advances by at least min(3,Q−1−s). For an old prefix site whose right
majority could be bad, x is one of p−2,p−1,p. Its bad right-vote label
is at least s−2>=3; all five left inputs are good and the first three
are inside, forcing Flag1=1. For each new site x=p+d, 1<=d<=3, not
past the next bad boundary, at least three left inputs are in the good
prefix. Its bad label s+d>=6 makes all five left inputs inside, again
forcing the good left vote. A good right vote needs no repair. At a
bad boundary C, the prefix x<=C−1 is separately invariant: the only
potentially bad right votes in its last three sites have labels
Q−3,Q−2,Q−1, and all left inputs are good and inside.

**Boundary startup — proved.** Suppose this invariant prefix ends at
C−1, and all bad sites lie in [C,C+v−1]. Set q=ceil(v/kappa). By
(J15b), through q+2 updates any bad label is at most

    v−1+3(q+2).

If this is <Q−5, (J15a) applies throughout that interval. After q
updates there are no quiet bad sites: their right edge has moved at
least kappa*q>=v sites to the left of C. They remain absent for the
next two updates. At update q+1, sites C,C+1,C+2 have three good
left inputs; Flag1=1 selects good geometry, while a wrong output with
Flag1=0 would be a forbidden quiet bad site. These three sites are
therefore good. At q+2, sites C+3,C+4,C+5 have three protected good
left inputs that are inside even for bad labels 3,4,5, and their
inconsistency source forces the good left vote. The former prefix
cannot retreat while quiet bad sites are absent. We now have a good
prefix through C+5, so ordinary advance resumes with s=5. This
startup takes at most ceil(v/kappa)+2 updates.

**At most two startups, with v<=w+5 — proved.** Put
delta=(a−theta_1) mod Q and C_0=a−delta. If delta<=5, use the initial
good prefix C_0−1 and start there with extent v<=w+delta<=w+5.
At the next possible startup C_0+Q, the right barrier gives

    v <= C_true−(C_0+Q) <= delta+w−1 <= w+4.

There is no third startup, since C_true<C_0+2Q when w+5<Q. If
delta>=6, the initial prefix a−1 has s>=5. Ordinary advance reaches
C_0+Q−1. Its three-site advance and (J15b)'s three-site growth cancel;
the final partial advance loses at most two sites, so the extent at
this first startup is <=w+2. At C_0+2Q the right barrier gives
v<=delta+w−1−Q<=w−2. A third startup would be beyond C_true.
If no bad sites remain or the prefix reaches the protected suffix,
the construction stops earlier.

**Bounds and permanence — proved.** For SP2, v<=146 and q=ceil(v/3)
give v−1+3(q+2)<=2v+7<379=Q−5. For G17, v<=67 and q=v give
v−1+3(q+2)=4v+5<379. Thus every required startup meets its proviso.
The initial prefix anchor is at least a−5; the target is C_true−1.
Their distance is at most Q+w+4. Each ordinary update advances at
least one site, and there are at most two startups. Hence

    T_geom <= Q+w+4 + 2(ceil((w+5)/kappa)+2).              (J15c)

This is 588 for G17 at w=62 and 631 for SP2 at w=141. The proof is
self-consistent with the Workspace-off assumption: both bounds,
and their flag-clearance extensions below, are below T_wf. Once
the prefix meets the good suffix, every Address/Age vote is correct
everywhere, independently of flags and simulation fields. Geometry
therefore remains correct for all future time, including later
Workspace stages. Source-free aligned Flag1 clears in 212 updates
for G17 (§10) and 216 for SP2 (J11); this gives the table's 800/847.
The tracked initial prefix begins at least at a−5 and never retreats,
while the protected suffix begins at C_true. This proves the stated
two-colony confinement as well as the lifetime bound.

The local certificate is
[check_sparse_phase_repair.py](proofs/check_sparse_phase_repair.py),
with [SP2_coherent_phase_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/SP2_coherent_phase_certificate.json).
It checks the actual maintenance reductions for all 1024 two-colour
neighborhoods and every inside-mask regime (11 G17, 14 SP2), with
all observed Flag1 and common-Age bits free. It also checks all valid
Address additions for offsets −8,...,8, the prefix implications,
the protected suffix for all 384 addresses, and every width in the
table. The reduction to phase equality and inside masks makes these
universal local identities, rather than sampled phase differences.
The unbounded-line and time argument is the proof above; the
certificate is not a finite simulation substituted for that argument.

**Finite support — measured only.**
[check_coherent_phase_physical.py](proofs/check_coherent_phase_physical.py)
ran 1536 cases for each rule on 15,360-site rings, with a clean twin,
six widths, eight placements, eight phase differences and four initial
Flag1 patterns. All other fields began as random raw bits. Every tested
case satisfied the theorem's hypotheses, with no later noise. All
Address/Age words agreed with the reference at the proved geometric
bound, remained equal at the flag bound, and all four flags were then
zero. The last observed geometric differences were at updates 148
for G17 and 151 for SP2. Substantial simulation-field differences
remained at the final times; the test does not claim all-field repair.
The maintenance cone stayed away from the periodic edge during the
source-free horizon. This was a CUDA check using static pack/unpack
helpers, with no native-C comparison. The saved inputs, per-colony
tracking and receipts are
[G17 inputs](../figs/robustness/G17_coherent_phase_inputs.npz),
[G17 tracking](../figs/robustness/G17_coherent_phase_tracking.npz),
[G17 receipt](../figs/robustness/G17_coherent_phase_physical.json),
[SP2 inputs](../figs/robustness/SP2_coherent_phase_inputs.npz),
[SP2 tracking](../figs/robustness/SP2_coherent_phase_tracking.npz) and
[SP2 receipt](../figs/robustness/SP2_coherent_phase_physical.json).

**Coherent clock damage as well — proved conditional extension (J16).**
The common-clock hypothesis can be weakened without changing either
rule. In J15, give every good-colour site initial Age=age_code(A) and
every bad-colour site initial Age=age_code(B), for these integer ranges:

| Rule | Good clock A | Bad clock B | Width/bounds |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| G17 | 0,...,12737 | 0,...,12949 | same as J15 |
| SP2 | 0,...,20466 | 0,...,20682 | same as J15 |
