Keep every other J15 hypothesis. Then by T_geom every site has good
Address and Age=h^t(age_code(A)), permanently thereafter. Flag1 is zero
at the same displayed flag-clearance bound. These are sufficient clock
ranges for this proof, not optimal ranges or permission to omit the
Workspace-source exclusion.

To prove the extension, let alpha_t=h^t(age_code(A)) and
beta_t=h^t(age_code(B)). Inductively each Address colour carries exactly
its own Age word. A three-of-five Address colour majority also supplies
three identical Age words on that side. Thus the Address and Age votes
select the same colour. If alpha_t=beta_t they still agree, trivially.
With two distinct Address phases, an opposite-colour Age mismatch is
already an opposite-colour Address mismatch; its inside count cannot
raise an extra source. Same-colour joint supporters match both words.
Consequently the exact colour/Flag1 reduction and (J15a) are unchanged,
and the output pair stays in the two-colour domain. This observation
does not apply to unrelated Age words within an Address colour.

The barrier's good suffix has common Age alpha_t and permits arbitrary
left clocks, so G6 still applies. Every prefix implication selects the
good left pair, not just its Address. The rest of J15's boundary/time
proof is unchanged and erases every bad pair within T_geom. Before
that time, both possible computed clocks are below the Workspace
launch range: A+t<T_wf and B+t<T_wf for 0<=t<T_geom. Afterwards only
the good clock remains and A+t<T_wf for 0<=t<T_flag. These inequalities
follow from A<=T_wf−T_flag, B<=T_wf−T_geom, and the bounds in J15.
They also exclude period wrap before repair. Thus zero Workspace
sources, and hence zero Flag2, close the induction through geometric
repair; the aligned source-free flag-clearance proof then applies.
Once all pairs are good, both votes keep correct geometry even during
future Workspace stages.

[check_paired_phase_repair.py](proofs/check_paired_phase_repair.py) and
[paired_phase_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/paired_phase_certificate.json)
certify the local extension with both Age words free (32 Age bits for
G17, 34 for SP2), all nine observed Flag1 bits free, all 1024 colour
neighborhoods and the same inside-mask regimes. The prefix checks
also verify the selected good Age and its actual increment. The
actual launch predicate is checked at every legal tick below T_wf
(13537 G17, 21313 SP2). J15's phase arithmetic, suffix and global
bound proof are reused with their explicit hypotheses verified above.
An initial failed symbolic comparison used the two equivalent
orientations of an XOR multiplexer; the limited rewrite algebra did
not prove their equivalence. The final checker uses the circuit's
right-vote orientation and needs no new algebra axiom or rule change.

Finite paired-clock support is **measured only**:
[check_paired_phase_physical.py](proofs/check_paired_phase_physical.py)
ran 2048 cases for each rule at its maximum proved width, using good
clock ticks zero and the maximum allowed A, and four bad-clock ticks
including the maximum B. It crossed eight placements, eight shifts
and four Flag1 patterns. All other fields were random raw bits, with
no later errors. Every case met both bounds; the last observed
geometry differences were again at 148/151. Non-geometric residues
remained at the flag bound. The receipts and saved inputs/tracking are
[G17 receipt](../figs/robustness/G17_paired_phase_physical.json),
[G17 inputs](../figs/robustness/G17_paired_phase_inputs.npz),
[G17 tracking](../figs/robustness/G17_paired_phase_tracking.npz),
[SP2 receipt](../figs/robustness/SP2_paired_phase_physical.json),
[SP2 inputs](../figs/robustness/SP2_paired_phase_inputs.npz) and
[SP2 tracking](../figs/robustness/SP2_paired_phase_tracking.npz).
This was CUDA only, with the periodic edge beyond the maintenance
cone during the source-free interval.

**First-period simulation and a localized upper pair — proved for this
restricted seed (J17).** Fix A=0 in J16. Translate coordinates so the
good phase is zero, and write E_a for G17's augmented encoding or E_2a
for SP2's. Let g be the proved geometric bound (588/631), and set
z_g=decode(X_g) on the true colonies. Even with arbitrary other fields
everywhere at state zero,

    X_U = E_a(F(z_g))             (G17),
    X_U = E_2a(F_SP2(z_g))        (SP2).                    (J17)

Here the whole physical state, not just its decode, agrees. If additionally
X_0 agrees with E_a(z_0) or E_2a(z_0) outside the seed interval I, then
z_g differs from z_0 only in the at most two adjacent true colonies
intersecting [a−5,b]. This realizes an arbitrary upper pair replacement
**before** the first upper update for this seed. It does not supply an
effective error map for arbitrary physical trajectories.

**Proof of the upper support.** Every represented bit of an upper
state has its logical position in the work-area layout and its five
Info holders at offsets −2,...,2. Each of these holders lies strictly
inside its true colony; no represented position is logical 3 or Q−3.
For a colony outside the stated pair, all five holders have canonical
good geometry for every time before repair, by J15's confinement.
Their initial Info values agree with z_0. The actual Info update is
the majority of those same five holders, except at commit or the
special signal; its wipe factor is

    NOT(computed_Flag1 AND (computed_Address != old_Address)).

At these good holders the Address comparison is false, regardless of
flags, so the wipe cannot act. Their common current Age is the physical
tick t. There is no commit for t<g<U−1, and the special signal acts
only on logical 3/Q−3, not on represented data. Thus induction preserves
every represented Info value of this colony through state g. No mail,
scratch or front input can enter that Info-majority branch. Consequently
its decoded upper state remains z_0. Colonies in the pair may have any
decoded state; no correctness there has been assumed.

**Proof of the whole boundary.** At g, geometry is globally aligned
with legal Age age_code(g). The next update makes each represented
Info value's five copies agree with their majority z_g. Thereafter
that represented value is static until commit: the wipe is off on
aligned geometry, and the later special signal uses unrepresented
positions. Workspace sources remain off until their scheduled window.
The source-free flag bounds quiet Flag1 by 800/847; Flag2 is already
zero and remains so before the window. Both times are below the second
gather's load at 3840. Therefore the second and third gathers are
correct, even if the first histories and every simulation field at
g were arbitrary. Their reloads replace earlier mail; the third capture
has two correct operands in maj3(h1,h2,passing).

All certified history inputs are ready before evaluation: G17's latest
third capture is 9591, SP2's 8257, and evaluation starts at 9792 for
both. Since g<9792, non-evaluation front/pending reset removes earlier
garbage; the Hold stage wipe at 9791 precedes every certified store.
The universal program certificates exclude every scratch read without
an earlier defined write. They compute all output bits, key registers
and early commands for precisely z_g, irrespective of any remaining
unused starting fields. Couriers, special signals, subsequent quieting
and commit then have exactly the preconditions and outputs already
proved in §6/(J13). Commit clears all other lower fields and installs
E_a(F(z_g)) or E_2a(F_SP2(z_g)). This proves (J17). Notice that this
uses the two clean later gathers, not an assumption that the first
gather or initial decoded upper bit was correct. ∎

**Complete clean recovery from two initial encoding levels — proved
corollary.** If z_0 itself is a complete boundary encoding E_a(y) or
E_2a(y), the upper pair replacement corrects in one upper update:
F(z_g)=F(z_0), or F_SP2(z_g)=F_SP2(z_0). For G17 this is (7).
For SP2 at this Age-zero boundary, the local J11 two-fault certificate
gives correct geometry and computed Flag1/Flag2 zero for any two
overwritten sites; Workspace sources need three supporters and cannot
fire from two bad inputs. Every five-copy value has at least three
correct holders. Age zero loads mail from that voted Info, has no
history capture, commit, special signal or evaluation arrival, and
resets front/pending/register fields. Hold, scratch and histories were
zero and their votes stay zero. Info keeps its correct majority
because computed Flag1 is zero, even at an overwritten raw Address.
Fresh Workspace flags are zero because their window is off. These
are all fields of the actual SP2 schema, so its complete one-step
state equals the clean upper update. This argument is stated at the
boundary encoding; it does not invoke an unproved damaged upper orbit.

By (J17), the entire physical state at U therefore equals the clean
trajectory's state at U. With no later noise, deterministic evolution
keeps equality forever. In particular an initially intact infinite
hierarchy has completely recovered after this restricted seed. This
is not a theorem for errors at all stages, arbitrary islands, or
independent continuing noise.

Finite support for (J17) and the corollary is **measured only**:
[check_phase_period_recovery.py](proofs/check_phase_period_recovery.py)
used two initial boundary encodings on 147,456 sites and eight
maximum-width seeds per rule. Replacements were arbitrary raw bits
subject to J16's geometry/flag constraints, with placements including
true boundaries, shifts 3/160, and bad clocks zero/the maximum B.
At state g the decoded upper changes were inside the proved pair;
their NumPy upper updates exactly equalled the clean update. At U,
all eight full physical states and the clean twin equalled the entire
fresh clean encoding. No later faults or native-C comparison were used.
Saved replacements, initial states and decoded upper states accompany
[G17 receipt](../figs/robustness/G17_phase_period_physical.json),
[G17 inputs](../figs/robustness/G17_phase_period_inputs.npz),
[G17 decoded states](../figs/robustness/G17_phase_period_decoded.npz),
[SP2 receipt](../figs/robustness/SP2_phase_period_physical.json),
[SP2 inputs](../figs/robustness/SP2_phase_period_inputs.npz) and
[SP2 decoded states](../figs/robustness/SP2_phase_period_decoded.npz).

**Remaining gap — unproved.** An actual level-1 error can introduce
several phases, incoherent clocks, Flag2 and Workspace sources, and
continuing E0 faults. Such a state need not reduce to two colours;
quiet ancestry and the startup proviso above do not give its repair
time. In particular, G4's 141-site seed does not meet G17's w<=62
hypothesis or either rule's paired-clock/flag hypotheses. J15–J17 do
not discharge general P6, localized simulation P7, the upper error map P8,
or the all-level iid argument. It proves a restricted repair result
at small Q; it does not supply a sufficient or minimal change for
the requested reliability theorem.

### SP3: a separate vote change and an arbitrary-island eroder

**Explicit new construction: G17, SP1 and SP2 are unchanged.** SP3 retains
SP2's quiet diagnostic, fast voted mail, sparse histories, schema and
constants, but replaces its geometry selector:

    old: vote_right = exists AND (NOT computed_Flag1 OR computed_Flag2)
    SP3: vote_right = exists AND NOT computed_Flag1.          (J18)

Flag2 and Workspace.Flag2 are still computed, represented and simulated;
they cannot override the left vote. This is not a proved minimal or
sufficient reliability change. Gray's higher-island Flag2 proof does not
transfer; a new higher-island argument is required.

The isolated sources are [prefix_selection.py](proofs/prefix_selection.py)
and [proposed_sparse_prefix.py](proofs/proposed_sparse_prefix.py). Its
Q384/U55296, width259, radius12, NP128/NPe40/MP67 instance has 22,960 gates.
The candidate SHA256 is
`a699c413c58c658ee48bf37bb7f6c9559c146ee80c4f5ec4edd916304104ce89`;
the netlist SHA256 is
`b3b703c17db4a03825f8a89827385ee6598a4e072e7de882af632d331205f0e5`.
Its own [ROM](../figs/robustness/SP3_program.npz),
[listing](../figs/robustness/SP3_program_listing.json),
[capture table](../figs/robustness/SP3_capture_table.json) and
[build receipt](../figs/robustness/SP3_program_build.json) come from
[build_sparse_prefix_program.py](proofs/build_sparse_prefix_program.py).
The schedule uses NPe38/NP81 within 40/128, with 30,810 instructions;
it is not SP2's ROM attached to a changed rule.

**Own-ROM and total output — proved.**
[check_sparse_prefix_schedule.py](proofs/check_sparse_prefix_schedule.py)
and [its receipt](../figs/robustness/SP3_symbolic_schedule.json) prove
all 259 final outputs, two early flags and 19 key registers for every
Boolean input. They check 4677 defined scratch reads with delay at least
five. Early Flag2/Flag1 stores are at 20154/20432, before deadline 21024;
evaluation ends at 46656 and commit is at 55295. Actual fixed capture
coordinates are checked, not external unimplemented controls.
[check_sparse_prefix_front.py](proofs/check_sparse_prefix_front.py) and
[its receipt](../figs/robustness/SP3_front_certificate.json) prove
all-raw-word front uniqueness and I=0 output completion outside work.
Use that completion to define F_3 on every raw state.

**Encoded self-simulation — proved.** Let E_3/E_3a use SP3's own
schema/layout, with upper Flag2/Flag1 at unused Info 58/325 in E_3a.
For every upper configuration z on Z,

    F_3^U(E_3(z))  = E_3a(F_3(z)),
    F_3^U(E_3a(z)) = E_3a(F_3(z)), U=55296.                 (J21)

J13's physical proof applies with these verified substitutions. At aligned
physical geometry both side votes are the same canonical Address/common
Age, so (J18) preserves it for every physical flag value. Flag predicates,
copy protocol, sparse captures, couriers, match/commit rules and stage
wipes are unchanged. The new two-fault certificate below closes healthy
maintenance. Histories are ready at 577/4417/8257. The own program computes
F_3 and its early stores precede the same couriers. Unchanged source-free
216+212 flag clearing gives quiet flags by 22510, before commit. These
are every physical precondition of J13; its full-boundary conclusion now
represents F_3. Reapply at boundaries and use compactness/finite-time
induction for noiseless closure at all levels of this fixed rule.

The E0-only complete-encoding proof J14 also transfers: each side geometry
vote has three correct inputs independently of (J18); copy errors stay in
N_t union N_(t−1), with at most two errors per five-holder vote; flags
quiet before gathers/commit. Consequently

    X_(nU)=E_3a(F_3^n(z)) outside N_(nU),
    decode(X_(nU))=F_3^n(z).                               (J22)

This is **proved conditionally** on complete initial encoding and global
E0 spacing, not on arbitrary higher-error damage.

**Arbitrary-island theorem — proved, noise-free.** Initially all physical
Address/Age pairs outside I=[a,b] are canonical true-phase Address
(x−theta) mod Q and Age zero. Inside I, of width 1<=w<=196, both raw
words may be arbitrary and unrelated, including unused words. All other
fields may be arbitrary everywhere, except that the first true colony
strictly right of b has Flag1=Workspace.Flag1=0. There are no subsequent
overwrites. Set t_0=2ceil(w/4). Then every Address **residue modulo Q**
and every exact raw Age permanently match the reference by

    T(w)=t_0+ceil((Q+w+t_0−1)/3).                          (J20)

Through repair, wrong residues/Ages are confined to
[a−(t_0+1),C_true−1], where C_true is the first true boundary after b.
This interval lies in at most two adjacent true colonies. Raw Address
aliases stay in those same two colonies, but need not stay within this
pointwise interval. The separate normalization proof gives canonical
Address everywhere by T(w)+43; all four flags are zero by T(w)+472,
before the Workspace window. Thus w141 gives phase/Age by271, raw geometry
by314 and flags by743; w196 gives324/367/796.
No hypothesis is imposed on Flag2/Workspace.Flag2
even outside I. The quiet right colony and absence of continuing noise
are explicit hypotheses.

**Right confinement and local sources — proved.** The actual maintenance
net's geometry/Flag1 outputs have no Flag2/Workspace.Flag2 ancestors.
The complete 279-output circuit, including instruction keys, strengthens
this: only next physical Flag2 depends on either raw input field.
Thus physical errors limited to these fields cannot influence geometry
or any other field's future updates; they do not replace a theorem for
arbitrary whole-cell errors.
Flag1 sources only raise it. G6's barrier proof applies to the first
right true colony: inside samples exclude outside flags, the quiet joint
supporters satisfy J11, and its correct clock t<T_wf=21313 disables fresh
Workspace.Flag1 regardless of simulation fields. It stays quiet. Farther
right both geometry votes are correct regardless of flags. Hence bad
geometry stays below C_true. As in G3 its right edge is at most b+3t:
beyond the edge plus three, both votes have three correct inputs.

**Two-tick prefix bound — proved for residues and exact Age.** Throughout
this prefix/ancestry proof, a correct pair means Address residue and exact
raw Age, allowing Address aliases. The actual adder sends each
phase-correct left input to the canonical center Address. A right whole-word
majority, if it exists with three phase-correct inputs, has the correct
residue: its three-member support intersects those three inputs. If it
does not exist, (J18) selects the correct left vote. Exact Age has the
usual three-identical-input majority. These facts extend the growth and
prefix arguments to phase-correct aliases.

Suppose x<=p has correct pairs at time t, with reference clock alpha.
One update leaves x<=p−3 correct. At the next update, x<=p−2 therefore
has five phase-correct left
inputs. A wrong output would have to be quiet and select a right
majority under (J18). Its right Address v must be 0,1,2: with five correct
left inputs any larger v has three inside mismatches in Address, or
in Age if the Address phase is correct but the selected Age is wrong.
J11 then requires three quiet joint right supporters at x+j, 1<=j<=5,
in the preceding state. Their raw Addresses are exactly v+j, by the
checked unique inverses. Every supporter has wrong geometry; a correct
pair would produce the correct output after the clock increment.

For y=x+j<=p, the earlier update had five correct left inputs, so a quiet
wrong pair there can have Address only 0,1,2. For y=p+d, 1<=d<=3, it had
correct left inputs at distances d,...,5. Since x<=p−2, j>=d+2 and
v+j>=d+2, placing at least three correct left inputs inside. Wrong
Address phase makes all three disagree in Address. Correct Address
phase with a wrong output Age means its earlier right Age differed
from alpha, so all three disagree in Age. This raises Flag1 and
contradicts quietness. No unique clock predecessor is assumed. Thus
all three alleged quiet supporters would need v+j<=2, possible for
at most two j. We have proved

    p_(t+2)>=p_t−2,
    p_t>=a−1−t              for even t,
    p_t>=a−3−t              for odd t.                    (J19)

**Quiet ancestry and sustained advance — proved.** A quiet wrong output
with Address v<Q−5 has three quiet joint right supporters. Choose the
rightmost, at displacement three to five. Unless at initial time or
raw Address >=Q−5, repeat. Its Address increases by the displacement
and the pair remains wrong. Additional Workspace/Flag1 sources may remove
a quiet node, but cannot create an exception to this requirement. A path
to initial time has displacement >=3T. One reaching a near-end word has
displacement at least D=Q−5−v and duration k>=ceil(D/5).

At even t_0, (J19) gives p>=a−1−t_0. For a prospective wrong output at
T=t_0+1 and x>=p−2 with v<=4, an initial-time ancestry would end at or
beyond a+2t_0>b. A near-end ancestry would end at least at x+D, while
its earlier right-edge bound is b+3(T−k). For v=0,...,4,

    min(D+3ceil(D/5))=600,
    x+D−[b+3(T−k)] >=595−w−4t_0 >0.                      (J20a)

Neither stop is possible. At x<=p+3, three left inputs are correct: a
wrong right pair with v>=5 raises Flag1, while v<=4 would be a forbidden
quiet wrong output. The prefix therefore advances at least three and
never retreats. Induct: increasing p by three and T by one leaves the
near-end slack unchanged and strengthens the initial-time contradiction.
Advance persists until the protected right suffix is reached, a distance
at most Q+w+t_0−1, proving (J20). Every w<=196 has positive slack;
w197 fails this sufficient estimate only, not a proved survival threshold.
All bounds are below U/32=1728 and T_wf, closing the clock premise.

**Confinement, raw normalization and flags — proved.** The worst pre-t_0
prefix bound is a−t_0−2 at the last odd time, so wrong residues/Ages
never extend left of
a−(t_0+1). Afterwards advance is monotone. Since w+t_0+1<Q, rounding
the right end to C_true−1 adds no colony beyond the at most two meeting
[a−(t_0+1),b]. Global residue/Age alignment is permanent: the left vote
is canonical; any existing right vote has the correct residue, and both
Age votes agree, whatever flags or simulation data.

Let J be the union of those at most two whole true colonies. Raw Address
also stays correct outside J. The protected suffix proves this on its
right. To its left, induct on time: all left inputs are canonical, and
an aliased output with the correct residue can occur only at true Address
0,...,127 from at least three aliased right inputs in the **same** true
colony. That colony is outside J and had no such inputs. Thus no alias
appears in a new colony. Once every residue is correct, §7's actual-adder
normalization proof applies verbatim: all left adjusted words are
canonical, while right aliases are dominated by a three-of-five right
update in each 128-site strip. It empties within43 updates. Hence raw
Address/Age is globally canonical by T(w)+43. One further update resets
both Workspace fields before their window. The unchanged aligned
source-free 216+212 clearing proof gives all flags zero by T(w)+472,
even from arbitrary initial flags or interior launches.

The43-update allowance corrects a raw-word overstatement in the initial
version of this proof. Five canonical left inputs and a common Age can
coexist with right raw Addresses385,...,389, producing quiet Address384
at true Address0. Its residue is correct. The source implication alone
therefore does not prove immediate raw normalization; the certificate
below checks this snapshot and the full raw-adder table.

[check_prefix_selection_proposal.py](proofs/check_prefix_selection_proposal.py)
and [SP3_prefix_selection_certificate.json](../figs/robustness/SP3_prefix_selection_certificate.json)
verify the actual dependency exclusion, all 384 one-step prefix cases
with free clocks/flags and two free right geometry words, both-component
inside-source implications, the two-tick child-count contradiction,
all corrected width bounds, the raw-adder/alias cases, the protected suffix
and 34,944 healthy two-fault
cases. Clock implications have both words free and use truth-checked
Boolean absorption/subsumption identities. The induction above is the
proof; experiments below provide separate finite support.

**Finite full-CA support — measured only.**
[check_sparse_prefix_islands.py](proofs/check_sparse_prefix_islands.py)

**Localized first-period recovery — proved, with extra encoding hypotheses.**
Start at physical Age zero in E_3a(z_0) and replace every raw field in I

pair. Here g=T(w)+43 includes raw normalization. After repair, copies

before the second gather. The two clean later gathers, 9791 Hold wipe,
defined scratch reads and SP3's own program give

    X_U=E_3a(F_3(z_g)).                                   (J23)

This is J17's full proof with the new repair/flag bounds substituted;
every late program/courier/commit precondition was verified above. If
z_0 itself is E_3a(y), J17's complete Age-zero one-step upper correction

F_3(z_g)=F_3(z_0); the entire physical state is clean at U and stays
clean without later noise. This allows arbitrary raw words and all

**Finite support for J23 — measured only.**
[check_sparse_prefix_period.py](proofs/check_sparse_prefix_period.py) checked
eight arbitrary whole-state bursts at physical Age zero on 147,456 sites,

**Pristine operational correction at every clock — proved.** Let
`(ξ^l)_(l>=0)` be a static infinite SP4 augmented hierarchy, with canonical
Address, Age zero, zero flags/work, and `ξ^l=E_4a(ξ^(l+1))` at every level.

are zero, the auxiliary augmentation bits initially vanish too. Write
`H_t^l=F_4^t(ξ^l)`. At every physical tick and level, the four flags are
zero, geometry is canonical with Age `age_code(t mod U)`, and every
consumed five-holder value has its five agreeing copies. This includes the
compact register source when an actual front consumes it. It does not
require overlapping register windows away from that front to agree.

Indeed J28 realizes each full period at each level. Given a healthy upper
input with zero flags, its computed Flag1/Flag2 are zero: both geometry
votes agree, the joint diagnostic has five quiet supporters, and no raw
flag/Workspace source is present. The certified early program therefore
stores zero commands. Both couriers carry zero, both signals are zero,
and the physical Workspace sources stay zero. Maintenance then leaves
physical flags zero throughout that period. The copy/front induction in
J28 gives the stated agreement invariant at every intermediate update.
Apply this simultaneously at every level over successive completed periods,
as in (6). The upper input at the start of period n is the already covered
state `F_4^n(ξ^(l+1))`; its time n is no greater than physical time nU.
For the first period, the static healthy input itself establishes its zero
computed commands. Thus this is induction on finite elapsed time, not an
assumption that an infinite downward induction has finished.

For any such orbit state H_t^l, overwrite arbitrary states at sites D,
with at most two sites in every interval of eleven sites. Then

    F_4(overwrite(H_t^l,D))=H_(t+1)^l, for every t,l.     (J35)

The density condition gives three correct inputs in each five-site
Address/Age vote. All left inconsistency and Workspace tests use an
eleven-site interval. The eight right Flag1 inputs contain at most two
faults; a faulty center with two faulty right flags would require three
faults within span8. Each joint right vote and quiet-support diagnostic
still has three exact, quiet supporters. Hence computed Flag1 is zero.
The same center-plus-left argument and zero computed Flag1 erase a
corrupt Flag2 and prevent a new one. Geometry and its pre-increment
control clock are exact, so raw-Address wipes are off.

Every ordinary copy voter reads five consecutive physical holders for
one logical bit. Its three good inputs give the correct value, including
the speed-eight Mail voters displaced from the output's neighborhood.
Thus a fault count of at most two in the whole radius12 neighborhood is
unnecessary. The compact front consumes only the appropriate five-copy
source window; its controls and selected source are exact. Voted pending
writes/forwarding, instruction keys, own-ROM lookup, operands, captures,
signals and commits consequently agree with the pristine update even
during evaluation or a stage boundary. This proves every declared
physical output, as well as the instruction keys, in (J35).

**One real set in any pristine work period, with an exact upper error
map for computed boundaries — proved conditionally.** Start from ξ^0 in that static infinite
hierarchy and allow errors only in one real c16 level1 set S and the
separated original E0 pattern. Replacement words are arbitrary. Let τ be
the first tick at which S has a same-tick triple of span at most10.
If there is no such tick, the union's per-tick eleven-site density is at
most two, so J35 makes every computed state pristine. Suppose τ exists.
Choose the closest pair `(p,τ),(q,τ)` from an earliest such triple, with
`p<q` and `q−p<=5`. Set

    n=floor(τ/U), s=τ−nU, C=Q*(floor((q+15)/Q)+1),
    B={C/Q−2,C/Q−1}, m=n+1, Z_k=F_4^k(ξ^1).

C is the same protected true boundary as J31/J33. Both true colonies
immediately before C contain the entire possible geometric damage:
the left bound p−208 is at least C−2Q, and the right bound is C−1.
The fixed pair B may include a clean colony; it is a convenient uniform
support, not a claim that both its cells become faulty. Use the already
defined convention `Y_t=F_4(X_(t−1))`, with Y_0=ξ^0, and overwrite Y_t to
obtain X_t. For the fixed decoder `D_4`, which reads voted Info at the
true layout positions, the **computed-boundary** sequence has

    D_4(Y_(kU))=Z_k for k!=m;
    D_4(Y_(mU))=Z'_m, differing from Z_m only on B;
    F_4(Z'_m)=Z_(m+1);
    X_((m+1)U)=E_4a(Z_(m+1)) outside current E0.          (J36)

Every subsequent full physical boundary is pristine outside current E0.
The first boundary at mU need not be a complete encoding. Equivalently,
the whole computed-boundary decoder sequence is exactly a pristine upper trajectory
with one arbitrary two-cell replacement **at upper input time m**:
first perform the clean update from m−1 to m, then replace B before the

### A compiler counterexample independent of the G17 ROM

**Proved (J56).** The current scheduler is not correct for every circuit it
accepts. [jobsched.py](../gacsca/jobsched.py) flattens an associative XOR
tree to a list of leaves in `Dag`. `Engine.leaf_pending` then turns that
list into a set. Repeated XOR leaves cannot be discarded this way:
`u XOR u XOR v = v`, while the set fold computes `u XOR v`.
AND and OR are idempotent; XOR is not. This is a compiler issue for the
other coding agent, independent of the rule's repair mechanism.

SP5's actual circuit contains, for example, node8371 with flattened
leaves `[3135,3135,8321]`; node3135 is the central stored Age bit16.
Another such tree repeats central Age bit0. The original compiler produces
a completed listing with31,356 instructions but fails its64-vector replay:
20 intermediate comparisons fail. More decisively, a literal Boolean
counterexample has central Address8/Age1, left-neighbor Addresses3,4,5,6,7
at offsets−5..−1 with Ages6,5,4,3,2, all right words zero, all other raw
fields zero and external instruction zero. Every Address is legal.
The desired output is Address8/Age2/Flag1=1/Flag2=0; the original scheduled
program returns Address8/**Age1**/Flag1=1/Flag2=0. Two final Age Hold bits
differ. This is an exact evaluation of the archived Boolean listing, with
no execution of an invalid native ROM lookup.

The narrow remedy is to retain the binary XOR tree when its flattened
leaf list has duplicates. The isolated
[xor_multiplicity_scheduler.py](proofs/xor_multiplicity_scheduler.py)
changes the flattening guard from `len(leaves)<3` to
`len(leaves)<3 or (op==M_XOR and len(set(leaves))!=len(leaves))` in a
fresh scheduler namespace. It does not mutate the active module. This
removes the exhibited multiplicity loss; it is not a proof of the compiler
on every possible circuit. SP5/SP6's particular rebuilt programs instead
receive independent universal output verification in J57.

The original failed receipt, driver and listing are retained as
[failure](../figs/robustness/SP5_initial_schedule_failure.json),
[archived driver](../figs/robustness/SP5_initial_schedule_failure_driver.py),
and [archived listing](../figs/robustness/SP5_initial_schedule_failure_listing.json).
[check_xor_multiplicity_scheduler.py](proofs/check_xor_multiplicity_scheduler.py)
and its [certificate](../figs/robustness/xor_multiplicity_scheduler_certificate.json)
pin both listings and the [witness](../figs/robustness/SP5_xor_scheduler_witness.npz).
No claim is made that the independently certified G17 ROM has this fault.
Changing the active compiler or rebuilding a registered candidate is left
to a separately flagged coding change.

valid=WF2=1, shared counter c and no other live holders. At most two
arbitrary whole packet-component words per eleven-site row are overwritten.

counter c+1. If c>=1791, all computed outputs are zero. Consequently a
packet born at counter0 lasts for exactly1792 state rows, counting its
birth row, then disappears. Raw exceptions are only current overwrites.

since there are only two faulty words. Thus it equals the true pair.

range calculation forbid a retained tag. The counter condition and its
increment give the asserted output. Iteration establishes the lifetime. ∎

increments it, giving counter at least t+1. All live outputs have counter

stays zero. The finite-support assertion follows from J77b's identical

are at1..5, with tag x−1 and count0. All other initially eligible packet
and coded-flag carriers, anywhere on Z, have count at least1 or are
inactive. There are no subsequent births. GF/Age/NF1/NF2 and all other

are unrestricted. Then:

The source, relative-counter, birth and right-boundary hypotheses are

the selected count increments without overflow. Hence all cohorts of
count exactly t descend from the five fresh count0 packet words; all

J96 is sufficient for its particular trace, but requires holes to

It uses global E0 separation rather than only a per-row fault count.

holes occur singly or in adjacent pairs, with at least five forced

**computed coded force** to be1 on C outside H. At sites in H it may

whole-cell singleton/adjacent-pair errors mutually(24,24)-separated,
at every row including the right exterior. All initial colony GF/Age,
ordinary flags, other fields and components are free **subject to
this subsequent force-history premise**.

Then every computed GF/Age on C is correct by

    T + 1 + 448 + |H| <= T + 577,

and remains correct while the hypotheses hold. No initial source,
stored Flag2 ones or condition on when holes appear is required by
this maintenance implication. It does not assert that arbitrary
components actually produce its required force history.

Proof. An update sets computed Flag2=1 at every forced site. After
one initialization update this supplies four guaranteed left Flag2
ones at offsets−5,...,−2 for every possible hole. At any hole x whose
five right GF/Age pairs are correct, consider two local facts.

First, if its previous computed Flag2 is1, it remains1 and chooses
correct RF GF/Age in every E0 row. If self is uncorrupted, at least
two of the four left support ones remain. Because the right-selected
canonical address x≥5 puts these supports inside the frame, neither
Flag2 erasure condition holds. If self is overwritten, its only
possible companion in this eleven-site window is an adjacent site
at offset−1 or+1. None of the four guaranteed supports is corrupted,
so the four ones turn Flag2 on regardless of self's raw value. Three
right GF/Age pairs survive in all cases. Notice that an arbitrary
two-site nonadjacent fault pattern would not justify this self-fault
case; E0's actual group shape is used.

Second, with arbitrary previous self Flag2, if none of these four
supports is overwritten, all four inside ones make both its on and
keep branches1. Thus it immediately obtains Flag2=1 and correct
GF/Age. A failed acquisition must therefore involve an error at
one of x−5,...,x−2. All eleven required inputs x−5,...,x+5 on the
**next** row are then error-free: every such site has spatial distance
at most10 and temporal distance1 from that blocking E0 group, both
less than24. Its guaranteed left supports consequently succeed in
the next update. The companion is on the same row as the blocker,
so it cannot itself be an error on the next row.

Induct on a correct right suffix, maintaining computed Flag2=1 at
its already crossed holes. Forced sites in the suffix always select
the correct right mode. Crossed holes stay correct with Flag2=1 by
the first local fact, so the suffix and its reference clock advance
through every intervening row. Its next predecessor, if forced, is
acquired in one update. If it is a hole, the second fact acquires it
in at most two updates, with computed Flag2=1. There are448 holders
and at most one extra update for each hole, after the initialization
update. This proves the stated bound and subsequent persistence. ∎

For the maximum envelope size, read addresses from left to right.
Record the last five hole bits. A new hole is allowed precisely when
bits at distances2,...,5 are zero; addresses0,...,4 are forbidden.
The recurrence retaining the maximum hole count for each five-bit
suffix enumerates every admissible envelope. It gives max|H|=128,
attained by pairs5,6;12,13;...;446,447. Hence the numerical bound577.

For each of the next1792 computed updates, GF has exactly the displayed

**Proof. Packet votes have a smaller relevant support than their
displayed radius-five input window.** For an eligible packet at a
reader x∈[1,5], let τ∈[0,4] be its output tag and r=x−τ−1 its integer
origin. Thus r∈[−4,4]. An eligible input at x+j has raw tag k∈[0,4].
For it to vote for that output cohort, it must satisfy

    (k−j) mod16 = τ,     −5≤j≤5.

Since k−j−τ lies in[−9,9], the equality implies k−j=τ without wrap.
Consequently x+j=r+k+1 lies in the actual five-position frame
[r+1,r+5], hence in **[−3,9]**. Count equality can remove votes but
cannot add an outside vote. This holds for every candidate cohort,
every counter and every winner of the minimum-counter selector, not
only for the proper origin0 source. The exact arithmetic certificate
checks all4400 raw-tag cases and125 eligible matches. Conversely,
an eligible packet directly forced at y≤−4 has origin y−k−1≤−5.
The no-wrap witness lemma preserves its origin on nonbirth retention;
such a word cannot enter a frame with origin[−4,4]. Ineligible raw
tags≥5 cannot vote. This is why arbitrary far-left forcing is harmless
to the relevant packet induction; treating the whole displayed input
window as sparse would unnecessarily exclude the theorem's adversary.

checks suffice here. Additional dense forcing has no site in that

by24 from every other error, whereas these three sites are all
within four spatial units at the same tick. Thus all three sites
belong to real level1 errors. They belong to the same such error
because distinct real level1 errors are24Q spatially separated at
the same tick. If two sample blocks had at least three errors, their
points would still belong to the same real1 set S: the four blocks
have spatial diameter64, and64<24Q. Choose two points from each
of the two blocks. Each pair consists of two disjoint candidate
level0 singletons in E\E0, linked at distance<24 and contained
in a Q×U box, so each is a candidate level1 subset of S. The
nearest points of any distinct sample blocks are at least16 apart:
their centers are20 apart or more and their radii are2. The two
candidate subsets are therefore(c,c)-separated at c16. This
contradicts condition(iii) for S to be a real level1 error. The
150 block-point checks verify that finite spacing arithmetic, but
the argument covers arbitrary finite or infinite global error sets
satisfying the stated decomposition. ∎

calculation applies, so the factorization covers all2097152 raw

## 13. Evidence and how to read the existing claims

This audit ran the short reproductions in §§5–6 and the universal symbolic
certificate in §6, and checked the pinned parameters.
The conditional flag proofs in §10 additionally have exhaustive local
certificates, together with a C/CUDA reproduction of the command-launch
counterexample. The clock certificate in §7 checks all 65,536 raw Age
words. These are separately scoped certificates, not a reliability proof.
It also ran a focused noiseless GPU consistency check: two periods on
147,456 physical sites, from a structurally healthy upper ring with arbitrary
other fields, matched the **entire** fresh canonical encoding at both
boundaries. This is explicitly finite experimental support for (5), not
the universal proof. Its driver, saved input, kernel identity and receipt are
[check_noiseless.py](../figs/robustness/check_noiseless.py),
[noiseless_upper.npz](../figs/robustness/noiseless_upper.npz) and
[noiseless_canonical.json](../figs/robustness/noiseless_canonical.json).

A new bounded adversarial structural probe used 512 one-tick, sixteen-site
errors, each certified as one real level-1 error at c=16. It crossed eight
Address shifts, four Age offsets and all sixteen constant combinations of
the four flag bits; copied words had legal Address/Age values. It ran a
32-colony finite slice from Age 2000 for 4096 ticks, before flag couriers,
with no surrounding E0 noise. Every sixteen ticks it compared Address,
Age and the four flags to its clean twin. The last sampled Address/Age
difference was at offset 128, Flag1 at 320 and Flag2 at 192. At the final
tick all six structural fields matched in all 512 cases. The largest
sampled wrong-Address count was 29; Flag1's was 523.

**This is not an all-field recovery result:** 272 cases still differed in
simulation fields at the final tick, with up to 803 sites differing. Nor do
sixteen-tick samples establish a per-tick recovery deadline. These finite
results do not cover arbitrary seeds, continuous sixteen-tick forcing,
surrounding E0 noise, or an intact infinite upper configuration. The driver,
case-by-case receipt, counts and hashes are
[probe_flag_seeds.py](../figs/robustness/probe_flag_seeds.py),
[flag_seeds.json](../figs/robustness/flag_seeds.json),
[flag_seeds_addr.npz](../figs/robustness/flag_seeds_addr.npz) and
[flag_seeds_summary.json](../figs/robustness/flag_seeds_summary.json).
The summary also records the first attempt's exit 137 during large snapshot
unpacking; its incomplete run supplies no evidence. The successful run
streams small chunks.

A subsequent sustained-burst probe evaluates the mathematical completion
of §6, including unused words. Its execution object zero-pads ROM rows
384,...,511 **in memory only**; no candidate, generator, or stored ROM was
changed. The actual invalid-arrival example of §6 agrees on every output
bit between this completed C, NumPy and CUDA evaluation. This does not
fix or test the original unguarded native lookup on that example.

Each burst overwrites sixteen sites for sixteen ticks, a literal real
level-1 set at c=16. At Age 2000, 2,048 cases cross four Address patterns
(384, 500, 511, and a coherent canonical shift by 32), four Age words
(the current legal word, 37152, 17868, 65535), sixteen flag combinations,
two constant patterns for all other fields, and start Addresses
0,64,128,320. Every update is tracked. Without surrounding noise, the last
Address/Age difference is at offset 250, and all 2,048 cases still have
some **non-geometric** state difference at offset 1024. The eight
longest-lived cases reproduce their geometry lifetimes on the full
147,456-site ring. Whole-state equality with the smaller ring is checked
only on its central [5120,7168) interval, protected for 1024 updates by
the radius-five causal buffer. The first attempted comparison included
unprotected edges and failed; it supplied no whole-slice equality claim.

Four further runs use the same 2,048 seeds, followed from offset 40 by
26-by-26 spaced adjacent-pair overwrites with random, all-one, inverted,
or next-colony-copy values. Their groups are mutually at least (25,26)
separated and are more than 24 ticks after the last burst point, so they
are actual E0 errors relative to S. The pair threshold is explicitly
65536, since the native API's nominal probability one gives 65535/65536.
Current direct faults are excluded from the per-update comparison. The
last **indirect geometric** differences occur at offsets 250,247,247,250
respectively; no indirect geometry difference occurs at either 648-tick
deadline in these runs. E0 starts only after the initial burst, and these
four lattices are a small subset of the allowed adversarial patterns.

An additional 1,536 cases at Age 13537, the flag-window start, place the
same sixteen-by-sixteen bursts at Addresses 368,376,380, including
boundary-crossing seeds. Without E0, their last geometric difference is
at offset 254. **All these statements are finite measurements, not P6,
P7 or an all-time threshold.** They do not cover every raw-word pattern,
every stage, every real level-1 shape, or mixed E0 during initial forcing.

the status “proved” for an unbounded quantified repair statement.

The five existing `GrayErrorClassTest` tests passed; their log is
[classifier_tests.log](../figs/robustness/classifier_tests.log). Document links,
the displayed probability arithmetic and exponent identities, and unchanged
rule-source hashes were checked in
[validation.json](../figs/robustness/validation.json). These checks support
reproducibility; the proofs in §§3–4 do not rest on sampled tests.
The reproducible provenance/arithmetic validator is
[validate_audit.py](proofs/validate_audit.py). It checks receipt and source
hashes; it does not promote a measured repair statement to a theorem.

The updated [LEDGER.md](LEDGER.md) keeps the original IDs and the four
repository status labels. Its “assumed” includes a required but unproved
claim with no universal verification; “measured only” and “argued and measured”
are also unproved for purposes of the theorem. Source locations for this
audit are Gray §§5.1–5.5, pp. 16–43, in
[gray_readers_guide.txt](../papers_txt/gray_readers_guide.txt), and Gács
Definitions 3.1, 10.3, Condition 10.4, Lemmas 10.5 and 11.7, and §11's
parameter conditions in [gacs_2001.txt](../papers_txt/gacs_2001.txt).
